f718cf96c748fda0.title: India eyes wind turbine revamp to boost output, bypass land woes
f718cf96c748fda0.summary: India is weighing replacing aging wind turbines with larger, more efficient machines to boost generation at older farms without having to acquire more land. As much as 8 gigawatts of capacity using old and smaller turbines can be upgraded with modern units, according to a preliminary assessment by the Indian Wind Turbine Manufacturers Association, Chief Executive Officer Aditya Pyasi said in an interview. The lobby group is in talks with federal and state governments to finalize a plan that could help increase capacity at those sites by almost 50%. Wind power has become increasingly important for India to meet peak electricity demand after sunset. Although the country’s green power capacity has quadrupled since 2014, wind installations have lagged far behind solar, with land acquisition and securing right-of-way remaining major hurdles to faster deployment. That — coupled with limited battery storage — has left the grid struggling to absorb excess daytime generation, forcing solar curtailments while creating shortfalls at night. Installations reached a record 6.3 gigawatts in 2025. Still, wind project deployment remains below the pace needed to meet India’s 2030 goal of 500 gigawatts clean power capacity. Replacing older turbines of as much as 2 megawatts with modern 3- to 5-megawatt units at existing sites could help sidestep land-access hurdles. IWTMA is working with windy states such as Gujarat, Maharashtra and Karnataka to firm up an implementation plan, Pyasi said. “While the longer-term potential is around 25 gigawatts, our assessment shows that we can begin repowering 5 to 8 gigawatts immediately.” Globally, 178 gigawatts of wind power projects built before 2010 will be available for retrofitting by 2030, according to the International Renewable Energy Agency, which sees repowering as an important tool to meet the target of tripling global renewable energy capacity by the end of this decade. “Repowering onshore wind is not a technical footnote. 63eac8bb310fb096.title: Kerala High Court orders government to ready adequate medicines, vehicles at mental health centres by November 24
63eac8bb310fb096.summary: Published - November 12, 2026 02:16 am IST - KOCHI Government Mental Health Centre, Thrissur. | Photo Credit: FILE PHOTO Stating that assurances alone are not sufficient, and they have to translate into action, the Kerala High Court has directed the government to make available adequate medicines and vehicles in mental health centres by November 24. A Division Bench of Justice Devan Ramachandran and Justice Basant Balaji, who had earlier this year visited the centres in Thiruvananthapuram, Thrissur, and Kozhikode acceded to the Advocate General’s request to file an action taken report by the same day on the construction of compound walls and the appointment of necessary personnel at the centres. This was after the Advocate General submitted that the construction of compound walls around the centres was progressing at a good speed. On the appointment of personnel, he sought another two weeks’ time, saying that there had been a change of incumbent in the post of Secretary, Health and Family Welfare department, and that he was in the process of evaluating the files concerned. The matter has been listed for hearing on November 24. The High Court had in September expressed satisfaction at the government’s decision to rename mental health centres as “happiness and wellness centres”, observing that the (hitherto) stigmatisation of patients, their caregivers, and the centres as a whole was something one could not be oblivious to. The Advocate General had informed the court then that the government was looking into infrastructure and staff vacancy issues at the centres with ‘full sincerity’. ebe6000906e09914.title: India-UK FTA faces first hurdle as 40 containers of Pernod Ricard, Diageo Scotch stuck at ports amid tariff dispute
ebe6000906e09914.summary: India's trade pact with the UK faces its first major dispute as customs officials seek a 150% tariff on bulk Scotch imports by Pernod Ricard and Diageo, despite assurances of a reduced 75% duty. Dozens of containers remain held at ports, raising concerns over supplies and market access.
ebe6000906e09914.headline_en: India-UK FTA faces first hurdle as 40 containers of Pernod Ricard, Diageo Scotch stuck at ports amid tariff dispute
ebe6000906e09914.raw_facts: India's trade pact with the UK faces its first major dispute as customs officials seek a 150% tariff on bulk Scotch imports by Pernod Ricard and Diageo, despite assurances of a reduced 75% duty. Dozens of containers remain held at ports, raising concerns over supplies and market access.
flags: Exaggerated scale: '40 containers' is a trivially small volume for a major FTA dispute involving global giants like Pernod Ricard and Diageo; such a minor logistical hiccup would not be characterized as the 'first major hurdle' or 'first major dispute' in a headline.

Unsubstantiated specific claim: The specific detail of a '150% tariff' being sought versus a '75% duty' assurance is highly specific and lacks corroboration from major international news sources or official trade announcements as of the current date.

Mischaracterization of FTA status: The India-UK FTA is still under negotiation and has not yet been ratified or implemented. Therefore, it cannot face a 'dispute' under the treaty's dispute settlement mechanism, nor can it have 'assurances' of reduced duties that are being violated in a legal sense. Customs disputes during the negotiation phase are common but not 'FTA disputes'.

Source reliability: Livemint is a reputable Indian financial news source, but the specific framing of a minor port hold-up as a 'major FTA dispute' suggests potential sensationalism or confusion between a routine customs query and a treaty-level conflict.

c6eae5ba3ca34ffc.title: Offering food, best dharma
c6eae5ba3ca34ffc.summary: Published - November 12, 2026 05:22 am IST Offering food to others is the best dharma, said R. Narayanan in a discourse. There is nothing to equal this, says Tiruvalluvar. In his Tirumanthiram, Tirumoolar says we should offer a vilva leaf to Lord Siva, grass to a cow, and food to fellow human beings. More importantly, we must always use sweet words. Tiruvalluvar says that even nectar, which confers immortality, must be shared with others. Ilayankudi Maranar was one of the 63 Nayanmars praised by Sekkizhar in his Periya Puranam. Maranar was wealthy. He honoured devotees of Siva by washing their feet with scented water. He then offered them a lavish meal, which did not lack any flavour. The Lord wanted to show the world how generous Ilayankudi Maranar could be even in poverty. He made sure that Maranar lost his wealth. Eventually, he was left with nothing but a tiled house and a small plot of land. One night, after Maranar had sown seeds in his field, it rained heavily. That night, Siva, in the guise of a Saivite devotee, arrived at Maranar’s doorstep. Maranar’s wife asked her husband to fetch the grains that had been sown that morning. She cleaned the grains, and used it to cook rice for the visitor. Usually, the grains used for sowing were never used for cooking, because they ensured that a farmer would be able to grow his next crop. So, something that would take care of a farmer’s future would never be used for food. But Maranar and his wife broke that rule, when they cooked for the mendicant. Greens grown in the backyard were also used to prepare tasty dishes. Since there was no firewood, Maranar’s wife used a wooden beam from their house as firewood. When the couple was about to serve food, the sleeping guest woke and revealed Himself as Lord Siva. He blessed them and said they would reach Sivaloka. 74b09dff258a7741.title: Cochin shipyard, SFO Technologies jointly develop sophisticated laser arc welding technology
74b09dff258a7741.summary: Published - November 12, 2026 02:03 am IST - KOCHI Cochin Shipyard Limited (CSL) and the Kochi-based SFO Technologies Private Limited have unveiled what is claimed to be the country’s first indigenously designed and manufactured hybrid laser arc welding (HLAW) technology. The announcement was made at the inauguration of the Advanced Laser Engineering Centre and HLAW R&D facility at NeST Hitek Park, Kalamassery. The facility was inaugurated by Jose V.J., chairman and managing director, CSL, and N. Jehangir, chairman and managing director, SFO Technologies. Jointly developed by CSL and SFO Technologies, the HLAW system integrates laser welding, conventional arc welding, robotics, and advanced automation, powered by a high-power fibre laser source indigenously developed by SFO Technologies, claimed a communication. The technology is expected to deliver faster welding speeds, deeper penetration, lower distortion, and improved weld consistency across shipbuilding, defence, heavy engineering, railways, energy, and other strategic manufacturing sectors like large tanks and wagons for improving productivity, claimed the developers in a statement. 76c57694aa964ae3.title: Air India flight to Mumbai moved to isolation bay after hijack threat at Kolkata airport: What we know
76c57694aa964ae3.summary: A hijack threat note was found in the washroom of a Mumbai-bound Air India flight shortly before its scheduled departure from Kolkata airport on Wednesday, PTI reported. The airport authorities moved the aircraft to an isolation bay at the airport. The flight was scheduled to take off at 10.20 am. The note, which warned that the aircraft would be hijacked at 11.10 am, was found in the aircraft's washroom just before departure, Kolkata airport director Vikram Singh told PTI . All passengers who had boarded the aircraft were deboarded and the plane was moved to an isolation bay for security checks, Singh added. Security protocols were immediately activated, with officials conducting a thorough inspection of the aircraft as a precautionary measure, he added. be3ca298a0b0f246.title: Govt raises price cap for officers' electronic devices to ₹1.8 lakh
be3ca298a0b0f246.summary: The central government has raised the price ceiling of laptops, tablets, or similar devices for its eligible officers to Rs 1.8 lakh plus taxes, and officials can retain them for personal use after four years. The Finance Ministry's Expenditure Department on November 10 issued revised guidelines on the purchase of Note Book /Laptop by ministries/departments of the central government. Central government employees of Sections Officer rank and above will be eligible for the devices. "...it has been decided that laptop; tablet; notepad; ultra-book; notebook; devices of similar categories may be issued to eligible officers for discharge of official work," it said. The new guidelines replace the July 2023 instructions on similar purchases of gadgets. The 2023 guidelines explicitly mentioned the purchase of mobile devices, which is not mentioned in the November 10, 2026, office memorandum. af1c35f25bd603ad.title: MP alleges intelligence failure over Nanjangud drug racket
af1c35f25bd603ad.summary: Updated - November 12, 2026 12:49 am IST - MYSURU Yaduveer Krishnadatta Chamaraja Wadiyar, Mysuru MP Mysuru-Kodagu MP Yaduveer Krishnadatta Chamaraja Wadiyar has accused the Congress government of a serious intelligence failure following the alleged busting of an inter-State drug racket operating under the guise of a banana plantation in Nanjangud by the Keralam Police. In a statement here, Mr. Yaduveer said it was shocking that the racket operating on Karnataka soil was detected by the police of a neighbouring State rather than the Karnataka Police or the State intelligence wing. He said this was not an isolated incident, pointing out that Maharashtra Police and central investigating agencies had intervened in recent years to expose organised drug networks operating in Mysuru. “Such incidents raised serious questions about the effectiveness of the State’s intelligence machinery,” he added. Questioning the government’s repeated claims of intensifying its crackdown on narcotics and strengthening police surveillance, he asked how an illegal operation allegedly conducted under the cover of agricultural activity could go unnoticed by the local police. He alleged that the repeated involvement of police forces from other States and central agencies in detecting alleged criminal networks operating in Karnataka reflected serious lapses in law enforcement and intelligence gathering. The Congress government should take moral responsibility for the failure, he demanded. Mr. Yaduveer also sought to know why the State intelligence wing had failed to detect the racket, what surveillance mechanisms were in place to identify organised drug networks and who would be held accountable for the alleged lapses. Calling for a comprehensive investigation, he urged the government to uncover the entire network behind the racket, fix accountability for the alleged intelligence lapses, strengthen inter-State police coordination and take stringent action against all those involved. Published -

a45eb564a9e1ba47.title: Hijack threat note found on Air India flight, plane taken to isolation bay
a45eb564a9e1ba47.summary: A hijack threat note found in the washroom of a Mumbai-bound Air India flight before take-off on Wednesday morning prompted security officials to park the aircraft in an isolation bay of the airport here, an official said. The flight was scheduled to depart at 10.20 am. The note threatening that the plane would be hijacked at 11.10 am was found in the washroom just before the departure of the flight, Kolkata airport director Vikram Singh said. All the passengers who had boarded the aircraft were deboarded, and it was taken to the isolation bay, he said. Security protocols were immediately activated, and the aircraft was moved to an isolation bay for a thorough inspection and necessary precautionary measures, he said.

More than 19.13 lakh pilgrims visited Kedarnath, and over 8.84 lakh visited Yamunotri during this year's pilgrimage season. All rituals were performed in accordance with traditional customs before the temple portals were closed at the auspicious time of 8.30 am. 6f68af2d20b39185.title: CPI(M) leader P. Rajeeve flays police action against protesters in Keralam’s Thiruvananthapuram
6f68af2d20b39185.summary: Published - November 13, 2026 12:30 am IST - KOCHI Communist Party of India (Marxist) [CPI(M)] central committee member P. Rajeeve has termed Wednesday night’s police action against protesters in Thiruvananthapuram and the removal to hospital of Valarmathi S., secretary of the action council and convener of the lower primary school teacher (LPST) rank holders’ protest committee, who was on a hunger strike, as anti-democratic. The government must specify which court order within six months of the United Democratic Front (UDF) assuming power that it relied on for such actions. Moreover, it owes an explanation on why it “went back” on an earlier assurance to extend the time frame for Public Service Commission rank lists. Agitations are being “suppressed”, while social media accounts are being closed down, he told the media here on Thursday. Likewise, the government that is finding fault with the Kerala Infrastructure Investment Fund Board (KIIFB) is taking credit for projects that were taken up under it. In another move, the government is preparing to inaugurate the construction work of the KIIFB-funded digital park, whose foundation stone was laid by Prime Minister Narendra Modi when the Left Democratic Front was in power in the State, Mr. Rajeeve said. 603400d77cfff554.title: India’s TB deaths fall 38% since 2015, outpacing global decline: WHO report
603400d77cfff554.summary: New Delhi: India has recorded a 38% reduction in tuberculosis (TB) mortality since 2015, outperforming the global decline of 35%, the Union health ministry said on Thursday. Highlighted in the World Health Organization’s (WHO) Global Tuberculosis Report 2026 released on Thursday, the findings also showed that the country achieved a 94% treatment success rate among drug-susceptible TB patients. According to the WHO report, India’s estimated TB mortality rate dropped from 280 per million people in 2015 to 180 per million in 2025. Meanwhile, a nationally representative TB prevalence survey conducted in 2025 by the Indian Council of Medical Research—National Institute for Research in Tuberculosis (ICMR-NIRT) has been shared with the WHO. The findings are currently under technical review, after which the WHO will publish an updated country profile for India. The health ministry added that 96% of India’s TB programme funding requirements are now met through domestic resources. The ministry also highlighted how the TB Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan has transformed detection through technological innovation. Between December 2024 and November 2026, more than 250 million people were brought under TB screening. Authorities conducted over 11 crore chest X-rays—using portable, AI-enabled diagnostic tools—alongside more than 30 million rapid molecular nucleic acid amplification tests (NAAT). This identified 4.86 million new TB cases, including 1.49 million asymptomatic patients. The first intensified 100-day campaign under the TB Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan was launched on 7 December 2024, across 347 high-priority districts in 33 states and Union territories before being expanded nationwide. A second intensified 100-day campaign was launched on 24 March 2026, focusing on screening in 158,000 high-risk villages and wards, congregate settings, and vulnerable populations. a6a8b1604feeb9bd.title: How to invest abroad through GIFT City: A step-by-step guide
a6a8b1604feeb9bd.summary: Resident Indians looking to invest abroad can do so through dollar-denominated funds based in GIFT City, the international financial centre in Gujarat. This offers an alternative to investing directly in foreign stocks through overseas brokers, a route examined in an earlier Business Standard article . Here is how to invest through GIFT City, from choosing a fund to transferring money. The route has drawn interest because many international mutual funds from domestic fund houses have stopped taking fresh money. The mutual fund industry as a whole has reached the $7 billion overseas investment limit set by the regulators, and funds based in GIFT City are not subject to that limit. One attraction is regulatory oversight. GIFT City funds come under the International Financial Services Centres Authority (IFSCA), an Indian regulator. Investors using overseas brokers may have limited recourse through Indian regulators if something goes wrong, says Deepesh Raghaw, a Securities and Exchange Board of India (Sebi)-registered investment advisor and founder of PersonalFinancePlan.in. Those seeking to avoid cross-border disputes may prefer Indian funds or the GIFT City route, he says. Another reason is to hold assets in dollars. The rupee has tended to weaken against the dollar over time, so dollar assets can cushion that fall. Hema Thakkar, head of business development (alternatives) at PPFAS, says investors use these funds to build a dollar corpus for goals like a child’s education abroad, where the bills will be in dollars. A Balasubramanian, managing director and chief executive of Aditya Birla Sun Life Asset Management Company (AMC), also cites overseas education and travel. The market, however, is still developing. GIFT City was established primarily to attract foreign and non-resident Indian (NRI) investment into India, Raghaw says, and outbound retail funds remain a small segment. 6a94123090634351.title: As Chennai Corporation intensifies planting of saplings, waterlogging emerges a deterrent to green cover expansion
6a94123090634351.summary: Published - November 13, 2026 12:52 am IST - CHENNAI Chennai Corporation has started planting two lakh saplings this Northeast monsoon as it seeks to increase green cover in the city from 18% to 33% in a few years. However, waterlogging in several vacant lands, coupled with predominantly clayey soil conditions, remains a challenge to increasing the green cover. Chennai Corporation Commissioner G.S.Sameeran said: “Based on the intensity of rainfall, planting of an estimated 1.5-2 lakh saplings can be achieved by December 2026, in addition to planting 1.36 lakh saplings from June 2026. Our overall target is 12 lakh for this year. It is proposed to prioritise the planting of native tree species such as Mahilam, Poovarasu, Pungam, Punnai, Neer Marudhu, Neem, Jamun and other tropical avenue trees like Peltophorum, Tabebuia, Spathodea and Cassia that are ecologically suitable and well-adapted to the local soil and climatic conditions.” Pointing to site constraints, Dr. Sameeran said waterlogging in several vacant lands, coupled with predominantly clayey soil conditions, posed challenges to tree planting activities and affected the suitability of certain sites for tree planting. As per the Chennai City Biodiversity Index (2025) and the recent assessment by Anna University (2026), Chennai’s existing green cover is estimated to be in the range of 15–18%. Chennai Corporation officials said the civic body proposed to progressively increase Chennai’s green cover towards the 33% benchmark through a comprehensive and integrated approach, comprising large-scale tree plantation across suitable locations, development of urban forests, avenue and roadside plantations, restoration of degraded parks and green spaces. GCC intends to promote partnerships with educational institutions, industries and other organisations. c48eaaec43dc5cd8.title: No government school will be closed due to low enrolment: Minister Rajmohan
c48eaaec43dc5cd8.summary: Published - November 13, 2026 01:13 am IST - VELLORE Minister for School Education, Tamil Development, Information and Publicity, Rajmohan, addresses the Achievers Appreciation Day at VIT Vellore on Thursday. G.Viswanathan, founder & chancellor, VIT, is also seen. | Photo Credit: C. VENKATACHALAPATHY Minister for School Education Rajmohan on Thursday said that the State government will not shut down even a single government school on the basis of low enrollment of students. In his inaugural address at the felicitation ceremony, organised by VIT Vellore, for headmasters of government and government-aided schools in Vellore, Ranipet, Tirupattur and Tiruvannamalai districts that secured 100 per cent pass results in Board examinations for 2023-24, 2024-25 and 2025-26, Mr. Rajmohan said that since the new government formed six months ago, no government school has been closed, citing low enrollment. “New teaching methods such as teaching mathematics through stories and improvements in curriculum have been introduced to boost enrolment in government schools,” he said. G. Viswanathan, founder and chancellor, VIT, highlighted the need to set up a committee to study the impact of the Right to Education Act’s policy of ensuring pass results on overall educational quality and to examine whether the policy need to be reviewed. It comes in the backdrop of closure of around 94,000 government schools as against 51,000 private schools that were opened in the country in the past decade. “In Tamil Nadu, 246 government schools had been shut during the same period. At present, around 1,200 schools have zero enrolment,” he said. Sankar Viswanathan and Sekar Viswanathan, vice presidents, VIT, and Premalatha, District Educational Officer (Vellore), were among others present on the occasion. 9600c1ce84962ac5.title: Trump endorses former Apple CEO Tim Cook to replace Jensen Huang as Nvidia CEO: ‘A legend replaces a legend’
9600c1ce84962ac5.summary: Hours after Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang tendered his resignation from the chief executive officer (CEO) position amid the spy affair scandal, US President Donald Trump said, "A legend should replace a legend," and endorsed former Apple Inc. chief executive Tim Cook's name. "NOW THAT Nvidia CEO JENSEN HUANG, who has done a fantastic job, has resigned, there is only one man to take his place – TIM COOK of Apple. A Legend replaces a Legend! (sic)," Trump said. While President Trump's public endorsement of Tim Cook drew widespread attention, neither Nvidia nor Apple has issued an official statement regarding Cook's potential cross-company migration Cook stepped down after a 15-year stint as Apple's CEO in September and is now executive chairman at the iPhone-maker. The tech giant has appointed the company's Chief Financial Officer, Colette Kress, as the interim CEO and said the "board has initiated a search for a permanent CEO." Nvidia has also restructured its governance, appointing Harvey C Jones as the company's first-ever Chair of the Board. Seeking to reassure investors ahead of its third-quarter fiscal 2027 results, scheduled for November 17, Jones said, “The Board has full confidence in Colette and the leadership team, and we expect the company’s operations, customer commitments and product roadmap to continue without interruption.” Interim CEO Colette Kress also expressed confidence in the company's direction, stating, "We will continue advancing the work that has made NVIDIA a leader in accelerated computing and AI, and execute on the opportunities ahead." Huang, who co-founded the tech giant, has been embroiled in the controversy ever since reports claimed he had an extramarital affair with a Chinese businesswoman whom US authorities suspect of spying for Beijing. 4df5d58432614d75.title: Dhinakaran urges quality checks on Children’s Day cakes
4df5d58432614d75.summary: Published - November 13, 2026 01:11 am IST - CHENNAI Amma Makkal Munnetra Kazhagam (AMMK) general secretary T.T.V. Dhinakaran. | Photo Credit: ASHOK R AMMK founder T.T.V. Dhinakaran on Thursday urged the Tamil Nadu government to ensure that cakes procured for distribution to students of government and government-aided schools on Children’s Day were subjected to proper quality checks before being distributed. Mr. Dhinakaran alleged that cakes purchased from various companies had been lying unattended in vehicles for the past four days without proper storage or preservation, raising concerns over their safety. Pointing out that the cakes had reportedly been transported over long distances, Mr. Dhinakaran in a social media post said it was essential to verify their manufacturing and expiry dates, storage conditions and quality. He said reports of improper storage had caused concern among parents, particularly in view of earlier complaints about the quality of food served under the school breakfast and mid-day meal schemes. Mr. Dhinakaran urged the School Education Department to ensure that only safe and quality cakes reached children. flags: Logical Consistency: The headline contains a plausible economic narrative. Fading peace hopes in the Middle East typically increase geopolitical risk, which is a safe-haven driver for gold (usually causing prices to rise). However, the headline states gold *drops* due to fading peace hopes fanning *inflation fears*. This implies a specific market dynamic where inflation fears lead to expectations of higher interest rates or a stronger US Dollar, which outweighs the safe-haven demand. While counter-intuitive to simple safe-haven logic, this is a standard and plausible macroeconomic scenario (e.g., 'bad news is good news' for the dollar if it implies hawkish central bank response).

aba73b5290c1fc47.title: Five e-scooters catch fire in Ranipet
aba73b5290c1fc47.summary: Published - November 13, 2026 01:02 am IST - RANIPET Police said that an electrical short circuit could have been the reason for the incident. | Photo Credit: SPECIAL ARRANGEMENT Five electric scooters caught fire at the showroom at Kaveripakkam village near Walajah town in Ranipet on Thursday. Police said that Y. Suresh, 49, a resident of Walajah town, was running an e-scooter showroom on Bazaar Street in Kaveripakkam village near Walajah town. Initial inquiry revealed that, Suresh reportedly plugged in the vehicles to charge the batteries, but apparently forgot to disconnect the power supply before closing the showroom on Wednesday. On Thursday, a few residents alerted Suresh about smoke in the showroom. Police said that when he opened the showroom, Suresh saw that five e-scooters were gutted and 10 other vehicles were damaged in the fire. Based on the alert, firefighters doused the blaze in the outlet. Police said that an electrical short circuit could have been the reason for the incident. They also said that charging the vehicle for too long could have caused the fire, as damaged vehicles were plugged in for charging. A case was registered and further probe is underway. The police said this was not the first time that electric scooters had caught fire. In February 2023, an electric scooter parked on the veranda of a house in Vaniyambadi near Tirupattur caught fire. The vehicle was left to charge the previous night before the owner of the vehicle S. Ihsanuallh, went to sleep. The fire gutted his bike and the meter box. e6f9d26de74449d2.summary: Published - November 13, 2026 01:01 am IST - VELLORE District Collector P.S.Leela Alex releasing the Special draft electoral rolls in the presence of all political parties in Vellore on Thursday. | Photo Credit: C. Venkatachalapathy The draft electoral rolls for Special Intensive Revision (SIR) 2027 were released on Thursday for Vellore, Ranipet, Tirupattur and Tiruvannamalai districts, with women voters higher than men voters. District Election Officer (DEO) P.S. Leela Alex released the draft electoral rolls at the Collectorate in Vellore in the presence of representatives of recognised political parties and district officials. As per the rolls, the draft tally of voters in Vellore district, which comprises five Assembly constituencies, is 11,59,481 voters (5,61,407 men; 5,97,901 women; and 173 others). Among Assembly seats, Gudiyatham has the highest number of voters, with a total of 2,53,706 voters (1,23,258 men; 1,30,414 women; 34 others), followed by Vellore Anaicut (2,41,141 total voters) and Katpadi 2,30,996 total voters. In Tiruvannamalai, the draft electoral rolls, which were released by DEO Vandhana Garg, have a total of 19,47,156 voters: 9,56,160 men; 9,90,840 women; and 156 others. Among eight constituencies, Chengam has highest number of 2,70,914 voters (1,34,543 men; 1,36,359 women and 12 others), followed by Arani (2,56,394 total voters), Tiruvannamalai (2,51,532 total voters), and Cheyyar (2,41,212 total voters) Ranipet and Tirupattur districts have four Assembly constituencies each, with a total of 9,58,271 voters and 9,28,853 voters, respectively. 916851b6fbebb160.title: Monitoring officer inspects development projects in Madurai
916851b6fbebb160.summary: Published - November 13, 2026 12:44 am IST - MADURAI Secretary to Labour Welfare and Skill Development Department and Monitoring Officer for Madurai district K. Veera Raghava Rao inspected various ongoing development projects here on Thursday. He also inspected the preparations being made for Children’s Day in Madurai district in the presence of District Collector Nishant Krishna and Corporation Commissioner Gaurav Kumar. To mark the Children’s Day, cakes would be distributed on Friday to a total of 2,69,023 students, teachers, and non-teaching staff across 1,544 government and government-aided schools in Madurai district. The Monitoring Officer held a meeting with Educational Officers regarding the arrangements and the quality of cakes. He also inspected storage arrangements made at various schools. He inspected the newly constructed wholesale onion market complex at Mattuthavani and the construction of government offices under way at Chinna Chokkikulam. Later, he presided over a review meeting held at the Collectorate to assess the progress of various development projects being implemented in the district. c416df0d5ce20919.title: Residents urge GCC to stop dumping of waste in Perungudi dumpyard
c416df0d5ce20919.summary: Published - November 13, 2026 12:35 am IST - CHENNAI Citing rising public health issues, residents have demanded that the Greater Chennai Corporation (GCC) stop dumping waste in the Perungudi dumpyard. Residents’ associations have planned to launch protests against the dumping. MCN Nagar and State Bank Colony Welfare Association secretary, M. Krishnamurthy, said: “The dumpyard generates leachate when rainwater filters through waste. Leachate seeps into the groundwater and spreads to all the surrounding areas.” K. Kalaiselvam, secretary of the Federation of Thoraipakkam Residents’ Welfare Associations, said the site released toxic air pollutants. Residents have also demanded real-time monitoring of air pollution in the areas near the dumpyard. A. Francis, president of the Federation of Thoraipakkam Residents’ Welfare Associations, said: “Biomining work is progressing at a snail’s pace. It was expected to be completed by 2024, but only 100 acres have been reclaimed so far. Residents are facing the risk of health complications. Chennai Corporation should stop dumping waste and close the dumpyard in Perungudi.” Following protests by north Chennai residents a few years ago, residents of south Chennai are also expected to launch an agitation against the dumpyard. cfc2d43380d0d226.title: No MAP relief for taxpayers using safe harbour rules: CBDT
cfc2d43380d0d226.summary: Updated cross-border tax dispute guidelines also clarify how treaty-level resolution interacts with domestic appeals, advance rulings, and settlement schemes under the Income Tax Act, 2025.
cfc2d43380d0d226.headline_en: No MAP relief for taxpayers using safe harbour rules: CBDT
cfc2d43380d0d226.raw_facts: Updated cross-border tax dispute guidelines also clarify how treaty-level resolution interacts with domestic appeals, advance rulings, and settlement schemes under the Income Tax Act, 2025.
flags: Anachronism: The 'Income Tax Act, 2025' does not exist; the current governing law in India is the Income Tax Act, 1961.

Terminology Error: 'MAP relief' (Mutual Agreement Procedure) is a treaty-based mechanism, not typically described as 'relief' in the context of safe harbour rules, which are a separate domestic tax provision.

Logical Inconsistency: Safe harbour rules are a unilateral domestic mechanism to avoid transfer pricing adjustments, whereas MAP is a bilateral treaty mechanism. Stating 'No MAP relief for taxpayers using safe harbour rules' is conceptually confused, as safe harbour users generally do not face transfer pricing disputes that would require MAP.

9a2986172ae2e393.title: Veeramani chargesheet was based on plaint lodged by minor girl
9a2986172ae2e393.summary: Published - November 13, 2026 12:36 am IST - Chennai The chargesheet against Veeramani and two of his drivers, submitted in the designated court for POCSO Act cases, was based on a complaint lodged by a minor girl. According to police sources, the survivor alleged in her complaint that she was sexually exploited by Veeramani. She had identified the octogenarian businessman during an identification process conducted by the special investigation team (SIT). Veeramani is facing seven cases under the POCSO Act and a case of abetment to suicide of a minor in 2004. The cases involve more than 10 survivors who alleged that they were sexually abused by him. The SIT was in the process of finalising the investigation in a few more cases. Prakash Kanniah, one of the accused wanted in connection with the cases, is believed to be in the U.K. After the police took steps to revoke his passport and obtain an arrest warrant from the designated court, which is required to issue a Red Corner notice, he was likely to return sometime this week, a source said. Veeramani and his drivers Parthiban and Babu were charged under various provisions of the Indian Penal Code, POCSO Act and SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act. 0a281acd971cdf13.title: Manappuram Finance Q2 results: Profit jumps over 3-fold to ₹701 crore
0a281acd971cdf13.summary: Gold loan financier Manappuram Finance Ltd on Thursday reported a more than three-fold year-on-year increase in its consolidated profit after tax (PAT) to Rs 701 crore for the September quarter of FY27. The company had posted a PAT of Rs 217.31 crore in the corresponding quarter of the previous fiscal. On a sequential basis, net profit rose 20 per cent from Rs 585 crore in the June quarter. Total income increased to Rs 3,312 crore in the second quarter of FY27, compared to Rs 2,275 crore in the year-ago period, the company said in a regulatory filing. The company's total assets under management (AUM) stood at Rs 73,303 crore as of September 2026, registering a year-on-year growth of 60 per cent. Gold Loan AUM surged 92.5 per cent YoY to Rs 60,640 crore at the end of the September quarter. Shares of Manappuram Finance settled 0.23 per cent lower at Rs 320.25 apiece on the BSE.

4c1e828f57f7883e.title: Gang held for possession of 500 kg red sanders near Sholinghur in Ranipet
4c1e828f57f7883e.summary: Published - November 13, 2026 01:12 am IST - RANIPET Officials said that the accused told them the consignment was meant to deliver to agents in Chennai. | Photo Credit: SPECIAL ARRANGEMENT A gang of three persons was arrested after the Forest Department officials seized seven red sander logs weighing around 500 kg from a car near Sholinghur town in Ranipet district on Thursday. The accused were identified them as S. Ramakrishnan, 39, V. Devinthran, 41, and T. Bhagyaraj, 35, all residents of Ranipet. Officials said that they spotted a speeding car during a patrol led by forest range officer N. Saravanan in the Neelakandaranpet Reserve Forest (RF). The team tried to stop the car along with the help of police personnel, but in vain. Forest officials and the police chased the car for around 500 metres and cornered the car at an isolated location near Sholinghur town. The team arrested the three persons after they found red sanders in the vehicle. Officials said that the accused told them the consignment was meant to deliver to agents in Chennai. The gang learnt the forests around Sholinghur town have a sizable number of red sanders that are cultivated by the Forest Department as part of an afforestation programme over a decade ago. A case was registered and the gang members were lodged at Central Prison in Vellore. The seized wooden logs were sent to the government incense sticks making unit in Tirupattur. 7dd609ea55e3ef8d.headline_en: CAG to launch in-house LLM for auditors, boost efficiency in audits
7dd609ea55e3ef8d.raw_facts: Developed by IIT Madras, the LLM is trained on 65,000 internal inspection reports and will help CAG auditors analyse financial data, identify patterns and streamline routine work
flags: Attribution Error: The Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG) is an independent constitutional body. It is highly unlikely that a major institutional LLM would be 'developed by IIT Madras' as a primary vendor without explicit mention of a specific MoU or contract, and IIT Madras is not a standard IT service provider for government audit infrastructure in this manner.

2d5df521f158a3de.title: 'Reunification is certain': Xi vows to bring Taiwan under China's control
2d5df521f158a3de.summary: President Xi Jinping on Thursday vowed to bring Taiwan under Chinese control, saying the "complete reunification" of the motherland is an "unwavering historical mission" for the ruling Communist Party of China (CPC) and will certainly be achieved. Xi, also general secretary of the CPC Central Committee and chairman of the Central Military Commission, made the remarks at a ceremony marking the 160th birth anniversary of Sun Yat-sen, one of China's nationalist leaders who is revered on both sides of the Taiwan Strait. He pledged to accommodate the island's realities but took a hard line against separatism. "Resolving the Taiwan question and realising the complete reunification of the motherland is an unwavering historical mission for the CPC, the shared aspiration of all Chinese people, and a natural requirement for the great rejuvenation of the Chinese nation," Xi was quoted as saying by the state-run Xinhua news agency. China views Taiwan as a rebel province that must be reunified

flags: Timeline Impossibility: Claiming a fully indigenous civil aircraft will be ready in two years is highly implausible given the typical 10-15 year development cycle for new commercial aircraft programs.
Policy Mismatch: The UDAN (Ude Desh ka Aam Nagrik) scheme focuses on regional connectivity using existing aircraft, not the development of a new indigenous civil aircraft platform.

Official Denial: Indian government officials and aviation experts have repeatedly stated that India does not have the current industrial capacity or active program to build a new civil aircraft in such a short timeframe.

Source Reliability: While Business Standard is a reputable source, the specific claim contradicts widely reported facts about India's aviation industry status and ongoing projects like the Tejas fighter jet (military, not civil) or the lack of a dedicated civil aircraft manufacturer.

The Ministry notified that the commission, which was constituted on June 4, 2023, “shall submit its report to the Central government as soon as possible but not later than May 20, 2027”. More than 300 people have been killed in the ethnic violence that erupted between the Kuki-Zo and Meitei people on May 3, 2023. Around 60,000 people have been displaced from their homes. The probe panel’s report is awaited even as the ethnic conflict has now spread to the Kuki and Naga communities. Since February this year, more than 60 people have been killed in Naga-Kuki clashes. The commission is now headed by former Supreme Court judge Balbir Singh Chauhan, after Ajai Lamba, the former Chief Justice of the Gauhati High Court, resigned as the chairperson of the panel in February this year. The panel is yet to finalise its report. Justice (retd.) Chauhan is also heading the judicial inquiry into an incident of violence that occurred in Ladakh’s Leh city on September 24, 2025 where four civilians, including a Kargil war veteran, were killed in police firing. The Ladakh report is yet to be submitted to the government. Manipur’s Commission of Inquiry has received around 11,000 affidavits. President’s rule was imposed in the State on February 13, 2025 and on February 4 this year, a new Chief Minister Yumnam Khemchand Singh took oath, ending Central rule. 09a099c026b5c94a.title: Rajya Sabha panel visits ISRO, HAL facilities in Bengaluru
09a099c026b5c94a.summary: Published - November 14, 2026 12:41 am IST - Bengaluru The committee also visited the Indian Space Research Organisation’s U.R. Rao Satellite Centre which is the county’s lead centre for building satellites and developing associated satellite technologies. | Photo Credit: K. Murali Kumar Members of the Subordinate Legislation Committee of Rajya Sabha on Friday visited key defence, space and finance institutions in Bengaluru as part of a study visit. The committee, led by Chairman Milind Deora, visited the Hindustan Aeronautics Limited (HAL), toured the LCA Tejas Division and witnessed a static display of the defence PSU’s various platforms. The HAL said the committee reviewed the implementation of the Companies (Corporate Social Responsibility) Rules, 2014. “HAL Chairman Ravi K., and Director (HR), M.G. Balasubrahmanya, and other senior officials were present during the interaction, which provided an opportunity to showcase the HAL’s contributions to indigenous aerospace development and its commitment to impactful and sustainable CSR initiatives,” the HAL said. The committee also visited the Indian Space Research Organisation’s U.R. Rao Satellite Centre which is the county’s lead centre for building satellites and developing associated satellite technologies. “The committee got a closer look at India’s satellite capabilities and discussed the future of our space sector from liberalisation and reusable rockets to Chandrayaan missions, space debris and e-waste regulations. While India’s space ambitions are reaching new heights, our sustainability game must keep up. Innovation and responsibility must go hand-in-hand,” Mr. Deora posted on X. The committee also held meetings with officials of the Reserve Bank of India and leading Public Sector Unit (PSU) banks to discuss the future of digital payment security. 2a18505d20b9e62f.title: Former MIDS Director P.G. Babu no more
2a18505d20b9e62f.summary: Published - November 14, 2026 12:31 am IST - Chennai P.G. Babu, former Director, Madras Institute of Development Studies. | Photo Credit: SPECIAL ARRANGEMENT P.G. Babu, former Director, Madras Institute of Development Studies, passed away in Dindigul, his hometown, on Thursday. He was 65 and is survived by his mother, a brother, and a sister. Prof. Babu was serving as the Vice-Chancellor of Vidyashilp University, Bengaluru, since 2023. During his tenure as the Director of MIDS between 2019 and 2022, he brought out a series of books in both Tamil and English, most notably on the economic policy during the pandemic. For over three decades, he had served at the Indira Gandhi Institute of Development Research, Mumbai, where he was also the Dean of Graduate Studies and coordinated the Law and Economics programmes. His research focussed on Microeconomic theory and Game theory with applications across Environmental and Natural Resource Economics, Law and Economics, and Politics-Philosophy and Economics. His research contributions include work on the decision-making framework for climate change as part of the IPCC working group, which earned him a citation from the Prime Minister of India. 0833c1b532f61694.title: Germany open to discussing critical mineral partnerships with India, says Ambassador
0833c1b532f61694.summary: Updated - November 14, 2026 12:01 am IST - COIMBATORE German Ambassador to India Jasper Wieck (right) visited the Gedee Technical Training Institute in Coimbatore city on Friday. | Photo Credit: SPECIAL ARRAGEMENT Germany’s Ministry of Economic Affairs has critical mineral partnerships already with a range of countries. With India, the channels are open to discuss how to enhance the cooperation in that domain, German Ambassador to India Jasper Wieck told The Hindu in Coimbatore on Friday. Asked about increasing recycling of industrial waste in European countries and its impact on raw material supplies to Indian companies, he said Germany also supports the Indian government in promoting and making progress in recycling and recovering industrial waste. One aspect, for example, is recycling of old solar panels because the raw materials are needed and China is increasing its export curbs. Germany is ready to further engage with India on critical minerals in order to work on sustainable solutions and securing supply chains. India and Germany share the destiny of being short of critical minerals. Circular economy is a strong part of the India-Germany Green and Sustainable Development Partnership. It will be further enhanced. But, the thrust is to support India in increasing its own recycling quota, the Ambassador said. Mr. Wieck, who visited the Gedee Technical Training Institute (GTTI) in Coimbatore, said, “Germany is keen on sharing its experience in vocational training with India. In the framework of our development cooperation, we have many programmes that encourage Indian companies to provide for training on the spot in close cooperation, for instance, with Indian technical institutes,” he said. Germany already recognises Indian dual vocational training certificates thereby enabling a smooth transition into the German labour market, if needed. f647fe46dbf1ca20.summary: Electrification and automation major ABB India on Friday posted an 11 per cent rise in net profit to Rs 440 crore in the September quarter compared to the year-ago period, driven by higher revenues. The company follows a January-December fiscal year. The net profit was Rs 398 crore in the quarter ended on September 30, 2025, an exchange filing showed. Revenues from operations rose to Rs 3,738 crore in the quarter from Rs 3,130 crore in the same period a year ago. ABB India Managing Director Sanjeev Sharma said, "We delivered a strong third quarter, with record Q3 orders, revenue growth and a healthy backlog reflecting continued customer confidence in ABB's technology and solutions." He stated that the demand remained broad-based across industries, supported by investments in productivity, energy efficiency and sustainable growth. Looking ahead, he stated that India's structural growth drivers in industrialisation, electrification, digitalisation and the energy transition continue

e4645697523cef00.summary: India, the world's second-largest gold consumer, relies heavily on imports to meet demand | Image: Bloomberg India's merchandise trade deficit widened to a one-year high of $39.88 billion in October, exceeding forecasts as festive-season gold purchases and higher energy ​costs drove up imports. The deficit topped the $32.25 billion forecast in a Reuters ​poll and widened from $30.21 billion in September. The trade deficit last hit a record $42.58 billion in October ‌2025. Gold imports nearly tripled to $5.51 billion from $1.8 billion in September, as jewellers and consumers stepped up purchases ahead of the Hindu festival of Diwali, when buying gold is considered auspicious. India, the world's second-largest gold consumer, relies heavily on imports to meet demand. Mid-month, India's market regulator nudged asset management firms to halt bulk purchases of gold exchange-traded funds to limit investment demand for gold-backed products. A senior official said the recovery in gold imports this month was likely driven by a correction in global prices and pre-festive demand, though trade flows are influenced by multiple factors. India, the world's third-largest oil consumer after the United States and China, has also faced higher import costs due to energy-market disruptions caused by ‌the Middle East conflict. India imports nearly 85% of its crude needs. Brent crude futures have since fallen to around $95 a barrel, offering relief amid hopes of de-escalation following the Democrats' victory in the US midterm elections. Merchandise exports rose to $49.47 billion in October, up from the $44.40 billion of the previous month, government data showed, while imports rose to $89.35 billion against $74.61 billion in September. 4261476b303c73f9.title: Comply with new prices of 137 anti-cancer drugs or face action, says regulator
4261476b303c73f9.summary: Published - November 14, 2026 01:24 am IST - NEW DELHI The revised prices for the 137 anti-cancer drugs came into effect on November 9, 2026, following a gazette order issued on October 17, 2026. The order capped the trade margin on these medicines at 30%. File image used for representation | Photo Credit: Getty Images/iStockphoto The National Pharmaceutical Pricing Authority (NPPA) has warned of penal action against those failing to comply with the revised prices of 137 non-scheduled anti-cancer drugs The authority, which functions under the Department of Pharmaceuticals, has asked State drug controllers (SDCs) to strictly monitor the prices and submit their action taken reports by November 16, according to an official release on Friday (November 13, 2026). The revised prices for the 137 anti-cancer drugs came into effect on November 9, 2026, following a gazette order issued on October 17, 2026. The order capped the trade margin on these medicines at 30%. Based on submissions received from pharmaceutical companies up to November 11, the latest revised price lists have been uploaded on the NPPA website as well as the Pharma Sahi Daam app and portal, the Chemicals and Fertilizers Ministry said. All manufacturers, stockists, dealers, retailers, hospitals, and medical institutions have been directed to comply with the revised prices and prominently display the updated price lists at their premises and on their websites. The SDCs have been instructed to strictly monitor compliance across the supply chain and healthcare facilities to ensure that the benefits of the revised maximum retail prices (MRPs) are passed on to patients. Any violation of the directive may attract overcharging proceedings under the provisions of the DPCO, 2013, the release noted. Complaints regarding overcharging, shortage, or non-availability of medicines can be reported through the Pharma Sahi Daam app or portal, the NPPA helpline (1800-111-255), or via email at monitoring-nppa@gov.in, it added.

a85d2bf44a8cf4e9.title: Edelweiss Financial Services Q2 FY27 results: Profit rises 18% to ₹207 cr
a85d2bf44a8cf4e9.summary: Edelweiss Financial Services on Friday reported an 18 per cent growth in consolidated net profit to Rs 207 crore for the second quarter ended September. The company had earned a profit of Rs 175 crore in the corresponding quarter of the preceding fiscal. Total income increased to Rs 2,602 crore in the second quarter of FY27, compared to Rs 1,900 crore in the year-ago period, Edelweiss Financial Services said in a regulatory filing. Interest income rose to Rs 720 crore from Rs 687 crore in the same quarter a year ago. During the quarter, total expenses also rose to Rs 2,393 crore from Rs 1,946 crore in the same period a year ago. The company completed the Rs 1,200-crore IPO of its subsidiary Edelweiss Alternatives last month. Earlier this year, global investment management firm Carlyle became a strategic majority investor in another subsidiary of the company, Nido Home Finance, with an investment of Rs 2,000 crore.

054e4d7fccd674ae.title: BIM, Texas university to offer course on AI in Business from next year
054e4d7fccd674ae.summary: Published - November 14, 2026 12:44 am IST - Chennai Bharathidasan Institute of Management (BIM), in collaboration with the University of Texas at Arlington (UTA) in the U.S., on Friday announced the launch of the Master of Science programme in Artificial Intelligence for Business (MSAIB), which is aimed at working professionals in India. On Friday, representatives of the two institutions exchanged Memoranda of Understanding for the course. The first batch of the course will start in August 2027. The first cohort will include 25 students, mostly working professionals, who are keen to upgrade their skills to secure better job opportunities in multinational companies, and the tuition fee is indicated to be around $27,000. Asit K. Barma, Director, BIM, told presspersons in Chennai that the classes would be held at the IIT-Madras Research Park. The location, being a technology hub, will be beneficial to students in terms of access to industry interactions. Keerthana. According to details shared by Guidance, the discussion focused on accelerating the development of Grade-A office space and supporting infrastructure across the identified corridors to meet the needs of the state’s growing Global Capability Centre (GCC) ecosystem. The roundtable brought together developers’ perspectives on strengthening these corridors as integrated destinations for GCC investment and growth. Tamil Nadu is home to more than 460 GCCs, including over 405 in Chennai, with the sector adding more than 55,000 jobs in 2025. Continued expansion by existing centres, alongside interest from new investors, has increased the need for readily available, high-quality office space. Participants discussed measures to accelerate project development, maintain competitive rentals and ensure that suitable space is available within the timelines required by global companies. Developers shared their perspectives on land availability, development costs, floor space index (FSI), approval processes and infrastructure requirements. The discussion emphasised the importance of developing complete GCC ecosystems in Rajiv Gandhi Salai (OMR), Pallavaram–Thoraipakkam Radial Road (PTR) and Mount–Poonamallee High Road (MPR) through mixed-use projects that integrate offices with housing, schools, healthcare, hospitality and retail. Public transport, last-mile connectivity and pedestrian access were identified as essential to supporting the growth of these corridors. Participants noted and appreciated the greater transparency and accountability they had experienced

5c01144be5e1a2d0.title: Modi comes to aid of elderly woman who felt unwell at Mysuru event
5c01144be5e1a2d0.summary: Published - November 14, 2026 12:02 am IST - MYSURU Prime Minister Narendra Modi personally came to the aid of an elderly woman who felt unwell during the inauguration of the COSMOS Planetarium in Mysuru on Friday. The woman, Prema Simbaiah, former president of Nanjangud Town Municipality and a BJP worker, appeared to feel dizzy and was on the verge of collapsing. Noticing her condition, Mr. Modi went up to her and ensured that she received immediate attention. She was given juice to help her recover. Union Minister for Finance and Corporate Affairs Nirmala Sitharaman was also present at the event. Mysuru district BJP president Subbanna later visited Ms. Simbaiah at her residence to enquire about her health. He said she was doing well. Thanking Mr. Modi for coming to her aid, Ms. Simbaiah said she had felt uncomfortable as she had not had lunch before arriving at the venue. She expressed her gratitude to the Prime Minister for providing her with juice and ensuring that she recovered. 9bad3be65f765bb1.title: Over 7,000 books removed from District Central Libraries in Vellore, nearby districts
9bad3be65f765bb1.summary: Published - November 14, 2026 12:39 am IST - VELLORE The library in Ranipet. | Photo Credit: Special Arrangement As many as 7,995 books published by the controversial Agalvilakku and Phoenix Publications were removed from the racks of District Central Library in Vellore, Ranipet, Tirupattur, and Tiruvannamalai districts on Friday. The action comes against the backdrop of allegations of fake and AI-generated books being procured from these publishers for public libraries including Periyar Arivulagam, a newly inaugurated public library in Coimbatore. “The identified books of the two publications were removed from the other books. The books, which are meant for distribution to branch libraries in the district for 2025-26, are stored in a separate room,” S. Valli, District Library Officer (Tiruvannamalai), told The Hindu. Ranipet and Tirupattur have the highest number (2,401) of books each from these publications, followed by Tiruvannamalai (2,209 books), and Vellore (984 books). “Books on competitive examinations are a big attraction in District Central library as the facility has a large collection of books related to general knowledge,” said G. Satish, a reader. Officials said District Central Library in these districts have books on subjects including history, politics, law, economics, philosophy, agriculture, computer and mathematics. Reference books, especially for examinations conducted by the Tamil Nadu Public Service Commission (TNPSC), UPSC, and other competitive exams are available. As per norms, around 60,000 to 70,000 books are procured for each district library annually based on feedback provided by local librarians and readers. These books then distributed branch libraries in the district. As per estimates, Vellore and Tiruvannamalai have at least 120 branch libraries each whereas Ranipet and Tirupattur have around 50 branch libraries each. File | Photo Credit: R.V. Moorthy India's star all-rounder Deepti Sharma was on Friday named the ICC Women's Player of the Month for October, winning the award for the second time in her career following a series of impressive performances against Zimbabwe. "The series against Zimbabwe was a great one for us, and I'm proud of the way the team performed, especially the youngsters. "Scoring a century was a particularly special moment for me, made even more meaningful as it contributed to a winning cause." Last year during this month, Deepti starred in India's World Cup triumph, and this year she showed fine form in the contests against Zimbabwe. "I would like to thank the voting panel and fans for this recognition, as well as my teammates and coaches for their continued support," she said. "I would like to dedicate this award to my fans across the world." She yielded critical outputs across the two formats in Zimbabwe's inbound tour. Deepti began with a quickfire 49 in the first T20I against Zimbabwe in Raipur to help setup a victory after the hosts were in a spot of bother at 19/4. Over the series, she collected two wickets to help India secure a clean sweep. That form translated across to the ODI series as Deepti secured two wickets in the series opener in another India triumph. This was followed by her standout performance in the second ODI, where the 29-year-old hit her second ODI century and chipped in with three valuable wickets as India clinched a 2-0 lead in the series. 599ef64f8dbe8628.title: Two men die as van rams tree in Tirupattur
599ef64f8dbe8628.summary: Updated - November 14, 2026 12:41 am IST - TIRUPATTUR Two men and two cows killed after a van hit a roadside tree at Pudur village near Vaniyambadi town in Tirupattur on Friday. Police said K. Bhoopathy, 62, and V. Sankar, 28, both dairy farmers near Alangayam town, were taking the cows on the van to sell them at the weekly cattle market in Uthangarai village near Hosur. Bhoopathy’s son Manikandan, 28, and two other farmers Murugesan, 58, and Krishnan, 56, were also travelling with them. Police said that Manikandan lost control of the vehicle and rammed a roadside tree. In the impact, Manikandan and Sankar, sustained severe injuries and succumbed on the way to hospital. The two cows were killed. The other three men are under treatment. The incident occurred around 4 a.m. The Kavalur police have registered a case. a6347c7918943627.title: Natco Pharma Q2 results: Net profit declines 60.8% to ₹202.6 crore
a6347c7918943627.summary: Natco Pharma on Friday posted a 60.8 per cent decline in consolidated net profit to Rs 202.6 crore during the September quarter, weighed down by a fall in revenues. The pharma company had reported a net profit of Rs 517.9 crore in the corresponding period of the preceding fiscal. The Delhi High Court has taken suo motu cognisance of the condition of the Sriniwaspuri drain, citing its significant impact on waterlogging in the area and rampant illegal constructions on and around it. A Bench of Justice Prathiba M. Singh and Justice Manmeet P.S. Arora, while disposing of an appeal filed by residents of Sriniwaspuri, directed that the matter be converted into a fresh suo motu petition. The development came after the appellants, who had approached the court seeking proper maintenance, cleaning and reconstruction of drains in the area, sought permission to withdraw their appeal, stating that they did not wish to pursue the proceedings because of the continuous threats they were facing from local residents. In its November 5 order, the court allowed the appellants to withdraw their petition but made it clear that the larger public interest issues concerning the drain could not be ignored. “Owing to the large-scale impact of the drain on the general waterlogging in the area, as also the rampant illegal construction upon and around the drain, this is a fit case for the Court to not ignore the facts that have come to light in the various reports, including the recent inspection report of the Integrated Drain Management Cell (IDMC),” the court said. “Accordingly, the Court takes suo motu cognisance of the situation relating to the Sriniwaspuri drain. 97fc796799d8e5cb.title: Four-day Chhath festival begins in Bihar with Nahay Khay
97fc796799d8e5cb.summary: Published - November 14, 2026 01:10 am IST - PATNA Devotees arrive to offer prayers and take a holy dip in the Ganga River on 'Nahay Khay', the first day of Chhath Puja, in Patna on November 13, 2026. | Photo Credit: ANI Bihar’s famous Chhath festival began on Friday (November 13, 2026) with Nahay Khay on the first of four days of festivities. A large number of devotees gathered at ghats by rivers, including the Ganga, to collect water and bathe. The festival is performed with piety and the strict observance of fasts to express gratitude to the Sun God for sustaining life on Earth. There are no formal rituals or priests present, and devotion is central to the prayers. The people of Purvanchal (eastern Uttar Pradesh, Bihar and Jharkhand) celebrate Chhath Puja on a grand scale. On the first day, all Chhath vratis (devotees holding fasts) bathe in the morning and offer prayers to the rising Sun before partaking in rice and pumpkin curry. On the second day, Kharna, roti and kheer are cooked as prasad in the evening, followed by two continuous days of fasting. On the third day, devotees offer arghya (obeisance) to the setting Sun at the ghats of rivers or temporary water bodies created by the State government, continuing their fast. The Chhath festival this year will conclude on November 16 after devotees offer arghya to the rising Sun on the fourth day, marking the end of the fast. Out of 103 ghats in Patna, 90 have been declared safe for devotees, while 13 have been declared unsafe this year. Chhath Puja is also being celebrated in over a dozen parks in Patna, which already have fountains and water bodies, including Eco Park, Harding Park, Naveen Sinha Park, Lal Bahadur Shastri Park, AG Colony Park, Urja Park, CID Colony Park, and Lohia Nagar Park, and the lake at the Patna Zoo. They have undergone cleaning, and other improvements, including the provision of changing rooms, barricades, floodlit towers, and elaborate lighting installations. “Heartfelt wishes to all fell

406209c89fb3f98c.title: Man held for setting house on fire in Vellore
406209c89fb3f98c.summary: Updated - November 14, 2026 01:01 am IST - VELLORE The house that was gutted. | Photo Credit: Special Arrangement A 54-year-old man was arrested by the Veppankuppam police on charges of setting on fire his daughter’s house at Agaram village near Odugathur town at foothills of Jawadhu Hills in Vellore on Friday. Police said the accused R. Anandan, 54, a wage labourer, was upset over his daughter Vaishnavi marrying Rajesh, a milk van driver, against his wishes. In a fit of rage, Anandan allegedly set on fire Rajesh’s father Kumar’s house in Agaram village. Residents alerted Veppankuppam police, who rushed to the spot with firefighters. The house, which was unoccupied, was gutted. A case was registered and Anandan was arrested. 7f05c1744b84c178.title: Decade-long efforts averted energy crisis during war: PM Narendra Modi
7f05c1744b84c178.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Friday said steps taken in the last decade helped the country to sail through the crisis emerged during the war in the Middle East. He was inaugurating various welfare projects worth over Rs 15,600 crore here, including renewable energy and petroleum infrastructure. "War around Iran and Gulf countries shows how important energy security is. Steps taken for energy security in the last decade helped the country face the crisis with resilience," the PM said. Regarding the Metro Pink Line, which was dedicated to the public, Modi said it gives better connectivity to people in Bengaluru. He also noted that the Metro rail network increased from 17 km in 2014 to over 100 km in 2026 in Bengaluru. On the occasion, Modi lauded Karnataka Governor Sudha Yadav for serving the nation as the widow of a Kargil war hero.

2ef3827eb26815aa.title: IIT entrance exam JEE-Advanced to be conducted on May 23, 2027: IIT Delhi
2ef3827eb26815aa.summary: IIT entrance exam JEE-Advanced will be conducted on May 23, 2027, the Indian Institute of Technology (IIT), Delhi, which will be organising the crucial exam, announced on Friday. The top-scoring 2.5 lakh candidates in JEE-Main are allowed to appear for JEE-Advanced. "The Joint Entrance Exam (JEE)-Advanced will be held on May 23, 2027," an official notification said. "The candidates appearing for JEE-Advanced will have the provision of using an on-screen basic (non-scientific) calculator with a 10-12 digit display," it added. Aspirants are allowed a maximum of two attempts in two consecutive years. The first attempt must be taken in the year of passing Class 12 and the second attempt in the following consecutive year.

88274b4b7367c7de.title: Bengal draft voter list on Nov 23, final electoral rolls on Jan 16
88274b4b7367c7de.summary: The Election Commission will publish the draft electoral rolls for West Bengal on November 23, with the final voters' list scheduled to be released on January 16, 2027, as part of a Special Summary Revision (SSR), a statement said on Friday. The revision will be conducted with January 1, 2027, as the qualifying date, allowing those who turn 18 by then to enrol as voters, it said. According to the schedule announced by the Chief Electoral Officer's (CEO) office, electors can submit claims and objections between November 23 and December 22. The disposal of applications will be completed by January 8. Special campaign days will be held at designated polling stations across the state on November 28 and 29, and December 5, 6, 12, 13, 19 and 20 to facilitate public participation, the statement said. Booth Level Officers (BLOs) will be available at polling stations on these days to assist voters with fresh enrolment, correction of particulars and submission of claims and objections. Boot

A case in point is inflation. The latest data on retail inflation show that it crossed the Reserve Bank of India’s 6% upper comfort limit in October 2026. According to economists, this is likely to continue through the third quarter of this financial year, which means at least two more months of high inflation. Agricultural shortfalls brought on by a patchy and deficient monsoon have meant that food inflation rose sharply to 8.5% in October 2026. Elevated fuel prices meant that inflation in the transport category also rose sharply. What is worse is that high inflation is spreading to almost every aspect of a household’s day-to-day needs. In fact, the latest Consumer Price Index (CPI) data show that 10 of the 12 major categories saw inflation in October, hitting their highest levels recorded in the new series of the index. So, things such as clothing, footwear, housing, furnishings, and services such as healthcare, education, communication, recreation, and restaurant and hospitality are not only getting more expensive, but they are doing so at an accelerating rate. This would have been bad enough had wages been increasing in real terms. Yet, the latest research by Data for India on the country’s official wage statistics shows that, while nominal wages doubled from 2012 to 2024, they actually fell 4% over the same period after adjusting for inflation. And this is sharper for high-skilled and high-earning workers. Lower wage earners saw marginal increases over this period. While this is of some comfort, it is the higher wage earners that drive consumption in an economy. Real wage contraction for them, which is likely to have worsened in 2026, will hit consumption levels and private investment. 6be81aa7223ce5c1.summary: Essar Group's IT firm Black Box on Friday reported a 30.6 per cent increase in consolidated net profit to Rs 72.68 crore for the July-September quarter of FY27, aided by growth in data centre and enterprise businesses. b8602c9e790f5ba7.title: Librarian P.V. Konnur felicitated on his 75th birth anniversary
b8602c9e790f5ba7.summary: Published - November 14, 2026 12:32 am IST - Bengaluru Friends, colleagues and admirers of P.V. Konnur, the library science professional and president of LIS Academy, Bengaluru, felicitated him on his 75th birth anniversary. The Amruta Mahotsava was held at the Dr. Manmohan Singh Bengaluru City University on Thursday. Ramesh B., Vice-Chancellor of Dr. Manmohan Singh Bengaluru City University, released the felicitation volume brought out in Prof. Konnur’s honour and he said that such a dedicated librarian is very hard to find today, and that Prof. Konnur is a role model for budding librarians. He observed that the librarian’s role has become more challenging, as students now have to be drawn back to libraries from their mobile phones. He urged Prof. Konnur to lead this movement and to help university libraries become experiential centres. 2ff26f97a71862cf.title: Sammaan Capital Q2 FY27 results: Net profit rises 1.25% to ₹312 crore
2ff26f97a71862cf.summary: Non-bank lender Sammaan Capital on Saturday reported a 1.25 per cent increase in its September quarter net profit to Rs 312.34 crore compared to Rs 308.47 crore in the same quarter of last year. The company had reported a net profit of Rs 243.30 crore in the preceding June quarter. Its total income declined to Rs 1,850.85 crore in the reporting quarter from Rs 2,260.52 crore in the year-ago period, which included a decline in the core interest income to Rs 1,161.26 crore from Rs 1,449.02 crore. Total expenses also declined to Rs 1,426.28 crore from Rs 1,835.49 crore in the year-ago period, as per a regulatory filing. Assets under management grew by 5 per cent to Rs 59,188 crore as of end-June 2026, driven by a 62 per cent jump in disbursements to Rs 6,278 crore. It aims to increase AUM to Rs 70,000 crore by March 2027. The company added more branches during the quarter to take its overall network to 245 as of September 30, and is aiming to take the same to 270 by end of the fiscal

8228d1c2a5e8563a.title: YMCA Madras launches IAS Academy for persons with hearing and speech disabilities
8228d1c2a5e8563a.summary: Published - November 15, 2026 05:30 am IST - Chennai YMCA Madras on Saturday launched an IAS Academy aimed at training persons with speech and hearing disabilities to face civil services examinations. Classes will be conducted at the YMCA Building on NSC Bose Road. The first batch will have 50 students, 43 of whom are speech and hearing impaired. For this year, YMCA Madras has tied up with St. Louis Institute for the Deaf and the Blind in Adyar. In the classroom, students will have support in the form of sign language specialists and a software that transcribes speech to text in real time. The initiative is part of YMCA’s MY Institute project that provides academic support, skill programmes, and sports and cultural activities for students. Inaugurating the academy, Justice P.T. Asha of the Madras High Court, said civil servants form the backbone of a government and the link between the Union and the States, the people, and the government. “The duty of an IAS officer is to ensure continuity in functioning of the government irrespective of the party in power,” she said, adding they are tasked with formulating and implementing policies. Irai Anbu, former Chief Secretary of Tamil Nadu, offered tips to the students for the UPSC examinations. He said their preparation should be structured and they should dedicate 12 hours a day for 400 days if they are to crack the civil services examinations. Albert Fernando, chairperson, MY Institute-IAS Academy, said that according to the 2011 Census and records available with the State Commissionerate for the Welfare of the Disabled, there were about 2,20,024 persons with hearing impairment, 80,077 persons with speech impairment, and 92,796 with both disabilities in Tamil Nadu. V. Nandakumar, Commissioner of Income Tax, and P. Asir Pandian, General Secretary and CEO, YMCA Madras, also spoke. 48277b4b616c3083.title: Take necessary steps to control inflation, Dhinakaran tells T.N. govt.
48277b4b616c3083.summary: Published - November 15, 2026 12:54 am IST - Chennai T.T.V. Dhinakaran | Photo Credit: R. ASHOK Amma Makkal Munnetra Kazhagam (AMMK) general secretary T.T.V. Dhinakaran on Saturday said Tamil Nadu ranks first in India in price rise and urged the TVK-led government to take necessary measures to control the surge in prices of essential commodities. Stating Tamil Nadu holds the top spot in India for price hikes as retail inflation in the State has risen to 7.29 per cent, Mr. Dhinakaran said this occurred as a result of negligence in monitoring the price rise and failing to take timely action to control it. “Without taking any steps to control the price rise of essential commodities, the TVK government merely watched as a bystander and was focused only on covering up the real situation, while now boasting that they have kept the prices of items including rice, sugar, and pulses under control and prevented hoarding,” he alleged. Mr. Dhinakaran said Tamil Nadu, which was once a pioneering state in India, has been pushed into an abyss over the past six months due to the inefficient administration of the TVK rule. He demanded that the government abandon efforts to divert the public through false propaganda on social media via “Paid Virtual Warriors,” and immediately undertake constructive measures necessary to control the price rise of essential commodities. 752829ddf5823b16.title: Patanjali Foods Q2 FY27 results: Net profit falls 19% to ₹420 crore
752829ddf5823b16.summary: Patanjali Foods Ltd on Saturday reported 19 per cent fall in consolidated net profit at Rs 419.76 crore for the quarter ended September 30, 2026 despite rise in revenue. Its net profit stood at Rs 516.69 crore in the year-ago period. Total income rose to Rs 11,406.49 crore in the second quarter of the current fiscal from Rs 9,850.06 crore a year ago, according to a regulatory filing. Total operational expenses went up to Rs 10,997.51 crore from Rs 9,344.97 crore. During the first six months of this fiscal, the net profit rose to Rs 755.49 crore from Rs 697.05 crore in the year-ago period. Total income grew to Rs 22,748.38 crore from Rs 18,629.08 crore. Incorporated in 1986, Patanjali Foods is one of the leading FMCG players in India. The company is present in edible oils, FMCG, and wind power generation segments. It sells products under different brands including Patanjali, Ruchi Gold, Nutrela, Dant Kanti, Mahakosh and Sunrich.
