18214fc7b57a6fc9.title: Residents seek exemption of taxes for non-commercial vehicles at Pallikonda toll plaza
18214fc7b57a6fc9.summary: Published - November 15, 2026 05:30 am IST - VELLORE Residents in 12 farming villages have been demanding exemption of taxes at a toll plaza in Pallikonda town on the Chennai – Bengaluru Highway (NH 48), which is maintained by National Authority of India (NHAI). “The stretch helps reach government hospitals in big towns like Gudiyatham, Anaicut, Vellore towns easier. Exemption of toll should be given to locals, who are mostly marginal farmers and petty traders,” said B. Pasupathi, a resident. As per study, more than 75,000 vehicles, mainly trucks and container lorries, use the stretch to reach Chennai and Bengaluru every day. The stretch has at least 20 underpasses to allow residents to cross the stretch. It also has four toll plazas between Walajah (Ranipet) and Krishnagiri, a distance of 148 km. “Special passes at nominal rates have been provided to residents in surrounding villages. Complete waiver of toll fee for residents is not feasible,” a NHAI official told The Hindu . At present, residents within a 20-km-radius of Pallikonda toll plaza are provided with a monthly special pass for non-commercial vehicles, with a fee of ₹360. Vehicles should be registered with a local permanent address to avail special passes. “Most of the residents are farmers and tractors are not allowed to pass the toll plaza, as they have been classified as commercial vehicles. After harvest, a large number of tractors are roped in to transport paddy to government godowns in towns. The toll plaza should exempt vehicles that form part of farming activity,” said T. Veeraiyah, a farmer. Residents said complete exemption of toll fee will help them cut travel cost and boost agriculture in the area. 18214fc7b57a6fc9.raw_facts: Published - November 15, 2026 05:30 am IST - VELLORE Residents in 12 farming villages have been demanding exemption of taxes at a toll plaza in Pallikonda town on the Chennai – Bengaluru Highway (NH 48), which is maintained by National Authority of India (NHAI). “The stretch helps reach government hospitals in big towns like Gudiyatham, Anaicut, Vellore towns easier. Exemption of toll should be given to locals, who are mostly marginal farmers and petty traders,” said B. Pasupathi, a resident. As per study, more than 75,000 vehicles, mainly trucks and container lorries, use the stretch to reach Chennai and Bengaluru every day. The stretch has at least 20 underpasses to allow residents to cross the stretch. It also has four toll plazas between Walajah (Ranipet) and Krishnagiri, a distance of 148 km. “Special passes at nominal rates have been provided to residents in surrounding villages. Complete waiver of toll fee for residents is not feasible,” a NHAI official told The Hindu . At present, residents within a 20-km-radius of Pallikonda toll plaza are provided with a monthly special pass for non-commercial vehicles, with a fee of ₹360. Vehicles should be registered with a local permanent address to avail special passes. “Most of the residents are farmers and tractors are not allowed to pass the toll plaza, as they have been classified as commercial vehicles. After harvest, a large number of tractors are roped in to transport paddy to government godowns in towns. The toll plaza should exempt vehicles that form part of farming activity,” said T. Veeraiyah, a farmer. Residents said complete exemption of toll fee will help them cut travel cost and boost agriculture in the area. But with the first-stage booster exploding shortly after Friday’s liftoff from Texas, the company fell short of its desired double catch. The space agency is paying billions of dollars for Starship to land Artemis astronauts on the moon later this decade and help build a permanent lunar base. Musk’s ambitions are even grander: He wants to launch a fleet of Starships to build a city on Mars. Separating neatly from its booster before things went awry, the upper-stage spacecraft soared into orbit and released 26 advanced Starlink satellites. Starship continued circling the world 165 miles (265 kilometres) up, with live views of itself and Earth streaming down via Starlink. Revanth Reddy assured the Public Health Foundation of India (PHFI) of the State government’s full support for establishing its Institute of Public Health Sciences (IPHS) Deemed-to-be University in Hyderabad, setting June 2, 2028, as the deadline for completing the proposed campus and promising assistance with land, funds, permissions and other requirements. 87ffa41497719095.title: Telangana Greyhounds get new shooting range at Rajendranagar
87ffa41497719095.summary: Updated - November 15, 2026 02:05 am IST - HYDERABAD DGP CV Anand with Anil Kumar, Director General of Police (Operations) and head of the Greyhounds and OCTOPUS units, and other senior officers at the Telangana Greyhounds facility in Rajendranagar, Hyderabad, on Saturday. Director General of Police C.V. Anand on Saturday inaugurated the SPS OODA Shoot House at the Telangana Greyhounds facility in Rajendranagar, with the unit asked to maintain its strength at no less than 700 personnel, and continue rigorous operational training. The new facility has been named after martyrs Sandeep, Pavan and Sridhar. The OODA concept, which stands for Observe, Orient, Decide and Act, has been incorporated into its training approach to help commandos assess situations, make decisions and respond quickly. Speaking at the event, Mr. Anand described the Telangana Greyhounds as a model for police forces across the country and said the unit, along with OCTOPUS, played an important role in addressing threats such as Naxalism, terrorism and hijackings. He recalled the role played by the Greyhounds in tackling Naxalite activities and terrorist threats during the 1980s. The DGP called for continuous training in jungle warfare and operations in rugged, hilly terrain, and asked personnel to remain prepared to respond to emergencies, including hijackings and terrorist attacks. He also urged the team to secure first place in the All India Police Commando Competition scheduled to begin in Jodhpur, Rajasthan, on February 2, 2027. The Telangana Greyhounds secured fourth place in the competition held two years ago. Mr. Anand also referred to the unit’s parade during the National Unity Day celebrations at Kevadia in Gujarat on October 31, which received appreciation. He commended personnel who had excelled in training and marksmanship. 19c537da3dcfd703.title: Total Chess: Martirosyan inflicts first loss on Carlsen
19c537da3dcfd703.summary: Published - November 14, 2026 11:20 pm IST - BUDAPEST Martirosyan posted a win over World No. 1 Magnus Carlsen before drawing the return game. | Photo Credit: Flickr.com Magnus Carlsen suffered his first loss in the Total Chess World Championship Tour pilot as Haik Martirosyan beat the World No. 1 and took the outright Group C lead on the third day of the Fast Classic stage here on Friday. The Armenian won with white before drawing their return encounter, leaving Carlsen winless after six games. Martirosyan had 10 points to Carlsen’s five. R. Vaishali secured her first Fast Classic victory, recovering from a defeat against Bibisara Assaubayeva to win their second meeting with an attack. The split results left the Indian on four points and the Kazakh on eight in Group D. Arjun Erigaisi overturned a difficult position to beat Wesley So with black before drawing the return match. His nine points put him level with Hans Niemann, three behind leader Maxime Vachier-Lagrave. R. Praggnanandhaa drew both games against Vladislav Artemiev in Group B, their first encounter lasting 89 moves. The Indian had four points and Artemiev five. Martirosyan’s attacking victory over Carlsen helped him move one point clear of Anish Giri, who followed a draw against Ian Nepomniachtchi with a win after a long battle. Nepomniachtchi and Shakhriyar Mamedyarov had seven points each. Mamedyarov drew twice against Abhimanyu Mishra, who had five. Vachier-Lagrave drew his game against Niemann before winning the return with white to reach 12 points. So had four. Group B leader Fabiano Caruana beat Vincent Keymer with black and drew their second game. Unbeaten with four wins and two draws, he had 14 points, four clear of Liem Le, who drew twice against Richard Rapport. Keymer had four points and Rapport five. In Group A, Andrew Hong handed Alireza Firouzja his first group-stage defeat before the leader won their return meeting. Firouzja retained top spot with 11 points. Hong had six. Jan-Krzysztof Du

7df78a651aea740f.title: Synod of Jacobite Church approves steps to canonise Patriarch Ignatius Peter III
7df78a651aea740f.summary: Published - November 15, 2026 01:00 am IST - KOCHI The Episcopal Synod of the Jacobite Syrian Church on Saturday (November 14) decided to complete the procedures to canonise Patriarch Ignatius Peter III, who convened the historic Mulanthuruthy Synod in 1876. The decision was taken as Patriarch Ignatius Aphrem II, the supreme head of the Universal Syrian Orthodox Church, accepted the Jacobite Church’s request to declare Ignatius Peter III a saint. A statement by the Jacobite Syrian Church said the decision was taken at a meeting of the Episcopal Synod, chaired by Patriarch Ignatius Aphrem II, at the Marthoman Cathedral in Mulanthuruthy during the 150th anniversary celebrations of the Mulanthuruthy Synod. Addressing the synod, the Patriarch called for collective efforts to establish lasting peace in the Malankara Church. Hailing from Mosul, Ignatius Peter III was the Patriarch of Antioch and head of the Syriac Orthodox Church from 1872 until he died in 1894. 2b47ede68deb4619.title: CBI searches 33 locations in six states in Mahadev betting app case
2b47ede68deb4619.summary: The CBI has conducted searches at 33 locations across six states in connection with its investigation into Mahadev online betting app case, recovering digital devices, mobile phones and documents indicating the use of mule bank accounts and hawala channels, officials said on Saturday. The agency said the searches were conducted on the basis of disclosures made by Sourabh Chandrakar, one of the platform's principal promoters, following his extradition from Oman. The searches, carried out over the past few days, targeted premises linked to panel operators of the betting platform, they said. The CBI spokesperson said live betting and gambling panels were found operating at several locations and subsequently dismantled. Chandrakar was extradited from Oman and arrested by the CBI on November 1.

Officials of Tamil Nadu State Transport Corporation (TNSTC) said that as part of preparatory works for the festival, L. Nirmal Raj, Secretary, Department of Transport, inspected a few temporary bus termini in the presence of Collector Vandhana Garg, S. Sridharan, Managing Director, TNSTC, and G. Kalaiselvan, deputy general manager (Commercial), TNSTC (Tiruvannamalai). “Basic amenities at the temporary bus termini will be done by the civic body. Additional sanitary workers will be roped in to keep the temple town clean during the festival,” K. Balasubramanian, Commissioner, Tiruvannamalai Corporation, told The Hindu. The transport department will operate 180 shuttle services from the bus termini to the 14-km Girivalam path and the Arunachaleswara temple. Private vehicles will not be allowed to enter town, especially during Maha Deepam day, to avoid congestion. Each commuter will be charged ₹10 for these services. Vehicles will be allowed to park in over 100 car parking lots that are away from the town. The parking space can accommodate around 20,000 vehicles. Jute mats will be laid upto a distance of two km, for visitors to beat the heat. Children at the festival will have wrist bands for safety. Roy memorial seminar on Saturday in the Nuclear Fuel Complex (NFC) on the theme - Innovations in Green Technologies & Sustainable Manufacturing: Shaping the Future of Chemical Engineering. a29277a425951066.title: Eight varieties of pharmaceutical ingredients worth ₹3.54 lakh seized in TG SAFE raid at Ameenpur firm
a29277a425951066.summary: Published - November 15, 2026 02:00 am IST - HYDERABAD The drugs wing of the Telangana Standards Authority for Food and Essential Drugs (TG SAFE) seized illegally stocked Active Pharmaceutical Ingredients (APIs) worth ₹3.54 lakh during a raid at a private company in Sultanpur village of Ameenpur mandal in Sangareddy district. | Photo Credit: Special Arrangement The drugs wing of the Telangana Standards Authority for Food and Essential Drugs (TG SAFE) seized illegally stocked Active Pharmaceutical Ingredients (APIs) worth ₹3.54 lakh during a raid at a private company in Sultanpur village of Ameenpur mandal in Sangareddy district. The raid was conducted at Neocell Biotechnologies Private Limited, located at the Medical Devices Park in Sultanpur, on Friday, following credible information about the illegal stocking of pharmaceutical ingredients for sale without a valid drug licence. According to TG SAFE, officials found eight varieties of APIs illegally stocked at the premises and seized drug stocks worth ₹3.54 lakh. Further investigation is under way, and action will be initiated against those responsible in accordance with the law, TG SAFE said. They further added that stocking APIs for sale without a valid drug licence is punishable under the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, with imprisonment of up to five years. TG SAFE’s Drugs Wing is responsible for issuing licences for the stocking and sale of APIs under the Act. d65c831667b2e00d.title: No prosecution for previously-enrolled voters filing Form 6: EC to SC
d65c831667b2e00d.summary: The Election Commission (EC) has told the Supreme Court that voters whose names are missing from draft electoral rolls despite having been enrolled earlier can apply afresh through Form 6 without the fear of prosecution. In an affidavit filed before the court, the poll panel said chief electoral officers have been requested to give wide publicity to the said clarification, in local languages as well. "It had been brought to the notice of the Commission that some apprehensions were expressed that applicants who were enrolled as voters in previous electoral roll(s) but whose names did not appear in the draft Electoral Roll during the SIR -- by filing Form 6, may face action for prosecution under Section 31 of the Representation of the People Act, 1950, on account of the fact that they were enrolled as voters in the previous electoral roll(s). "In order to allay such misapprehensions, the Commission ... has clarified that no prosecution will be launched against anyone for filing Form 6

1a8dffc89945a4da.title: Healthy habits, preventive care key to youth wellbeing, says surgeon
1a8dffc89945a4da.summary: Published - November 15, 2026 01:03 am IST - CHENNAI Cardiac surgeon, healthcare innovator and author Shriram Nene interacts with moderator Vasanthi Hariprakash during a session at the Next Gen Forum. | Photo Credit: Johan Sathya Das J Preventive healthcare and emotional wellbeing must become an integral part of nurturing the next generation, said cardiothoracic surgeon and healthcare innovator Shriram Nene at the NextGen Forum, a two-day conclave on youth safety and wellbeing, which concluded in Chennai on Saturday. Delivering the keynote address titled ‘Before They Become Patients: Why Wellbeing Must Begin Young’, Dr. Nene spoke about the importance of developing healthy habits and prioritising preventive healthcare from an early age. Drawing on his experience in healthcare and his recently released book, ‘21 Days to Good Health’, he highlighted the need to make everyday wellbeing a priority rather than focusing on healthcare only after the onset of illness. He also spoke about the role of emotional wellbeing in ensuring that young people grow up healthy. Organised by The Kindness Foundation on November 13 and 14, the forum brought together over 200 students aged 11 to 17 from more than 20 schools and over 25 experts from 15 sectors. The two-day event featured discussions on youth safety, mental health, digital risks, substance misuse and the challenges faced by young people. The insights from the conclave will contribute to a co-created White Paper on Youth Safety and Wellbeing, which will include young people’s perspectives and recommendations from experts for families, institutions and policymakers, said foundation founder and managing trustee Mahima Poddar. 72599b68cc6a8b03.title: TGPCB recommends closures, forfeitures over dusty construction
72599b68cc6a8b03.summary: Published - November 15, 2026 02:11 am IST The Telangana Pollution Control Board (TGPCB) has received several complaints regarding air pollution caused by dust emissions from construction projects in the Tellapur and Kollur areas of Sangareddy district. After receiving several complaints of air pollution due to construction, the Pollution Control Board (TGPCB) constituted Rolling Task Force Teams to these projects and assess compliance with environmental regulations and implementation of air pollution control measures. The team embarked on inspections and observed dust emissions from construction activity was aggravating air pollution. Several violations of environmental norms were also identified, the TGPCB stated. The Committee reviewed the environmental compliance of as many as 16 construction projects. After examining the severity of the violations, committee recommended the issuing of closure orders against projects where serious violations were identified, along with the forfeiture of bank guarantees. The committee also recommended forfeiture of bank guarantees in respect of projects where minor violations were observed. A period of 10 days was recommended for the concerned projects to rectify the violations. Three construction projects began construction activity without obtaining Consent for Establishment (CFE) from the Pollution Control Board, the TGPCB stated. The committee recommended the issuance of closure orders against these projects, it added. Two others were continuing construction activities in violation of the Orders for Suspension of Operations previously issued by the TGPCB, without obtaining permission from the Board for revocation of the suspension orders. A Ready Mix Concrete plant operating in association with another construction project was found to be functioning without obtaining Consent for Operation (CFO) from the TGPCB. fa9c0dcaf9fec7e4.title: Vaishnaw stresses need for India to make own semiconductor machinery
fa9c0dcaf9fec7e4.summary: Union Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw on Saturday stressed the need for India to make its own machinery and high-precision components for semiconductor production, as the Centre works to build a robust domestic ecosystem for the sector. Vaishnaw, Union Minister for Electronics and Information Technology, Information and Broadcasting, and Railways, made the remarks during a visit to the Ethereal Machines facility in Bengaluru, the PIB in Karnataka said in a post on X. He said the Centre, under Prime Minister Narendra Modi, was firmly committed to building a robust semiconductor ecosystem in the country. "In the spirit of 'Atmanirbhar Bharat', as envisioned by Prime Minister Narendra Modi, it is important that India develops and manufactures its own machines and high-precision components required for semiconductor manufacturing," he said. The Ethereal Machines facility was playing an important role in this direction by producing advanced machinery and high-precision components, he said.

ac44e8808ec5166e.summary: Published - November 15, 2026 12:22 am IST - CHENNAI AIADMK general secretary Edappadi K. Palaniswami. | Photo Credit: E. LAKSHMI NARAYANAN The AIADMK has announced a protest on November 18, demanding action over an alleged incident in which M. Ravisankar, the TVK MLA for Thuraiyur and Deputy Speaker of the Tamil Nadu Legislative Assembly, assaulted a social activist. In a statement, AIADMK general secretary Edappadi K. Palaniswami alleged that Karthik Kumar, a social activist who went to meet Mr. Ravisankar to submit grievances, was subjected to a “brutal attack” and “verbal abuse”. Mr. Palaniswami further claimed that after evidence of the assault surfaced, Mr. Ravisankar threatened the activist again and used a police officer to coerce the victim into posting on social media that the incident had never occurred. He remarked that this demonstrated how brazenly TVK legislators were engaging in hooliganism, which surpassed even what was depicted in films. Criticising Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay for remaining silent on the issue, Mr. Palaniswami announced that the AIADMK would stage a condemnation protest at 10 a.m. on Wednesday (November 18 near the Anna Statue at the Thuraiyur bus stand, demanding strict action against Mr. Ravisankar. 7e89d9cac50ff30d.title: DPIIT, commerce department authorised to issue defence industrial licences
7e89d9cac50ff30d.summary: The Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT) and Department of Commerce (DoC) are the competent authorities to issue industrial licences for defence purposes, the commerce and industry ministry said. According to an official communication from DPIIT, both departments can issue these licences under the Industries (Development and Regulation) Act, 1951. It stated that the industry department can issue licences for manufacturers located outside Special Economic Zones (SEZs), while the commerce department can issue licences for manufacturers located within these zones as well as for Export Oriented Units (EOUs). "It is reiterated that the following agencies (DPIIT and DoC) are competent to issue Industrial Licences for Defence purposes under the I (D&R) Act 1951, " DPIIT's press note said.

c2eea6fd68b63e51.title: Flood-prone areas to be monitored using drones in Chennai
c2eea6fd68b63e51.summary: Published - November 15, 2026 12:35 am IST - Chennai Residents in low-lying and flood-prone neighbourhoods across Chennai could be monitored more closely during the Northeast monsoon, with the Greater Chennai Corporation (GCC) planning to deploy drones across all 15 zones for 30 days, to help officials assess conditions on the ground. The initiative is intended to help civic officials keep track of vulnerable locations during periods of heavy rain and improve coordination of response measures. Aerial footage will allow officials to assess the situation in areas that may be difficult to monitor from the ground and identify locations requiring attention. Under the proposed arrangement, one drone and a trained operating team will be stationed in each of the city’s 15 zones, covering the northern, central, and southern regions. The teams will coordinate with zonal officials on the locations to be monitored and the timing of operations, according to officials. Live video feeds will be made available to designated GCC officials, while recorded footage will be handed over for subsequent assessment. The recordings will include details such as the date, time, zone, and location, wherever available. The footage is expected to support officials in assessing ground conditions in vulnerable neighbourhoods and in coordinating their response during the monsoon. The deployment will cover 30 days, with the operating teams required to follow the locations and priorities identified by GCC officials. c2eea6fd68b63e51.raw_facts: Published - November 15, 2026 12:35 am IST - Chennai Residents in low-lying and flood-prone neighbourhoods across Chennai could be monitored more closely during the Northeast monsoon, with the Greater Chennai Corporation (GCC) planning to deploy drones across all 15 zones for 30 days, to help officials assess conditions on the ground. The initiative is intended to help civic officials keep track of vulnerable locations during periods of heavy rain and improve coordination of response measures. Aerial footage will allow officials to assess the situation in areas that may be difficult to monitor from the ground and identify locations requiring attention. Under the proposed arrangement, one drone and a trained operating team will be stationed in each of the city’s 15 zones, covering the northern, central, and southern regions. The teams will coordinate with zonal officials on the locations to be monitored and the timing of operations, according to officials. Live video feeds will be made available to designated GCC officials, while recorded footage will be handed over for subsequent assessment. The recordings will include details such as the date, time, zone, and location, wherever available. The footage is expected to support officials in assessing ground conditions in vulnerable neighbourhoods and in coordinating their response during the monsoon. The deployment will cover 30 days, with the operating teams required to follow the locations and priorities identified by GCC officials. 10fdc4f1014ce468.title: VIT-A.P. researchers demonstrate low-cost photonic tech for non-invasive disease screening
10fdc4f1014ce468.summary: Published - November 14, 2026 11:45 pm IST - VIJAYAWADA Scientists from CATS Global (CASTLE Advanced Technologies and Systems), Nashik, Maharashtra, and VIT-A.P. University, Amaravati, Andhra Pradesh, have developed and demonstrated an innovative, low-cost optical sensing approach that could pave the way for affordable, non-invasive disease screening through breath analysis. According to a press release from the VIT-A.P., the research article titled ‘Photonic elastic-backscatter fingerprinting of exhaled-breath metabolites for non-invasive disease screening’, authored by professors Rao Tatavarti, Sridevi Nadimpalli and P. Arulmozhivarman Pachiyappan, was published on November 6, 2026, in the international journal Scientific Reports, published by Springer Nature. The study explores a photonic sensing technique that uses a simple, low-power laser and a position-sensitive optical detector to identify distinctive optical signatures associated with disease-related chemical compounds. According to the release, human breath contains hundreds of volatile organic compounds (VOCs) and other gases that can reflect changes in the body’s metabolic processes. Variations in the concentration of these compounds can be associated with different diseases, making breath analysis a promising approach for non-invasive health screening. However, conventional breath-analysis technologies often rely on sophisticated laboratory instruments, including mass spectrometers, gas chromatographs and advanced optical spectroscopy systems, which can be expensive and require specialised infrastructure. The study addresses this challenge, by demonstrating the potential of photonic elastic-backscatter fingerprinting to detect, distinguish and classify different disease-associated gas mixtures through subtle changes in the intensity and spatial position of scattered laser light. This approach offers a direction towards developing compact, cost-effective and potentially portable optical sensing systems,

9fad22104d19b253.title: Past weather trends show fewer cyclones crossing Tamil Nadu coast during Northeast monsoon
9fad22104d19b253.summary: Published - November 15, 2026 01:00 am IST - CHENNAI Senior meteorologists point out that only 22 of the 117 cyclonic systems that formed over the Bay of Bengal during October and November, between 1981 and 2025, made landfall along the State’s coast. | Photo Credit: VELANKANNI RAJ B Tamil Nadu has seen relatively fewer cyclonic systems crossing its coast during the Northeast monsoon in the past 45 years, noted meteorologists. The Bay of Bengal is churning its next cyclone for the season. However, the current predictions indicate the possibility of only less rainfall over the State. Senior meteorologists point out that only 22 of the 117 cyclonic systems that formed over the Bay of Bengal during October and November, between 1981 and 2025, made landfall along the State’s coast. Many of the systems moved northwards towards places such as Andhra Pradesh, Odisha, West Bengal, Bangladesh and the Arakan coast, while others weakened over the sea without crossing any coast. Y.E.A. Raj, former deputy director general of meteorology, Regional Meteorological Centre, Chennai, said 68 of the 117 systems moved north of Tamil Nadu towards the neighbouring States or countries, while 26 dissipated over the Bay of Bengal without making landfall. However, the State has received rainfall during some past years when the system dissipated over the sea. Citing IMD data, he said of the three to four weather systems or cyclones that generally form over the Bay of Bengal between October and December, only one comes closer to or crosses the Tamil Nadu coast. Going by statistics since 1981, Tamil Nadu experiences a coastal crossing roughly once every two years during October and November. The occurrence of three weather systems moving north of Tamil Nadu during October and November is not unprecedented. A similar pattern was recorded in 10 previous years, including 1983, 1996, 2010 and 2013, Mr. Raj added. Published - November 15, 2026 01:00 am IST Terms & conditions | Institutional Subscribe

European Council President Antonio Costa said the continent would be represented by the EU and five members of the "coalition of the willing" that backs Ukraine: the UK, France, Germany, Italy and Poland. 095d608f305cb939.title: Tamil Nadu unlikely to see significant impact of severe cyclonic storm brewing over Bay of Bengal
095d608f305cb939.summary: Published - November 15, 2026 12:46 am IST - CHENNAI The current weather predictions indicate that the well marked is expected to gain strength as a cyclonic storm and intensify further as a severe cyclonic storm. | Photo Credit: VELANKANNI RAJ B The weather system brewing over the Bay of Bengal is likely to intensify into a severe cyclonic storm by November 18. However, Tamil Nadu may remain largely on the fringes of its impact, according to the Regional Meteorological Centre (RMC). The season’s third cyclone is also likely to bypass Tamil Nadu and impact coastal Andhra Pradesh and Odisha. The current weather predictions indicate that the well marked low-pressure area over southeast Bay of Bengal is expected to gain strength as a cyclonic storm over the central parts of south and adjoining westcentral Bay of Bengal around November 16 evening. It is likely to further intensify into a severe cyclonic storm by November 18. While the weather agency is likely to provide clarity on the system’s movement and likely landfall location only after it consolidates into a depression, heavy rainfall warnings has been largely issued for other States, including Andaman and Nicobar islands, coastal Andhra Pradesh and Odisha, till November 20. The cyclone is likely to be named ‘Akvan’, suggested by Iran under the naming list of tropical cyclones over North Indian Ocean. Officials of the RMC said the possibility of heavy rainfall in Tamil Nadu remained low, given the system’s current position and expected trajectory. Rainfall of light to moderate intensity is likely to be concentrated over the southern and Western Ghats districts till November 20. V.R. Durai, Head, Regional Weather Forecasting Centre, RMC, said there was currently no indication of heavy rainfall over the State. Winds from Arabian sea and a minor system over south Tamil Nadu would trigger rainfall over the southern and Western Ghats districts. 2fad31e5af7a83b6.title: Trai bars 124,000 mobile connections in spam crackdown during July-Sep
2fad31e5af7a83b6.summary: Regulator TRAI took enforcement action against more than 1.24 lakh telecom resources and blacklisted 374 entities for one year for violating unsolicited commercial communication (UCC) norms during July-September, as it stepped up efforts to curb spam calls and messages. A total of 1,10,325 telecom resources, including mobile numbers, were barred from outgoing services for 15 days for the first violation, while 13,777 were disconnected for one year for repeat violations, according to TRAI's quarterly report for the second quarter of 2026-27. The regulator also blocked 3,725 SMS headers and blacklisted 374 senders for one year, during which they cannot obtain fresh telecom resources. TRAI received 15.29 lakh complaints of unsolicited commercial communications during the quarter, of which 7.23 lakh were classified as actionable. 71a15cd13e307813.title: Congress wants to contest 181 seats in 2027 UP polls, indicates Akhilesh
71a15cd13e307813.summary: Samajwadi Party (SP) chief Akhilesh Yadav indicated on Saturday that the Congress has expressed its wish to contest 181 seats in the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly polls, while asserting that the INDIA bloc would remain united to defeat the ruling BJP in the state. Asked at the Hindustan Times Leadership Summit in Delhi whether the Congress is seeking to contest 100 seats, Yadav said the party has demanded more than that. 048d7da609aa1a98.title: Listing may change 'Tata way', put profits ahead of philanthropy: Noel
048d7da609aa1a98.summary: Tata Trusts Chairman Noel Tata on Saturday said that listing Tata Sons will "fundamentally change" the over 150-year-old group's way of working and stressed that its largest owner will play a "constructive role" in engaging with the regulators to retain the conglomerate's unlisted character. Speaking at the Hindustan Times Leadership Summit here, Noel said while "some people" are proposing a listing for the group's holding company, he fears that enlarging the number of shareholders after a listing will shift its focus to profits from philanthropy. "My worry is that listing, which is what some people are proposing, will change the Tata way. And one day, if we have 30,000-40,000 shareholders, profit may take precedence over philanthropy. And I think that will fundamentally change the Tata way of working," Noel, who turned 70 on Friday, was quoted as saying. "Tata Trusts will play a constructive role with regulators and others to try and find a solution which keeps the Tata way the way

The fast services will stop at only five stations -- Sarai Kale Khan, Anand Vihar, Ghaziabad, Begumpul and Modipuram -- to reduce travel time for commuters, particularly office-goers and students travelling during rush hours, it said. Additional Divisional Railway Manager (ADRM-Infrastructure) P. E. Edwin and Central Bank of India, Hyderabad Region, General Manager M. Pichai signed the MoU on Friday, aimed at providing enhanced financial and banking facilities to the employees. As per the MoU, railway employees are eligible for salary accounts with zero balance, personal accident and term insurance coverage up to ₹1.5 crore and other benefits. SCoR Vijayawada Division Senior Personal Officer Prem Kumar Lakhawat, bank Vijayawada regional head E. Venkateswara Rao, Guntur regional head G. V. Ramana Rao and other officials were present. 68b71d3440fb4120.title: M.P. CM announces crop loss survey, financial aid for farmers in rain deficit Alirajpur district
68b71d3440fb4120.summary: Published - November 16, 2026 01:21 am IST - Bhopal Madhya Pradesh Chief Minister Mohan Yadav on Sunday announced a crop loss survey in Alirajpur to provide financial assistance to the farmers in the State’s worst rain-deficit district. Addressing a Janjatiya Gaurav Diwas programme, marking the birth anniversary of tribal icon Birsa Munda, in Jhobat, the CM announced he was issuing instructions to the District Collector to begin the survey and provide aid to farmers affected by rain deficiency. “I am issuing directions to the Collector to conduct a survey and help them as per the Revenue Book Circular (RBC) 6-4. You will get money in your accounts from the government,” he said. At least 11 districts of Madhya Pradesh have experienced severe rainfall deficit, with those in the Nimar and Malwa regions being the worst hit. It severely impacted kharif crops like soybean. Alirajpur, that falls under the Nimar region, recorded nearly 52% lower rainfall than normal. The government, though, has not announced such surveys in other affected districts, even as officials claim that discussions on relief measures are going on. Earlier in the day, Chief Minister and Governor Mangubhai Patel inaugurated ₹1,353.18 crore Dahi Micro Lift Irrigation Project in Dhar’s Dahi, which aims to provide irrigation through Narmada water to 47,000 hectares of agricultural land across 84 villages in Dhar and and 42 in Alirajpur districts. According to government officials, about a lakh farmers are likely to benefit directly from the project’s permanent irrigation facility. Last month, Mr. Yadav had launched another micro-lift irrigation project worth around ₹2,400-crore in Dhar’s Sardarpur. 3f12a661b2bffce7.title: Govt health spending triples, household burden eases
3f12a661b2bffce7.summary: New Delhi: India's government health spending nearly tripled over a decade, while households' share of the country's total healthcare bill fell sharply, pointing to a gradual shift away from out-of-pocket financing towards public funding. The share of healthcare expenditure borne by households declined to 42.7% in 2023-24 from 64.2% in 2013–14, according to the National Health Accounts (NHA) estimates released by the Union health ministry on Sunday. “The simultaneous increase in public healthcare financing and decline in the proportion of spending borne directly by households reflects India's progress towards a more accessible, affordable and financially protective healthcare system,” the ministry said in a release. Government health expenditure rose to ₹ 4.14 trillion in 2023-24 from ₹ 1.30 trillion in 2013-14. Its share of total health expenditure increased by 14.9 percentage points over the period, while per capita public health spending rose 2.8 times, from ₹ 1,042 to ₹ 2,959. “The most important development is the changing balance between public and household contributions to healthcare expenditure. A larger share of total healthcare spending is now being financed through government resources, while a considerably smaller share is being borne directly by households,” the ministry said. Primary healthcare received ₹ 1.53 trillion in government funding, supporting the rollout of Ayushman Arogya Mandirs. These centres offer preventive care, screening for non-communicable diseases , medicines and diagnostic tests at the community level. Financial protection through health coverage schemes also expanded. Social security expenditure on health, which includes government-funded insurance programmes such as Ayushman Bharat-Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (AB PM-JAY), state health insurance schemes, social health insurance and medical reimbursements for government employees, rose from 6% of total health expenditure in 2013–14 to 11% in 2023–24. 1f988140e5391ad1.title: Chhath Puja: Despite politics over Yamuna, Delhi stretch of river continues to be polluted
1f988140e5391ad1.summary: Published - November 16, 2026 02:22 am IST - New Delhi Devotees gather along the banks of the Yamuna, polluted with toxic foam, during the Chhath Puja festival in Noida on Sunday. | Photo Credit: PTI Despite the political slugfest over the Yamuna during yet another Chhath Puja, official data show that the river’s Delhi stretch remains heavily polluted for most of the year, with water quality improving during the monsoon, when floodwaters flush out pollutants. According to official data, the faecal coliform level (microbes from human and animal excreta) in the Yamuna at Asgarpur, where the river leaves the Capital, was 660 times the Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) desirable limit for bathing water quality in May, before the monsoon. The water quality improved in September, as it does every year after the monsoon. The Delhi government has yet to make the October data public. The Yamuna holds religious significance for people from Purvanchal (residents of eastern Uttar Pradesh and Bihar), who constitute a significant voter base in Delhi. Many observe Chhath Puja by taking a dip in the river. 6f3a68895a1f4b6e.summary: Foreign investors made a strong comeback to Indian equities in the first fortnight of November, pumping in Rs 84,290 crore after two consecutive months of net outflows, amid a global AI sell-off, falling crude prices and attractive large-cap valuations. The latest inflows follow net withdrawals of Rs 34,843 crore in October and Rs 35,861 crore in September, according to data from the depositories. According to the data, Foreign Portfolio Investors (FPIs) made a net investment of Rs 84,290 crore in Indian equities during November 2-13, covering nine trading sessions. With the latest inflows, cumulative FPI outflows from Indian equities have narrowed to around Rs 2.1 lakh crore in 2026 from nearly Rs 3 lakh crore a few weeks ago. d96f950228b38b31.title: Hyderabad hospital performs combined heart valve procedures in single sitting
d96f950228b38b31.summary: Published - November 16, 2026 12:29 am IST - HYDERABAD Doctors at Apollo Hospitals in Hyderabad performed Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation (TAVI) and Balloon Mitral Valvotomy (BMV) on an 83-year-old man in a single sitting on Saturday. The procedure was performed by cardiologists P.C. Rath and Manoj Kumar Agarwala during the Hyderabad Valve Meeting. The patient, who had previously undergone coronary artery bypass surgery and pacemaker implantation, was admitted with severe aortic and mitral valve stenosis. Doctors opted for a minimally invasive intervention involving the replacement of the aortic valve and balloon dilatation of the mitral valve. Both procedures were successfully performed through the femoral artery, accessed through the groin, under anaesthesia. The intervention was also demonstrated live during the Hyderabad Valve Meeting. Hyderabad is hosting leading interventional cardiologists and structural heart specialists from all over the world for Hyderabad Valves 2026, the fourth edition of a biennial scientific meeting focused on modern, minimally invasive treatments for heart valve disease. The meeting brought together Indian and international experts for live case demonstrations, specialist lectures and interactive discussions on complex valve and structural heart interventions. The conference features 26 live transcatheter cases from centres in India and overseas. The programme includes 11 live-case transmissions from leading international centres, including four from the USA, and six each from Europe and Apollo Hospitals, Jubilee Hills. Each demonstration provides an opportunity for specialists to discuss clinical decisions, procedural techniques and patient safety. 1039e25b926f94fb.raw_facts: Published - November 16, 2026 12:40 am IST - Chennai PMK president Anbumani Ramadoss on Sunday demanded that the monthly hike of ₹5,000 announced by the State government for guest lecturers, which would increase their salary from ₹30,000 to ₹35,000, be provided from September 1 instead of November 1. “Higher Education Minister Viswanathan assured [the Assembly] that the salary hike would be implemented retrospectively from September. It is unjustifiable that guest lecturers are being let down despite this assurance. At a time when guest lecturers are being paid very low salaries, delaying even this modest hike is an injustice to them,” he said. He also urged the government to increase their salary to ₹50,000 next year, in keeping with the recommendations of the University Grants Commission. “The Tamil Nadu government must also promptly fulfil all their other demands, including PF benefits, medical insurance, maternity leave for women guest lecturers, and a gratuity of ₹25 lakh upon retirement,” he said. Protesting workers gathered in Gazipur's Konabari and Mouchak areas, prompting police to use tear gas and sound grenades to disperse them. Factory owners said 50 units in the industrial zone were closed. The latest disruption comes amid weeks of protests over workers' demand to raise the minimum monthly wage from 12,500 taka (USD 100) to 30,000 taka (USD 240), with demonstrations and factory shutdowns reported across key industrial belts. Bangladesh is the world's second-largest garment exporter after China. The sector employs more than four million workers and accounts for over 80 per cent of the country's export earnings, making prolonged disruption a concern for international buyers and global supply chains. Vaishali needing to outscore both Vachier-Lagrave and Hans Niemann to stay in the title race at the Total Chess World Championship Tour Pilot in Budapest. Only the four group winners advance to the championship bracket. Arjun began the day three points behind Vachier-Lagrave. He drew their first game with black, then won the return with white. Niemann beat Bibisara Assaubayeva before the Kazakh held him to a 96-move draw, leaving all three leaders on 13 points. Including other income, the total consolidated income reached Rs 165.89 crore. The company's expenses during the half-year rose 35.79 per cent to Rs 155.67 crore, up from Rs 114.64 crore in the preceding six months, weighing on bottom-line growth. 527deebf21524cf2.title: India votes against UNGA resolution seeking moratorium on death penalty
527deebf21524cf2.summary: India has voted against a draft UN General Assembly resolution calling on nations to establish a moratorium on the death penalty. The 193-member UNGA adopted by recorded vote the resolution on Friday introduced by Mexico on 'Moratorium on the use of the death penalty', with 133 countries voting in favour of the resolution, 33 against and 16 abstentions. India, along with Bahrain, China, Egypt, Iran, Iraq, Japan, Kuwait, Maldives, Oman, Pakistan, Qatar, Saudi Arabia and the US, voted against the resolution. The resolution expressed deep concern about the continued application of the death penalty and reaffirmed the right of all countries to develop their own legal systems, including determining appropriate legal penalties in accordance with international law. It called upon all States to establish a moratorium on executions, with a view to abolishing the death penalty. It also called upon States which have abolished the death penalty not to reintroduce it. The resolution expressed

ff8f787b604d35c8.title: A hundred years ago | Bombay diamond mills
ff8f787b604d35c8.summary: Published - November 16, 2026 01:53 am IST Bombay, Nov. 15: The Diamond Mill, which was purchased some time ago for the Japanese Syndicate, will be run under the name of Toyo Podar Mills. After the machinery has been thoroughly overhauled and brought up to date, technical management and the business will be entirely under Japanese supervision. This is the first time that the Japanese have actually entered into the cotton textile manufacturing industry in India. Negotiations which were proceeding last month between a Japanese Syndicate and a local house of Mill Managing Agents for the purchase of a group of textile mills by the former have fallen through as the Japanese did not agree to pay the price demanded. 5d58a040bd292fc2.title: Couple from Tumakuru end their lives in Udupi district
5d58a040bd292fc2.summary: Published - November 15, 2026 10:44 pm IST - MANGALURU A 52-year-old man and his 48-year-old wife ended their lives by jumping off a bridge across the Seeta River, in Mabukala, Udupi district, on Saturday night, the Udupi district police said. The police said the deceased have been identified as as H. Srinivas Murthy and Ganga. According to the police, the couple were on a visit to pilgrimage places in the Karavali and Malnad regions. After visiting Murudeshwar in Uttara Kannada district, the couple came to Mabukala on Saturday evening. An autorickshaw driver saw the couple jump off the bridge after walking a few metres. He immediately called the police and reported the incident. The police carried out a search operation in association with firemen and local swimmers on Sunday morning. The bodies of the couple were found about 500 metres down the bridge. The reason for their decision to end their lives was unknown. A case has been registered at the Kota Police Station, and the bodies have been kept in a mortuary at the Government Hospital in Kundapur. The police were waiting for the family members of the deceased couple to arrive to continue their investigation. 073cb5355e462578.title: Sabarimala sets target of 75 pilgrims a minute on holy steps
073cb5355e462578.summary: Updated - November 15, 2026 07:30 pm IST As many as 75 pilgrims are expected to climb the 18 holy steps to the Sabarimala shrine every minute under a new crowd management target set by the authorities for the annual pilgrimage season, which kicks off on Tuesday. Devaswom Minister K. Muraleedharan said the police had been given necessary directions to achieve the target. Senior police officers were also reviewing the arrangements on the instructions of the Home Minister. The Minister also sought to dismiss concerns over the availability of appam and aravana during the season. He said his visit to the production centre had convinced him of the efforts being made by employees to ensure uninterrupted production by working round the clock.”The Devaswom Board had assured us that the pilgrimage season could be completed smoothly if 75 lakh tins of aravana were made available,” he said. He also assured that the State government would release the first instalment of payments due to local self-government bodies for setting up facilities for pilgrims within a couple of days. Instructions had also been issued to ensure adequate stocks of medicines at healthcare centres. All government departments involved in the pilgrimage arrangements were working in coordination to discharge their responsibilities, he said. Preparations for next year’s pilgrimage season would begin as soon as the current season concluded. The government had decided to launch infrastructure development works for the next season as early as February, after the temple closes following the pilgrimage season, the Minister added. 519bf9abeba60aa0.title: SpaceX makes first launch pad catch of Starship after its orbital return
519bf9abeba60aa0.summary: SpaceX's Starship made a triumphant return to Earth on Saturday, caught in midair by giant mechanical arms where its journey began 22 hours earlier. It was the grand finale that Elon Musk and his team hoped for - the first-ever capture of a Starship flying back from space. But with the first-stage booster exploding shortly after Friday's liftoff from Texas, the company fell short of its desired double catch. Wreckage remained in the Gulf of Mexico, cordoned off by buoys, as the stainless steel, bullet-shaped spacecraft lowered itself upright at the launch pad. The dramatic, sci-fi-like capture helped blot out the booster's messy miss. "Can you believe it?" shouted SpaceX commentator Dan Huot. SpaceX officials said Saturday's catch demonstrates the full reusability of Starship, intended for moon and Mars travel. Although Friday's booster recovery failed, the company had already made three previous booster catches, validating the technique. NASA welcomed Saturday's news. The space

97a374f93eb9025b.summary: Businesses adopting artificial intelligence (AI) should start with a measurable goal and judge success by the improvement it delivers rather than the number of AI agents deployed, as the technology moves from helping employees to doing work for them, a senior Oracle executive said. "It's important to remember that the number of agents deployed matters less than the improvement they deliver," Natalia Rachelson, Senior Vice President, Applications Development at Oracle, told PTI. Business leaders should pick an outcome they can measure, such as reducing the time spent resolving accounting errors or lowering transport costs, she said. "It's important to establish a baseline first so you can assess whether AI is making a meaningful difference," she noted. Companies then need to get the basics right: reliable data, clear ownership of processes, appropriate controls, and employees who understand how to work with AI agents. 8b1d0797e60f2388.summary: Exposure to extreme heat during pregnancy can lead to severe outcomes, including preterm birth, stillbirth and congenital abnormalities in newborns, prompting experts at the United Nations Climate Change Conference (COP31) to highlight maternal health risks and call for targeted adaptation strategies. The issue comes into focus as countries at COP31 prepare to discuss progress towards the Global Goal on Adaptation, a framework to help nations develop key adaptation measures, including those needed to address the health impacts of climate change. However, translating growing recognition of climate-related health risks into action remains a challenge, particularly in the absence of adequate financial support. According to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC), only about one per cent of formal climate finance under its financial mechanism is currently directed towards health. The broader issue of adaptation finance for developing nations is also expected

The camp provided medical services, including consultations, medicines, guidance to patients suffering from diabetes, hypertension, epilepsy and paralysis at a minimal consultation fee. A medical team from HCG Cancer Hospital also conducted free cancer screening tests for patients at the camp. 311ec4d9593f0875.title: CIAL sets up facilitation centre for Sabarimala pilgrims
311ec4d9593f0875.summary: Updated - November 15, 2026 06:50 pm IST - KOCHI Cochin International Airport Limited (CIAL) has set up a dedicated pilgrim facilitation centre at the airport for Sabarimala pilgrims. Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan will inaugurate the centre on November 17. Spread across 5,000 sq. ft., the centre is located near the police aid post, adjacent to the domestic arrival terminal and will remain open round the clock. KSRTC bus services are available to and from the airport from here, with a booking counter set up at the centre. Pilgrims can also book chartered bus services on demand. A dedicated counter for helicopter service bookings has also been arranged. The other facilities at the centre include a Devaswom help desk, prasadam coupon counter, prepaid taxi booking facility, vegetarian food outlet, and a rest area. A flight information display system has also been installed to provide real-time flight updates. Its proximity to the domestic terminal makes the centre easily accessible to pilgrims, says an official release. Around 11,000 pilgrims made use of the facilitation centre last year, including those from Tamil Nadu, Telangana, Andhra Pradesh, Malaysia, and Singapore, it says. d321864c04d665c0.summary: Published - November 15, 2026 11:26 pm IST - VISAKHAPATNAM To mark the sixth anniversary of the Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan (NMBA), Visakha Steel General Hospital (VSGH) of Rashtriya Ispat Nigam Limited (RINL), in association with Ukkunagaram Brahma Kumaris, organised a drug de-addiction awareness programme at the Learning and Development Centre auditorium in Ukkunagaram, according to a release in Visakhapatnam on Sunday. Speaking as chief guest, RINL Director (Commercial) G.V.N. Prasad underscored the organisation’s commitment to employee well-being. Describing substance abuse as a critical public health challenge, he stressed the need for timely medical intervention, counselling, and rehabilitation alongside collective community support. Guest speaker B.K.K. Yashwanth, Associate Professor of General Surgery at NRIIMS, detailed the physiological and psychological impacts of prolonged substance dependence on vital organs, highlighting lifestyle modifications and sustained support for recovery. The event featured a guided Raja Yoga meditation session by Ukkunagaram Brahma Kumaris focusing on mindfulness and mental resilience, an interactive Q&A on relapse prevention, and the administration of the NMBA pledge. 8f9e5dc91f822f2a.title: Depression over Bay of Bengal to turn into severe cyclonic storm by Nov 17
8f9e5dc91f822f2a.summary: A depression over the southeast and adjoining southwest Bay of Bengal is likely to strengthen into a severe cyclonic storm by November 17, the meteorological department said on Sunday. Rains are expected to occur in north coastal districts in Tamil Nadu, Puducherry and Karaikal area, it said. According to the latest weather report, Saturday's well marked low pressure area over the southeast Bay of Bengal moved northwestward, intensified into a depression and lay centred at 5.30 am today. It is very likely to continue to move northwestward, intensify further into a cyclonic storm over the central parts of south and adjoining west central Bay of Bengal on November, 16 and into a severe cyclonic storm on November 17. The data further added that in addition to northern Tamil Nadu districts, moderate rain at isolated places is likely to occur over western ghat and southern districts of the state from Monday. According to the bulletin, during the last 24 hours ending at 8.30 am on Sunday

6879830d61ccf3b9.summary: Dr Reddy's Laboratories has said the US health regulator classified the inspection outcome of its formulations manufacturing facility here as 'Voluntary Action Indicated (VAI)' and officially closed the inspection. In a regulatory filing on Saturday, the company said the Good Manufacturing Practices (GMP) inspection was conducted by the USFDA at its formulations manufacturing facility (FTO-3) in Bachupally, Hyderabad. The company had earlier informed the stock exchanges regarding the inspection on August 14, 2026. "We wish to inform you that the United States Food and Drug Administration (USFDA) has classified the inspection outcome as 'Voluntary Action Indicated (VAI)' and concluded that the inspection is officially closed under 21 CFR 20.64(d)(3)," Dr Reddy's said in the filing.

More than 11,000 cases have been recorded, and nearly half of those infected have died, according to government data. It is the deadliest of Congo's 17 outbreaks and is on track to surpass the death toll from the West African outbreak that killed 11,000 people between 2014 and 2016. Basic containment measures, including contact tracing and isolation, remain inadequate, raising doubts about authorities' ability to halt the outbreak. Experts say there is little chance of bringing it under control within the next year. 9fd615d49438ee16.title: Guest teachers in Haryana hold mock Assembly, demand regularisation
9fd615d49438ee16.summary: Updated - November 16, 2026 01:21 am IST - GURUGRAM Guest teachers in Haryana schools held a mock Assembly at the Mini Secretariat in Kurukshetra on Saturday, demanding regularisation under the three-year policy notified in 2014 in accordance with court orders. Organised on the call of the Rajkiya Anubandhit Adhyapak Sangh, the symbolic Assembly passed a resolution seeking regularisation of guest teachers by an overwhelming majority. The resolution will be submitted to Chief Minister Nayab Singh Saini at his camp office in Kurukshetra on November 29. The teachers will also hold a rally in Delhi on December 12 and submit the resolution to the President. Teachers said guest teachers had been serving in government schools for the past 21 years and contributing to the State’s education system, but the government continued to keep them in temporary employment arrangements instead of regularising their services. Following the court orders, the Haryana School Education Department issued speaking orders denying regular status to the guest teachers. They said the mock Assembly was organised to raise questions concerning the regularisation of guest teachers, judicial decisions and the government’s accountability on a public platform. The event was attended by educationists, intellectuals, employee union leaders from various departments, School Management Committee representatives, the Samyukt Kisan Morcha, student and youth organisations, advocates’ unions, writers’ associations, university professors, the Jan Sangharsh Manch, Kurukshetra, and social activists. These teachers, appointed between 2005 and 2008, are working as junior basic teachers, trained graduate teachers, and post graduate teachers. Addressing the media in Tirunelveli, he criticised Karnataka Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar for speaking arrogantly about going ahead with the project without respecting the law. He further urged Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay to remain vigilant on the issue. “The MDMK would announce its stand on the Mekedatu issue at its executive committee meeting scheduled to be held in Tenkasi,” he said. He alleged that corruption was rampant during both the previous AIADMK government led by Edappadi K Palaniswami and DMK government led by M.K. Stalin. Claiming that commissions had been fixed at specific percentages in various departments, he said that even teachers and nurses had to pay bribes amounting to several thousand rupees to secure transfers. However, the present government led by Mr. Vijay follows a policy of integrity, he noted. Drawing a parallel with the burning of the Jaffna Public Library in Sri Lanka by Sinhalese rioters, Mr. Vaiko alleged that irregularities and corruption had taken place at Periyar Arivulagam in Coimbatore. He said that the previous DMK government led by M.K. Stalin should take responsibility for the alleged irregularities, describing the incident as a major attack on the world of knowledge and learning. He demanded that a committee be constituted to investigate the matter and stringent punishment be imposed on everyone found responsible. He further expressed confidence that the alliance led by Chief Minister Joseph Vijay would register a landslide victory in the upcoming by-elections as well as the next assembly elections. 8b7759995151af33.title: ONGC takes over disputed Cambay block from Vedanta after court ruling
8b7759995151af33.summary: State-run Oil and Natural Gas Corporation (ONGC) has taken over operations and control of the disputed Cambay offshore block from Vedanta Oil & Gas Ltd following a Delhi High Court ruling, according to regulatory filings by the two companies. Vedanta Oil & Gas Ltd has recognised an impairment charge of about Rs 379 crore against assets and receivables linked to the block. The takeover of the CB-OS-02 block took effect on July 22, 2026, after the High Court's single-judge bench dismissed Vedanta's challenge to the government's decision not to extend the production-sharing contract, ONGC said in its quarterly filing. The block was operated by Vedanta, which held a 40 per cent participating interest; ONGC held 50 per cent, and Invenire Petrodyne Ltd had the remaining 10 per cent. a584679803420064.title: India's investments in US treasuries up $38.4 billion in June-August
a584679803420064.summary: India's investment in US Treasury securities increased USD 38.4 billion, or 21 per cent, between June and August, coinciding with substantial inflows of Foreign Currency Non-Resident (FCNR) (B) deposits into the Indian banking system. According to data compiled by PTI from the US Department of the Treasury, India's investment in US Treasuries rose to USD 219.7 billion in August 2026 from USD 181.3 billion in May 2026, just before the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) introduced the concessional facility. Gaura Sengupta, economist at IDFC First Bank, said the RBI's foreign exchange reserves increased during the period of FCNR(B) inflows, with a portion of the accretion being invested in US Treasury securities. The RBI had introduced a special USD-INR swap facility on June 8, 2026, to encourage foreign currency inflows and strengthen the country's balance of payments position. c3f7b46e93311ce8.summary: India's edible oil imports rose 6 per cent to 16.92 million tonnes in the oil year ended October 2026, and the import bill jumped 24 per cent to about Rs 200,000 crore, the Solvent Extractors' Association of India (SEA) said on Monday. Edible oil imports in the 2025-26 oil year (November-October) increased compared with 16.01 million tonnes a year earlier, when the bill was about Rs 161,126 crore, the trade body said in a statement. Total vegetable oil imports, including non-edible oils, rose 5 per cent to 17.24 million tonnes from 16.36 million tonnes. India imports edible oils to bridge the gap between domestic supply and demand, a practice that began in the 1990s. Over the past 20 years, import volumes have risen 2.8 times, while the cost has risen nearly 15 times, SEA said. Refined oil imports fell sharply to 0.82 million tonnes in 2025-26 from 1.74 million tonnes a year earlier, SEA said. 75bdaab340e1ba4a.summary: As the National Capital Region (NCR) and surrounding areas have been blanketed in toxic smog, demand for air purifiers has also risen sharply. A post-Diwali surge in demand for air purifiers, once seen as a recurring trend, is now part of a broader shift in consumer behaviour. The Tata Group entity, which operates the consumer electronics and durables retail chain Croma, said air purifier volumes have more than doubled in 2026. "North India, particularly Delhi-NCR, remains the strongest market, while Mumbai also sees an uptick during periods of poor air quality," CEO and MD Shibashish Roy was quoted as saying by news agency PTI. Amazon has also witnessed a sharp rise in demand, with air purifier sales on its platform doubling over the past week. "Air purifier sales on Amazon.in have doubled in the last week," said a company spokesperson, adding that consumers are increasingly exploring different models based on room size, filter types and features such as live AQI sensors through its AI-based shopping assistant. The Chamber of Trade and Industry (CTI) has written to Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman, seeking a reduction in the Goods and Services Tax (GST) on air purifiers, calling them "as essential as medicines", according to an Indian Express report. “With Delhi’s Air Quality Index (AQI) crossing 400, doctors have warned that breathing the polluted air is equivalent to smoking 20-25 cigarettes a day. fe34f8644c0dee12.title: Sebi may propose raising FPI beneficial ownership threshold to 25%
fe34f8644c0dee12.summary: Market regulator Sebi may propose raising the beneficial ownership identification threshold for foreign portfolio investors to 25 per cent from the current 10 per cent to ease compliance requirements and align India's regulatory framework with international best practices, an official said. The regulator is examining several areas where Indian regulations may be unnecessarily intrusive, adding to compliance costs and making the country's markets less attractive. "The regulator will soon issue another consultation paper outlining identified measures to simplify the compliance framework," he added. Citing international benchmarking, the official said several developed and emerging jurisdictions follow a 25 per cent threshold for identifying beneficial ownership. He said changes to certain provisions under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA) and its rules would require government intervention, while Sebi could take up other measures through its consultation process. In 2023

The United Forum of IDBI Officers and Employees (UFIOE), comprising the All India IDBI Officers' Association (AIIDBIOA) and the All India Industrial Development Bank Employees' Association (AIIDBEA), called the strike. Earlier this month, the UFIOE had gone on a two-day nationwide strike to oppose the proposed sale of a majority stake to Fairfax. In a strike notice served on IDBI Bank MD and CEO, the UFIOE said the strike would be observed across all branches and offices of the bank nationwide. The unions have demanded that the government and LIC stop the proposed sale of IDBI Bank to Fairfax Financial Holdings, describing the bank as a national asset. c347fb3e4c447c3d.title: FinMin examining suggestions for changes in equity capital gains tax: CBDT
c347fb3e4c447c3d.summary: The Finance Ministry is examining various aspects of capital gains tax on equities, and probable changes in taxation would come in the Union Budget for 2027-28, a senior official said on Monday. Central Board of Direct Taxes (CBDT) Chairman Ravi Agrawal said the ministry is considering suggestions from various stakeholders made during the pre-budget meetings. "We will consider it, and I'm sure on February 1 you will get to know. Analysis is being done of whatever issues have been flagged or points that have been raised by the stakeholders," Agrawal told reporters on the sidelines of the inauguration of a CBDT lounge at the IITF here. Agrawal said the different facets of the capital gains tax regime, including tax implications, will be examined, and the decision will be announced in the Budget. Industry chambers have already made representations to the Ministry recommending abolition of Long Term Capital Gains tax (LTCG). They also suggested rationalising short-term capital gains .

59377c3dc3ee9694.title: Chennai Corporation opens free public toilets at 853 locations
59377c3dc3ee9694.summary: Published - November 17, 2026 12:25 am IST - Chennai The Greater Chennai Corporation (GCC) has completed and opened free public toilets at 853 locations across Chennai, providing 7,644 seats, against its target of 10,444 at 1,479 locations. Work is under way at 193 locations, accounting for 1,270 seats, while steps have been initiated to establish facilities at another 433 locations with 1,530 seats, according to a press release issued on November 15. The figures leave 626 locations, with a total of 2,800 seats, yet to be completed under the scheme. Of these, facilities at 193 locations are under construction. The latest figures were released after GCC Commissioner G.S. Sameeran inspected a free public toilet at Anna Nagar Tower Park on Sunday. He interacted with members of the public to enquire about the use and maintenance of the facility. The GCC said the toilets were being designed to provide safe access for senior citizens, persons with disabilities, children, and transgender persons. Each facility has a worker appointed for cleaning and maintenance. Workers are provided with gloves, masks, and footwear, besides training in safety protocols, handling chemicals, and personal hygiene. A QR code facility has also been provided at the toilets for users to submit feedback and complaints. The complaints are monitored and addressed within a specified timeframe, with updates on their status sent to users, the release said. In February, the GCC held community consultation meetings at 437 locations where free public toilets had been established. The meetings, held across all 15 zones under the campaign ‘Our toilet, our responsibility’, covered issues such as cleanliness, maintenance, accessibility, water quality, and public safety. The February release did not specify the total number of toilet seats in operation. The GCC said it would consider establishing more toilets at its parks and burial grounds based on public demand. Published - November 17, 2026 12:25 am IST Ter

3cc95212521891fe.title: India’s unemployment rate dips to 4.9% in October on urban recovery
3cc95212521891fe.summary: New Delhi: India’s unemployment rate for those aged 15 years and above fell marginally to 4.9% in October from 5% in September as joblessness fell in urban areas but remained steady in rural centres, according to the latest Periodic Labour Force Survey Monthly Bulletin (PLFS-M) released by the statistics ministry on Monday. The unemployment rate in urban areas fell to 6.7% in October from 6.9% the previous month, driven primarily by a sharp fall in unemployment rate among urban women – from 9.2% in September to 8.7% in October. The unemployment rate , however, remained steady at 6% among urban men. The unemployment rate in rural areas remained static at 4.2% in October but remained well below the 4.4% level registered in October 2025. In rural areas, the unemployment rate fell both among men and women. While the unemployment rate fell back to 4.3% in October from 4.4% in the previous month among rural men, it fell to 3.8% from 3.9% among rural women. Compared with October, 2025, the overall unemployment actually fell from 5.2% to 4.9%. The rural unemployment rate declined by 0.2 percentage points from 4.4% in October 2025 to 4.2% in October 2026. It fell more sharply in urban areas, from 7% in October 2025 to 6.7% in October 2026, the ministry of statistics and programme implementation ( MoSPI ) said. According to the ministry, the overall unemployment rate among men aged 15 years and above remained stable at 4.9% in October 2026 compared with the previous month, continuing the downward or stable trend observed since June 2026. The unemployment rate among women declined across both rural and urban areas, falling overall to 5% in October from 5.2% in September, the ministry said. For rural women, the rate dropped to 3.8%—its lowest level in 2026. The Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS) is the primary official source of data on employment and unemployment in India. Since January 2025, its methodology has been updated to provide monthly and quarterly national estimates

While the unemployment rate fell back to 4.3% in October from 4.4% in the previous month among rural men, it fell to 3.8% from 3.9% among rural women. Compared with October, 2025, the overall unemployment actually fell from 5.2% to 4.9%. The rural unemployment rate declined by 0.2 percentage points from 4.4% in October 2025 to 4.2% in October 2026. It fell more sharply in urban areas, from 7% in October 2025 to 6.7% in October 2026, the ministry of statistics and programme implementation ( MoSPI ) said. According to the ministry, the overall unemployment rate among men aged 15 years and above remained stable at 4.9% in October 2026 compared with the previous month, continuing the downward or stable trend observed since June 2026. The unemployment rate among women declined across both rural and urban areas, falling overall to 5% in October from 5.2% in September, the ministry said. For rural women, the rate dropped to 3.8%—its lowest level in 2026. The Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS) is the primary official source of data on employment and unemployment in India. Since January 2025, its methodology has been updated to provide monthly and quarterly national estimates

082889053e29620a.title: Committee to inspect Valagerahalli Lake
082889053e29620a.summary: Published - November 17, 2026 01:00 am IST - Bengaluru The Lokayukta has acted on a petition filed by local residents, who raised concerns over the deteriorating condition of Valagerahalli Lake and the health hazards it poses. After examining the complaints and a report submitted by the executive engineer of the lake division of the Bengaluru West City Corporation, the Lokayukta observed that sewage was entering the lake along with rainwater. The Lokayukta expressed concern over the lack of adequate action by the authorities to prevent pollution and protect the lake. A joint inspection committee comprising the Chief Engineer (TAC) of the Karnataka Lokayukta, Superintendent of Police-1, Karnataka Lokayukta, and officials of the Karnataka State Pollution Control Board has been constituted. The committee has been directed to inspect the lake, assess its present condition, and submit a report with recommendations by November 30. The Lokayukta said action would be initiated against officials found guilty of dereliction of duty if steps were not taken to resolve the issue. ec92f89f9a9b7221.title: Events lined up for National Newborn Week at Government Stanley Hospital
ec92f89f9a9b7221.summary: Published - November 17, 2026 12:01 am IST - CHENNAI The Institute of Social Paediatrics, Government Stanley Medical College Hospital, is observing the “National Newborn Week” from November 15 to November 21 to create awareness about scientific newborn care, and to dispel prevailing myths and misconceptions. According to a press release, the theme for 2026 is “Small Babies, Big Potential. Invest in Follow-up Care to Protect Their Future”, highlighting the importance of regular follow-up and developmental monitoring of small babies. As part of the celebrations, hospital dean S. Jothikumar and institute’s director J. Ganesh distributed newborn care awareness pamphlets to nursing mothers and the public on Monday, and interacted with them to clarify their doubts. The week-long celebrations include educational sessions for nursing mothers on newborn care, Neonatal Resuscitation Programme training for undergraduate and postgraduate medical students, a session on prevention of sepsis for Newborn Intensive Care Unit staff nurses, a mentor visit to Thiruvottiyur Urban Primary Health Centre, and a lecture on Essential Newborn Care for nursing students. According to Sample Registration System 2024 data, India’s Neonatal Mortality Rate and Infant Mortality Rate are 18 and 24 per 1,000 live births, respectively, while Tamil Nadu has achieved lower rates of eight and 11 respectively. However, continued efforts are essential to further reduce preventable newborn deaths, the release said. Vice-principal R. Sathya Lakshmi and Resident Medical Officer Vanithamalar participated. d4ee39faf0d39627.title: 70% turnout in most districts as four-phase panchayat polls end in Rajasthan
d4ee39faf0d39627.summary: Published - November 17, 2026 01:34 am IST - JAIPUR The four-phase panchayat election process in Rajasthan concluded on Monday with polling held for 3,747 sarpanch and 33,885 ward panch posts across 25 districts. Voting exceeded 70% in most of the districts that went to the polls in the final phase. There were stray incidents of confrontation and violence at some places, though long queues of voters were seen at several polling stations since morning. Villagers in Jalore district’s Gundau and Bharatpur district’s Shakarpur staged protests and created a ruckus raising allegations of bogus voting. Police fired in the air and used force to disperse the supporters of two rival candidates for the sarpanch post at Mahu Gulawali in Dholpur district. The two groups clashed and hurled stones at each other, while one of them set on fire two motorcycles parked outside a polling booth. In Dholpur’s Baroli village, polling started in late afternoon amid tension over a shooting incident on Sunday that resulted in the death of one person following a clash over election-related rivalry. Police have detained the main accused and 10 others in connection with the incident. The allegations of fraudulent voting sparked tension in Kali Pahadi village of Khairthal-Tijara district and a verbal altercation between two groups escalated into a physical confrontation. Police arrived in the village on receiving information and brought the situation under control. An elderly person, who sustained serious injuries during the clash, was referred to Alwar for treatment. Voting for both sarpanch and ward panch posts was conducted through ballot papers. More than 1.05 crore voters were eligible to exercise their franchise at 11,905 polling stations. Counting of votes started immediately after the polling ended.
