Villagers in Jalore district’s Gundau and Bharatpur district’s Shakarpur staged protests and created a ruckus raising allegations of bogus voting. Police fired in the air and used force to disperse the supporters of two rival candidates for the sarpanch post at Mahu Gulawali in Dholpur district. The two groups clashed and hurled stones at each other, while one of them set on fire two motorcycles parked outside a polling booth. In Dholpur’s Baroli village, polling started in late afternoon amid tension over a shooting incident on Sunday that resulted in the death of one person following a clash over election-related rivalry. Police have detained the main accused and 10 others in connection with the incident. The allegations of fraudulent voting sparked tension in Kali Pahadi village of Khairthal-Tijara district and a verbal altercation between two groups escalated into a physical confrontation. Police arrived in the village on receiving information and brought the situation under control. 26e7ae12664ae0fd.title: India's sugar output more than doubles to 2.35 mn tonnes by Nov 15: ISMA
26e7ae12664ae0fd.summary: India's sugar production more than doubled to 23.59 lakh tonne in the ongoing 2026-27 season through November 15, as mills in top producer Maharashtra started crushing early, the Indian Sugar & Bio-Energy Manufacturers Association (ISMA) said on Monday. Output stood at 11.49 lakh tonne in the same period a year earlier, the industry body said. The sugar season runs from October to September, with crushing typically starting in October-November. The sweetener's production in Maharashtra, the country's biggest producer, jumped more than threefold to 18.51 lakh tonne from 5.25 lakh tonne a year earlier. Mills in the western state began crushing from October 8, earlier than in other states, and 154 mills were operating as of November 15, against 132 a year ago. Output in Uttar Pradesh, the second-biggest producer, fell to 2.10 lakh tonne from 4.25 lakh tonne, with 80 mills operational compared with 88 a year earlier. In Karnataka, the third-largest producer, output was little changed .

The Bengaluru Water Supply and Sewerage Board (BWSSB) has clarified that it has not granted any approval or issued a no-objection certificate (NOC) for the proposed 18.5-km Ragigudda-Kanakapura Road elevated corridor, which is planned along a water pipeline alignment in south Bengaluru. It also categorically stated that the Board had not issued any approval or NOC for construction of any structure along the said route. 1ce65c42fd8a5905.title: IISc researchers combine antibiotics to tackle drug-resistant TB
1ce65c42fd8a5905.summary: Published - November 17, 2026 12:49 am IST - Bengaluru Bacteria which cause tuberculosis Mycobacterium tuberculosis, 3D illustration Researchers at the Indian Institute of Science (IISc), have identified a strategy to restore the effectiveness of isoniazid, a frontline drug used to treat tuberculosis (TB), caused by the bacterium Mycobacterium tuberculosis (M. tuberculosis). According to the IISc, TB caused by M. tuberculosis, continues to remain one of the world’s most persistent health challenges. However, it said that what’s particularly alarming is the bacterium’s growing resistance to isoniazid. Now, researchers at the Department of Biochemistry have now identified a strategy to restore the effectiveness of isoniazid – by combining it with another antibiotic, vancomycin. They found that this combination can reverse isoniazid resistance in clinical isolates of M. tuberculosis and reduce bacterial burden in a mouse model. “Isoniazid resistance poses a major challenge in the treatment of TB. To tackle this problem, we started exploring ways to rescue the drug by reversing resistance,” said Nagasuma Chandra, Professor at the Department of Biochemistry and corresponding author of the study published in Microbiology Spectrum . PhD student and first author of the study, Sukriti Pal said that although several antibiotic combinations are available for TB treatment challenges presist due to drug-resistance. She said that the new study identifies a drug treatment strategy that can reverse resistance to isoniazid, an otherwise highly effective antibiotic. The researchers tested the combination of isoniazid and vancomycin against clinical isolates of M. tuberculosis obtained from patient sputum samples with drug-resistant TB, in collaboration with the National Tuberculosis Institute, Bengaluru. 6ade28a1b9578697.title: Chennai hospital treats 5-year-old girl with rare ‘Dancing Eye Syndrome’
6ade28a1b9578697.summary: Published - November 17, 2026 12:19 am IST - Chennai Dr. Mehta’s Hospitals treated a five-year-old girl with Opsoclonus Myoclonus Ataxia Syndrome (OMAS), a.k.a. Dancing Eye Syndrome, a rare autoimmune disorder associated with a thoracic tumour located adjacent to the aorta, the main artery that carries blood from the heart to the rest of the body. The team, led by M. Raghul, pediatric surgeon, performed minimally invasive surgery to remove the tumour. Shivan Kesavan, pediatric neurologist, treated the child for OMAS. The girl was brought to the hospital for treatment in April this year following darting eye movements, slurred speech, leg pain and involuntary jerking of the head. “Removing a thoracic tumour that is densely adherent to the aorta and the chest wall has its own complexities. Performing this through a minimally invasive thoracoscopic approach is technically challenging. Despite these complexities, the team removed the tumour completely, avoiding the need for an open thoracotomy,” said Dr. Raghul. She was discharged in May 2026 and during a recent follow-up visit with Dr. Raghul, the child had made a remarkable recovery, was fully active, and showed no signs of her earlier symptoms. Dr. Shivan Kesavan, Pediatric Neurologist, Dr. Mehta’s Hospitals spoke about the need for awareness of OMAS. 771daa3bbd8e1d0f.summary: Published - November 17, 2026 12:25 am IST - Chennai IIT-Madras will open its gates to the public as part of its annual Institute Open House slated for January 2 to 4, 2027. Those visiting the institute will have an opportunity to explore its advanced research laboratories, innovation centres, and student-led technology projects. There would be about 80 stalls exhibiting student- and faculty-led research and development projects, live demonstrations, and innovations. The visiting public will have access to over 100 laboratories, including four national research centres, 11 institute research centres, and 15 centres of excellence, all coming under 18 departments, a press release stated. Those interested may register on the website shaastra.org/open-house. The last date for registration is November 30. In a partition notice to her father, Lakshmi called on him, as head of the family, to discharge his fiduciary duties and ensure a "fair and lawful partition," according to a statement from her office on Monday. Her mother, Mallika Srinivasan, has publicly backed her claim, exposing a deepening rift within the family over the distribution of its wealth. Lakshmi maintains that she is entitled to an equal share under the Hindu Succession Act, 1956, as amended in 2005, and has an independent right to seek partition. e71a710c0506da22.title: GDP growth likely to ease to 5-quarter low of 7.5% in July-September: Icra
e71a710c0506da22.summary: India's GDP growth is estimated to slow to a five-quarter low of 7.5 per cent in July-September FY27 amid external headwinds and sub-par monsoon, rating agency ICRA said on Tuesday. The Indian economy had grown at 7.8 per cent in the first quarter (April-June) of FY27 and at 8.2 per cent in the second quarter of 2025-26 fiscal year. "The slowdown (in Q2) is expected to be mild but broad-based, led by agricultural, industrial and services sectors," ICRA said in a statement. Overall, ICRA projects the GDP growth to ease slightly to 7.5 per cent in Q2 2026-27 from 7.8 per cent in Q1 2026-27, exceeding the Monetary Policy Committee's forecast of 7.2 per cent for the quarter. ICRA estimates the farm sector to clock 0.2 per cent growth in Q2, as against 3.6 per cent in Q1 FY27. Industrial sector growth is seen at 7.2 per cent against 7.7 per cent, while the services sector is estimated at 9.1 per cent against 10 per cent. 5c353c948efc1a6c.title: Wheat sowing down 15% so far; overall rabi crops coverage falls 11%
5c353c948efc1a6c.summary: Wheat - the main rabi crop - has been sown on 50.07 lakh hectare so far this year, down by 15.27 per cent from 59.10 lakh hectare a year ago, according to data released by the Union Agriculture Ministry. The wheat crop is usually sown in October-November and harvested in March-April. In the 2025-26 crop year (July-June), wheat was planted on 336 lakh hectare. As per the latest data, the pace of wheat sowing is lagging behind as compared to last year due to the 13 per cent deficient June-September monsoon, which reduced residual soil moisture before sowing began. Experts said lower irrigation availability is another factor, with reservoir and canal water levels below normal in key wheat-growing states. Wheat requires several rounds of irrigation after planting. The Central Water Commission (CWC)'s November 12 data showed less storage in reservoirs. In a statement, its executive director Henri Tiphange condemned the actions of the MLA in sending obscene and inappropriate text messages to the Collector and trespassing into her residence. He said an investigation team, headed by a female officer of IPS rank, must be formed, and the matter subjected to a CB-CID inquiry. The affected Collector must not be transferred till the completion of the investigation. The Chief Minister must prove that TVK was a clean party by expelling the MLA from the party. This incident had occurred two months back and was discussed widely in the media. Besides, Villupuram Range DIG had confirmed this incident, according to a newspaper report. “That not even a single action has been taken against the MLA in a democratic country represents the height of authoritarianism. A few years ago, following a complaint by a female IPS officer who was harassed by senior police officer Rajesh Das while on security duty for the former CM, an investigation was conducted and the court awarded appropriate punishment to the perpetrator,” Mr. Tiphange said. Instead of conducting a transparent investigation in a similar manner, the TVK government was protecting the MLA. The Constitution guaranteed rights such as Article 15(3) (special protection), Article 21 (right to live with dignity), and Article 51A(e) (protecting the dignity of women). Why, then, had the rights guaranteed by the Constitution failed to protect the Collector, he asked. The affected IAS officer operated within the administrative framework of the government. 240b5d4dae42646d.title: VB-GRAMG may cost states up to 6 times more than Mgnrega: PRS report
240b5d4dae42646d.summary: The new rural employment scheme VB-GRAMG would have cost states six times more compared to MGNREGA if it had been implemented in the previous fiscal, a report by think tank PRS Legislative Research says, with larger states like Bihar, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra and Uttar Pradesh bearing the burden of an additional spending of Rs 2,000-3,000 crore. In its 'State of State Finances Report 2026-27', PRS has given an estimate of what states would have spent if the Viksit Bharat-Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin) (VB-GRAMG), which was implemented from July 1, 2026, was in place in the 2025-26 fiscal. "The VB-GRAMG scheme is being implemented from July 1, 2026. Had VB-GRAMG been in place instead of MGNREGA in 2025-26, states would have spent around six times what they actually spent under MGNREGA," the report says. 9bfdb7a8a8448f01.summary: Amazon on Tuesday announced plans to invest USD 7 billion (about Rs 65,393 crore) in renewable energy projects in India by 2030, in addition to the USD 4 billion already contracted, as it unveiled four new wind and solar projects with a combined capacity of 934 megawatts. The company said the investment makes it one of India's leading corporate purchasers of carbon-free energy. The four initiatives consist of a 234 MW wind farm in Karnataka -- marking Amazon's largest contracted wind project in Asia to date -- alongside a 200 MW hybrid solar-and-wind facility in the same state, a 300 MW solar installation in Madhya Pradesh, and a 200 MW solar project in Rajasthan. Secured through power purchase agreements (PPAs), the projects are part of the USD 4 billion in renewable energy projects already contracted by Amazon in India, the company said. 3d728dbcdf02d5bb.title: Ruling party MLA’s charge-sheet against govt. speaks volumes about corruption in Cong. rule: BRS
3d728dbcdf02d5bb.summary: Published - November 18, 2026 01:14 am IST - HYDERABAD Spokesperson of the Bharat Rashtra Samithi (BRS) and MLC Dasoju Sravan has stated that a ruling party MLA himself has exposed the rampant corruption and commission culture in the Congress Government. Citing recent remarks made by Jadcherla MLA Janampally Anirudh Reddy, Mr. Sravan on Tuesday demanded an answer from Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy on the charges against the government by the ruling party MLA. In a statement, he said the charge-sheet against the government from within the ruling party speaks volumes of the situation. Mr. Sravan commended Mr. Anirudh Reddy for courageously speaking out against corruption within his own government. “It is not a charge-sheet from the Opposition BRS, but from a ruling party MLA himself. This is a charge-sheet released against the corrupt governance by a ruling party MLA. He has painfully exposed why contractors are fleeing the State and why development works have come to a standstill,” Mr. Sravan observed. Mr. Sravan reminded the government of the good governance promise listed as the very first item in the Congress party’s election manifesto along with the promise of corruption-free governance in the national manifesto ‘Nyay Patra’. “Earlier, when Prime Minister Narendra Modi alleged that RR Tax was being collected in Telangana, we wondered what it meant. Now, your own MLA has spoken about a 20% commission racket. This is not Praja Palana but it is Percentage Palana”, Mr. Sravan said, seeking the response of the Chief Minister. 90f6a7a237d1786a.title: My aim is to just stay focused, says shooter Vivaan Kapoor
90f6a7a237d1786a.summary: Updated - November 18, 2026 12:21 am IST Vivaan highlighted the importance of the mental side of the game. | Photo Credit: Special Arrangement Focus, precision and razor-sharp reflexes are the bedrock of shooting. India’s Vivaan Kapoor, however, believes the game is as much about one’s mindset. The Jaipur-born shooter calls himself a “glass-half-full guy”, and he had every reason to live up to that description after his silver-medal finish in the men’s trap event at the recent ISSF World championships. Vivaan came within touching distance of gold before losing to Kuwait’s Abdulrahman Alfaihan in a shoot-off. The silver, however, was no small feat. He secured a quota place for India at the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics and became only the fourth Indian man to win a trap medal at the World championships. Vivaan with his World championships silver medal. | Photo Credit: Special Arrangement While the quota ensures India’s representation in the men’s trap event at Los Angeles, it does not guarantee Vivaan a place in the team. He will have to come through the National trials to earn the right to represent the country. “Standing on the podium was a dream, and there is not an iota of disappointment at missing out on gold. When you miss a target, you control your emotions and reset for the next shot. “Just like that, now, to make the Olympics cut, there’s no pressure as such. “I will not change my approach but there are some technical aspects that I need to work on. My aim is to just stay focused,” Vivaan told The Hindu. Having changed coaches just six months before the championships, Vivaan underwent an intense build-up, with three training camps under Olympic champion Giovanni Cernogoraz, two in Croatia and one in Italy. “Shooting alongside him in camps helped me get used to competing against top shooters. It made me calmer and better at controlling myself. Peter Wilson, our National coach, also helped me a lot with the mental aspect,” Vivaan said. Published - November 17, 202

e0b4baa1c5a987cc.title: Convocation ceremony row: Maharaja’s College council asks suspended students to accept their mistake
e0b4baa1c5a987cc.summary: Published - November 18, 2026 01:42 am IST - KOCHI A meeting of the council of Maharaja’s College, Kochi, held on Tuesday accepted an inquiry committee report that indicted activists of the Students’ Federation of India (SFI) for disrupting a convocation ceremony attended by Minister for Higher Education Roji M. John on October 30. The meeting recommended that V. Praneel Raj, chairperson, and Nafeesathul Misriya, vice-chairperson of the college union, who were suspended in connection with the incident on November 2, submit an apology admitting their mistake. The inquiry committee report found that the incident had caused disrepute to the image of the institution in the public domain, according to sources. The council observed that it did not wish to initiate further disciplinary action against the students, but they need to accept their mistake. The meeting took note of the case registered by the police against 10 SFI activists booked in connection with the protest. SFI activists staged the protest soon after the Minister completed his inaugural address at the convocation ceremony, seeking answers from him on the suspension of 16 students of Sree Sankaracharya University of Sanskrit, Kalady. The activists demanded that the Minister withdraw his alleged statements against those who were suspended for protesting against Vice-Chancellor Ciza Thomas. Following the protest, Mr. John had to leave the function midway. 572af06574b9e936.title: Kedarnath generates 73 tonnes of waste during 2026 Char Dham Yatra
572af06574b9e936.summary: Published - November 18, 2026 03:00 am IST - New Delhi A view of the Badrinath Temple, nestled between the Nar and Narayana mountain ranges on the bank of the Alaknanda river. File. | Photo Credit: PTI Pilgrims visiting the Kedarnath shrine generated 73 tonnes of waste during the 2026 Char Dham Yatra, more than three times the amount recorded last year. The yatra, which ended on Monday (November 16, 2026) with the closure of the Badrinath shrine portals, witnessed a record 65.65 lakh pilgrims this year. According to data shared by the civic body at Kedarnath, the 73 tonnes of waste comprised plastic bottles, food packets, Tetra Pak, and cardboard. Neeraj Kukreti, an official of the Kedarnath Nagar Panchayat, told The Hindu that waste generation this year was more than three times the 21.40 tonnes recorded in 2025. The waste generated in Kedarnath stood at 26.10 tonnes in 2024 and 32.58 tonnes in 2023, he added. To help manage the waste buildup near the temple, the district administration launched the ‘Carry Me Back’ initiative in June. The drive mobilised over 6,000 pilgrims to carry 14 tonnes of waste down to a collection point, from where it was sent for segregation and disposal.” The increase in waste generation comes amid a broader rise in pilgrim numbers across Uttarakhand’s Char Dham circuit, according to a comparative analysis released by the Dehradun-based SDC Foundation. Prepared by Anoop Nautiyal and Praveen Upreti, the study found that 65.65 lakh pilgrims visited the four Char Dham shrines — Kedarnath, Badrinath, Gangotri and Yamunotri — and Hemkund Sahib in 2026, registering a 29% increase over 51.07 lakh in 2025. The pilgrimage season extended from mid-April to mid-November. Kedarnath recorded 19,33,138 pilgrims, a 9% rise over the previous year. However, its average daily footfall declined by around 6%, from 10,113 pilgrims in 2025 to 9,476 in 2026. b506aaa32f42ba60.title: GRAP-III restrictions lifted in Delhi-NCR as air quality improves; Stage I and II curbs to remain in effect
b506aaa32f42ba60.summary: The Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM) on Tuesday revoked Stage-III restrictions under the Graded Response Action Plan (GRAP) in Delhi and the National Capital Region (NCR), citing a sustained improvement in air quality over the past three days. The decision was taken by the CAQM's GRAP Sub-Committee after reviewing the downward trend in pollution levels. However, measures under GRAP Stages I and II will continue across the NCR, along with the directions issued by the Commission in its October 30 order. Delhi's air quality remained in the 'poor' category on Tuesday morning, with the overall Air Quality Index (AQI) recorded at 238 at 8 AM, according to the Central Pollution Control Board ( CPCB ). Of the capital's 58 monitoring stations, 31 reported 'poor' air quality, while 24 recorded 'moderate' levels. Siri Fort was the only station to report 'very poor' air quality, with an AQI of 303, according to the monitoring data. The easing of restrictions comes after Delhi's pollution levels worsened ahead of Diwali . Stage-III measures were enforced on November 6, when the city's average AQI touched 382, falling in the 'very poor' category. The restrictions were aimed at preventing further deterioration in air quality. With the withdrawal of Stage-III curbs, restrictions on certain construction and demolition activities and specified categories of vehicles will be eased. However, pollution-control measures prescribed under the first two stages of GRAP will remain operational. Favourable weather conditions and changes in the movement of pollution from neighbouring regions contributed to the recent improvement in Delhi's air quality, according to Dr Manoj Kumar, an air quality and energy analyst at the Centre for Research on Energy and Clean Air ( CREA ). Kumar identified northwesterly winds reaching speeds of up to 15 kmph and a mixing depth of approximately 1,500 metres as key factors that helped disperse pollutants. VELANKANNI RAJ Advances in neonatal care, specialised medical infrastructure and multidisciplinary interventions are improving the survival prospects of babies born extremely prematurely, including those at the limits of viability, doctors at Rainbow Children’s Hospital said in here on Tuesday. To mark World Prematurity Day 2026, the hospital highlighted its expertise in managing periviable births, defined in India as deliveries at 24 to 25 weeks of gestation, and shared the journeys of children who overcame life-threatening complications following prolonged neonatal intensive care. Giridhar S., Clinical Lead – Neonatology, said advancements in neonatal care and the development of specialised facilities had improved survival prospects for babies born between 23 weeks and 25 weeks. He said the hospital had developed a dedicated ecosystem involving advanced ventilators, specialised incubators, round-the-clock neonatologists, a multidisciplinary team of specialists and an in-house human milk bank. Adequate nutritional support, infection control, developmental care and parental involvement were also crucial in managing extremely premature babies. “Regular eye and hearing assessments and developmental follow-up after discharge were essential,” Dr. Giridhar said. Shobana Rajendran, senior consultant neonatologist, presented the case of baby Pranav, who was born at 23 weeks weighing just 500 grams. After four-and-a-half months in the NICU, during which he required ventilator support and treatment for several complications, including extremely high blood sugar levels, he was discharged weighing two kg. ec062670af03020e.summary: Published - November 18, 2026 03:40 am IST London, November 17: “’Funk Holes’ for the civilian population during air raids are at present engaging the attention of the War Office, which is secretly earmarking a number of underground cellars tunnels and tubes for the purpose of ascertaining what cover is available in case of future emergency. Supplied with books and papers to pass the time, selected guardsmen who had first been rigorously medically examined yesterday spent several hours in an underground chamber adjoining the General Post Office tube. Scientists closely watched their behaviour and directed the supply of fresh air through the shaft as the soldiers showed signs of wilting in the stuffy atmosphere. 8aca1526b4d9f7d7.title: Release long-incarcerated Muslims on humanitarian grounds, says Jawahirullah
8aca1526b4d9f7d7.summary: Published - November 18, 2026 01:18 am IST - CHENNAI M.H. Jawahirullah leading the TMMK protest in Chennai on Tuesday. | Photo Credit: V.UMESH KUMAR Thousands of cadres of the Tamil Muslim Munnetra Kazhagam (TMMK) participated in a protest on Tuesday demanding that Muslim prisoners, who have been jailed for many years, be released on humanitarian grounds. They also sought that persons who belong to the Backward Class and Most Backward Class category, and convert to Islam, be allowed to avail 3.5% reservation meant for BC Muslims in Tamil Nadu. Speaking at he protest, Papanasam MLA M.H. Jawahirullah also criticised the TVK-led government, stating that it was not enough to just say they were supportive of Muslims. He demanded that an amendment be brought in the Assembly and passed to ensure that persons belonging to the BC and MBC be also allowed to avail the reservation. “We met the Law Minister and Public Works Minister. We met them along with former High Court Judge G.M. Akbar Ali…we spoke to them about how the Muslim prisoners can be released. They assured us that they would consider it. But, it didn’t happen. We also meet former Chief Minister M.K. Stalin, when he led the previous government. I have stressed the need to release prisoners, who had been jailed for many years, repeatedly in the Assembly. The DMK government released 41 life prisoners. Of which, 21 were Muslims,” he said. “What is stopping you from releasing the prisoners? This is why we say you are two-faced,” he said, referring to the TVK-led government. He said the TMMK had been the only movement that had been consistently speaking up for the release of such prisoners. “Many say that some of them were arrested under the Explosives Act, but the punishment is only seven years. How many years have they been in jail?” he added. Published - November 18, 2026 01:18 am IST Terms & conditions | Institutional Subscriber Comments have to be in English, and in full sentences. 922a90d56dc34cd7.title: Kerala High Court allows Cusat employees to seek review of suspension
922a90d56dc34cd7.summary: Updated - November 18, 2026 01:31 am IST - KOCHI The court instructed the petitioners to file an application before the Syndicate seeking a review of the suspension order. The Kerala High Court has held that the suspended employees of the Cochin University of Science and Technology (Cusat) can approach the university Syndicate seeking a review of their suspension. Justice P. Gopinath issued the interim direction in view of the Syndicate meeting scheduled for November 21. The court directed the Syndicate to examine whether the continued suspension was justified. It also instructed the petitioners to file an application before the Syndicate seeking a review of the suspension order. Cusat Employees Association members Anurin Salim, P.M. Sivadas, and Harilal had approached the court challenging the suspension order. The Syndicate had suspended the petitioners based on an inquiry report by the Vigilance and Anti-Corruption Bureau (VACB) into allegations of irregularities in appointments to the sweeper-cum-cleaner posts. They alleged that the officials were not given an opportunity to explain their position and that they were suspended before a charge memo was issued. 014844538ee51e7d.title: PM Modi proposes free e-visas, maritime plan to deepen India-Asean ties
014844538ee51e7d.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi has proposed a series of initiatives to strengthen India-ASEAN ties, including free e-visas for tourists from ASEAN countries, a long-term maritime cooperation plan, nuclear energy technical exchanges and collaboration in critical minerals. The proposals were outlined in a Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) statement following the 23rd ASEAN-India Summit in Manila on Tuesday. Among the key proposals is a long-term ASEAN-India Maritime Cooperation Plan covering connectivity, scientific research, disaster management, Coast Guard cooperation, maritime domain awareness and seafarers' security. Modi also proposed a joint cyber forensics training programme to build capacity in the region and ASEAN-India technical exchanges in nuclear energy. Other proposals include an ASEAN-India Space Hackathon and cooperation in mining and critical minerals. beb46b823c5f2b59.title: Delhi records Nov's cleanest air at AQI 204, but relief may be short-lived
beb46b823c5f2b59.summary: Delhi recorded its cleanest air this month on Tuesday, with the Air Quality Index (AQI) settling at 204 in the 'poor' category, offering some respite after days of deteriorating air quality, though the relief is likely to be short-lived. The last time the national capital recorded a lower AQI was on October 31, when the index stood at 117 in the 'moderate' category. Tuesday's reading was the lowest recorded in November, making it the least polluted day of the month so far. The relatively better air quality on Tuesday was partly due to favourable meteorological conditions, the Air Quality Early Warning System said. Northwesterly winds reaching speeds of up to 15 kmph and a mixing depth of around 1,500 metres helped disperse pollutants. Mixing depth refers to the height up to which pollutants can disperse and mix in the atmosphere. A lower mixing depth restricts the vertical movement of pollutants, leading to their accumulation closer to the ground and potentially worsening air ...

3217e18f521ae052.title: NGT declines to stay EC given to Musi river front project
3217e18f521ae052.summary: Updated - November 18, 2026 01:11 am IST The National Green Tribunal’s southern zone bench-Chennai declined to stay the environmental clearances issued for the Musi river front project taken up by the Telangana State government pending disposal of a petition filed by a resident of Hyderabad. The petitioner, Babu Rao, questioned the validity of the clearances issued by the Telangana State Environment Impact Assessment Authority (SEIAA) and other official agencies for the project. The petitioner wanted the NGT to restrain the officials from going ahead with the initial works relating to the project like acquisition of land, excavation, levelling of land, site preparation and construction. The matter was adjourned to December 3 for next hearing. 063e61ccc70ec880.title: Gold imports may fall to $40 bn in FY27 on duty hike: Commerce Secy
063e61ccc70ec880.summary: India's gold imports in the current fiscal could decline to USD 40 billion, down from about USD 72 billion in FY26, as the duty hike has helped slow inbound shipments, a top official said on Wednesday. Commerce Secretary Rajesh Agrawal said the duty hike effected from May has "slowed down" gold imports "a bit" so far this year, from around USD 60 billion every year. This has also helped manage the trade deficit, he said. In May, the government had hiked import duty on gold and silver to 15 per cent, from 6 per cent, to contain non-essential imports. India imported USD 71.98 billion gold in FY26, up from USD 58.01 billion in FY25. Gold imports declined about 40 per cent to USD 24.78 billion during April-October this year, from about USD 41.24 billion in the corresponding period in 2025. "I think... this year we will end up with USD 35-40 billion of gold imports. I think that is manageable in the current year... The current duty structure has a positive impact on the gold import," .

fdfacafe55849306.summary: Struggling SpiceJet's board on Wednesday approved a proposal to raise up to Rs 5,500 crore to shore up its financial position. The airline has been facing multiple headwinds, including financial and operational woes. At its meeting on Wednesday, the airline's board was apprised of investment discussions with potential new investors. The board has cleared the proposal to raise up to Rs 5,500 crore to strengthen the airline's financial position, rebuild capacity and drive its revival, according to a statement. Further, the board has directed the management to work towards closing it expeditiously. "The proposed fundraise may be undertaken through a combination of equity and other permitted instruments and will be subject to the requisite approvals," the statement said. 17d730c28f45b3d7.summary: Tata Steel, in partnership with Houston-based Utility Global, will undertake a project to produce hydrogen using steel plant off-gases at its Kalinganagar facility in Odisha, marking the first such initiative in the country, the company said on Wednesday. The two companies will undertake joint Front-End Engineering and Design (FEED) studies to support a Final Investment Decision (FID) by Tata Steel's board on the proposed project, it added. The proposed facility, based on Utility Global's H2Gen technology, will have a planned capacity of 10 tonnes per day (TPD) and use off-gases generated during the steelmaking process to produce high-purity hydrogen. ab094a789e27cc17.title: Ananya Birla gets a ₹50,000 ‘Made in India’ luxury watch from Farah Khan: All about the Jaipur Watch Company piece
ab094a789e27cc17.summary: Ananya Birla, entrepreneur and singer, opened the doors of her family's Mumbai residence—the historic Jatia House bought by industrialist Kumar Mangalam Birla for ₹ 425 crore in 2018—to filmmaker Farah Khan for a new episode of her vlog ‘Food With Farah’. While the grandeur of the mansion left the director visibly impressed, a rather unique timepiece that Khan brought as a present ended up taking centre stage during the visit. Presenting the horological piece by the homegrown brand Jaipur Watch Company to Birla, Khan said, “We got you this special gift from Jaipur,” revealing that the watch was specially picked from the brand's 'Gates of India' collection. Birla, admiring the present, said, “What I love is that it is made in India.” The Main Hoon Na director also highlighted that Indian brands are now crafting one-of-a-kind luxury pieces, and pointed out, “This is a Jaipur Gate.” She also revealed that the watch has a unique reversible feature: the bezel reveals Mumbai's iconic Gateway of India on the other side. Jaipur Watch Company, a homegrown luxury watch company, said its Gates of India – Gateway of India - LOTUS embraces the heart of Jaipur's City Palace's most celebrated entrances, the Lotus Gate/the Leheriya Gate of Pritam Niwas Chowk. “More than architectural masterpieces, these gateways symbolise prosperity, renewal, and the changing seasons, welcoming generations into the royal world of art, culture, and tradition,” the company said about its yet-to-be-released product. The watchmaker, however, said that the ₹ 50,000 watch Farah Khan gifted Ananya Birla can be pre-ordered and would take upto 75 days to process. The watch, Jaipur Watch Company said, is inspired by these iconic palace gates, reimagined as a passage through India's remarkable heritage. It features a unique flip mechanism that reveals the heritage landmark of Mumbai — the Gateway of India. With a smooth 360° rotation, the watch offers a refined dual-display design that reflects exceptional en

a6d1195950f3317e.title: Two Tamil Nadu schools win inaugural Children’s Earthshot Awards
a6d1195950f3317e.summary: Updated - November 20, 2026 01:08 am IST - CHENNAI Students of Kaligi Ranganathan Montford Matriculation Higher Secondary School with the inaugural Earthshot Challenge award. | Photo Credit: Special Arrangement Two schools in Tamil Nadu have won the inaugural I CAN Earthshot Challenge for developing solutions to environmental problems, ranging from plastic pollution to water conservation. Kaligi Ranganathan Montford Matriculation Higher Secondary School in Perambur, Chennai, won in the ‘Protect and Restore Nature’ category for its initiative, ‘Tiny Action, Mighty Impact’. A team of six students from Classes 7 and 8 took up the challenge of making their school more environmentally sustainable through four student-led initiatives focusing on carbon emissions, plastic waste, water conservation, and food waste. One of their interventions was collecting used milk packets from students of the school, which were washed, dried and handed over to Exnora International to be reused as grow bags for plants. “We collected more than 50,000 milk packets. Everyone supported us and brought them to school with interest,” said Janavi M., a Class 8 student who was part of the team. They also began collecting water discharged by the school’s 63 air-conditioners for reuse in cleaning corridors and restrooms and watering plants. S. Enitha said to reduce the carbon footprint of the school, the team encouraged parents to opt for walking or cycling for short commutes. “We learned to make seed balls and threw them in empty spaces around our school where nothing was growing,” she said. Teacher coordinator Gomathi said the team decided to take up four interconnected initiatives towards making the school carbon-neutral. “We cannot completely control carbon emissions, but we can take steps to reduce them and compensate by such small actions,” she said. The project was among 15 finalists selected from 974 submissions. The winners were announced at the Children’s Earthshot Awards Ceremony organised

4b9f2983919a6940.title: Reject rolls, use updated 2025 voter list for local polls, says anti-SIR Coalition
4b9f2983919a6940.summary: Published - November 20, 2026 06:01 am IST - Bengaluru The coalition has demanded that the government reject the SIR final rolls, conduct local body elections using the 2025 electoral rolls updated through the proposed social audit. | Photo Credit: File photo Rejecting the final electoral rolls published after the Special Intensive Revision (SIR), the Anti-SIR Coalition in Karnataka, pointing to the large-scale wrongful deletions and discrepancies, has requested the State government to conduct an independent social audit to identify eligible voters left out of the rolls. The coalition has demanded that the government reject the SIR final rolls, conduct local body elections using the 2025 electoral rolls updated through the proposed social audit, and take a clear stand on the issue amid uncertainty over which electoral rolls should be used for the upcoming local body polls. Recently, the State Election Commission directed that the SIR final rolls will be used as a base for GBA elections, slated to be held before December 31. However, the Congress-led State government, which has been opposing the exercise, has not announced a clear stand yet, though the issue was discussed in the cabinet. In a statement on Thursday, the coalition announced a State-wide investigation campaign from November 20 to December 20 to document cases of wrongful deletion, exclusion of eligible voters and procedural irregularities in the SIR process. Booth-level public hearings will be held at several locations across the State on December 20, it said. The coalition said Karnataka had an estimated adult population of 5.2 crore, while the final electoral rolls contained only around 4.5 crore names, leaving nearly 70 lakh people unaccounted for. It questioned how such a large gap could remain despite the Election Commission of India’s (ECI) stated objective of ensuring that no eligible voter was left out. 9b051c1130e81e0a.title: Nashik Court grants bail to Imtiaz Jaleel in TCS case on ₹50,000 bond
9b051c1130e81e0a.summary: Published - November 20, 2026 04:08 am IST AIMIM leader Imtiaz Jaleel. File. | Photo Credit: The Hindu The Nashik District and Sessions Court on Thursday (November 19, 2026) granted bail to AIMIM leader Imtiaz Jaleel, a co-accused in the TCS conversion and harassment case, after he appeared before the court and submitted a bond of ₹50,000, following the prosecution’s opposition to his plea. When Mr. Jaleel appeared before the court to file the application for bail, the counsel representing the state opposed the plea, but the court approved the release upon the submission of the bond because the sections invoked against him permit release on bail. The investigation into the TCS case established that Nida Khan evaded law enforcement for two months by staying in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar. During the probe into the shelter provided to Khan, officials questioned MIM corporator Matin Patel to determine who directed him. The retrieval of evidence from devices and items led the police to name Jaleel, Patel, and individuals associated with them as co-accused in the case for providing assistance to a person evading law enforcement. ff2134de32bccce3.title: ‘Do not take 140 crore Indians for granted’: PM Modi's blunt message to India Inc at FICCI AGM | 10 key takeaways
ff2134de32bccce3.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Thursday, November 19, urged Indian businesses to move beyond the domestic market, improve product quality, reduce import dependence and expand their global footprint, calling on industry leaders to make India First the foundation of their long-term investment decisions. Addressing the 100th Annual General Meeting and Annual Convention of the Federation of Indian Chambers of Commerce and Industry (FICCI) at Bharat Mandapam in New Delhi, PM Modi outlined opportunities across the pharmaceuticals, agriculture, food processing, engineering, steel and aluminium sectors. He also challenged businesses to translate the benefits of tax reforms into higher salaries and more employment, while invoking Mahatma Gandhi's message of Swadeshi and self-reliance. Here are the key takeaways from PM Modi's address: PM Modi urged businesses to stop treating India's large domestic market as an assured destination for products, stressing that Indian consumers deserve the same quality of goods as overseas buyers. He criticised the practice of selling products to Indian customers by describing them as "export quality". "Do not take 140 crore Indians for granted as an assured market where anything will sell. Even today, sellers tell customers 'this is export quality' to convince them it is good. What do you take our countrymen for? Do they not deserve good quality? This mindset must change; my countrymen deserve top quality," he said. He added that India's domestic market should serve as a launchpad for global competitiveness rather than become a comfort zone. "Our domestic market must not become our comfort zone. It should give us the confidence to compete in global markets," PM Modi said. The Prime Minister asked industry leaders to look beyond short-term business gains and prepare for emerging requirements in India and international markets. Sameeran at the Ripon Buildings on Thursday. | Photo Credit: Special Arrangement The Greater Chennai Corporation (GCC) discussed measures to prevent bird hits involving aircraft during landing and take-off at Chennai airport, in a meeting chaired by Commissioner G.S. Sameeran at the Ripon Buildings on Thursday (November 19, 2026). The meeting discussed measures to reduce bird movement along the Adyar river and its banks, expedite biomining operations to remove legacy waste at the Perungudi dumping ground, and prevent birds from nesting in the waterbodies established at Guindy. P. Rajkumar, General Manager (Operations), Airports Authority of India, Chennai International Airport; Deputy Commissioner (Health) Shubham Gyanadevrao Thakare; Chief Engineers Balamurali and P. Sankaravelu; and officials from the airport and the GCC were present. The protest was held in the wake of the onset of the Northeast monsoon, when it could be risky to conduct court proceedings at the dilapidated Judicial Magistrate court. “Work to build a permanent court complex should be expedited. An additional district court should also be set up in the court complex”, said A.C. Devakumar, president, Bar Association (Vaniyambadi). At present, Vaniyambadi has three lower courts that are located in different areas in the town. Each court, on an average, is located at least 1.5 km away from the other court. It has resulted in hardship for litigants, advocates, and court staff to commute from one court to another as some petitioners have cases in different courts that will be taken up on the same day. The Judicial Magistrate Court, the oldest among three courts, was located in the Government Estate since the 1920s. The District Munsif court, formed in 1995, was functioning from a rented room in the Government Commercial Tax building. The subordinate court that was created in 2009 was also operating from a rented room in the town. Every day, on an average, more than 150 litigants, mostly from Vaniyambadi taluk that comprises 45 villages, visit these courts. Around 75 advocates are working as regular practitioners. On an average, over 100 cases come up at each court every day. Currently, 1,500 - 2,000 cases are pending before each of these three courts. 33a189cc4e600e4a.title: A hundred years ago | Letter to Swedish academy
33a189cc4e600e4a.summary: Published - November 20, 2026 03:16 am IST London, Nov. 19: Mr. Bernard Shaw tenders his best thanks for the award (Nobel Prize) but says that his readers and audiences provide more than sufficient money for his needs and that his renown is greater than is good for his spiritual health. The money therefore to him is like a lifebelt thrown to a swimmer who has already safely reached the shore. He proceeds to point out some very advantageous sites in London which are being rapidly filled by agencies in which not only the Dominions but also the European powers exhibit very choice products to advertise travel attractions and all sorts of things to tempt the importer but a book is rarely exhibited. Sweden invites us to buy paper, but nothing is printed on it. The function of the Swedish paper seems to be to wrap up Australian apples. Sweden’s most valuable export is her literature of which Britons are deplorably ignorant. He suggests that the money accompanying the award should be funded and the proceeds annually used to encourage understanding in literature and art between Sweden and British Isles. especially the translations of valuable Swedish books. a7145ea5fe74af02.title: Kerala High Court disposes of PILs against reconstitution of Waqf Board
a7145ea5fe74af02.summary: Published - November 20, 2026 01:03 am IST - KOCHI A Division Bench of the Kerala High Court on Thursday disposed of all public interest litigations (PILs) related to the reconstitution of the Kerala State Waqf Board. The Bench observed that the reconstitution of the board had given rise to a fresh cause of action, following which the aggrieved parties had filed writ petitions. It said the petitions were required to be heard by a Single Judge in accordance with the roster. The High Court had in October refused to stay the reconstitution of the board. The court was considering appeals filed by former board chairperson K.S. Hamza and member C.K. Usman Haji against a Single Bench order refusing to stay the reconstitution. The court had then held that a stay could not be granted as the new board had taken charge. The State had reconstituted the board on October 16 and nominated nine new members. f3313cea8f44a530.title: Delhi High Court stays Lokpal proceedings against Defence Secretary
f3313cea8f44a530.summary: Published - November 20, 2026 03:47 am IST Solicitor General Tushar Mehta, representing the CBI, submitted that the issue may require deeper examination by the court. File. | Photo Credit: The Hindu The Delhi High Court on Thursday (November 19, 2026) stayed proceedings before the Lokpal against Defence Secretary Rajesh Kumar Singh in connection with a corruption complaint concerning promotions at the National Productivity Council (NPC). A Bench of Justice Subramonium Prasad and Justice Renu Bhatnagar sought responses from the Lokpal and the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) on a petition by Mr. Singh challenging the Lokpal’s March 4, 2025, and October 26, 2026, orders and the October 28 notice directing him to appear for proceedings under the Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act. The court listed the matter for further hearing on January 20 next year. The complaint alleges irregularities and corruption in recruitment and promotions at the NPC. The allegations against Mr. Singh relate to his decision to forward an advisory committee report concerning the promotions to the NPC’s Governing Body for appropriate action, instead of directing the organisation to act on the report. Solicitor General Tushar Mehta, representing the CBI, submitted that the issue may require deeper examination by the court. Senior advocate Vikas Singh, appearing for the Defence Secretary, said that the Lokpal’s October 26, 2026 order and October 28, 2026 notice are founded on the January 6, 2025 order and January 7, 2025 notice, both of which have already been quashed by the High Court. He said the Lokpal directed a hearing against the petitioner for the second time “without crossing the threshold” laid down by the High Court in its November 28, 2025, judgment in the same case. 28cc680cd32ebf8f.title: Centre proposes separate licensing norms for wholesale trade of bulk drugs
28cc680cd32ebf8f.summary: The Ministry of Health and Family Welfare has proposed a separate licensing framework for the wholesale trade of bulk drugs, including active and inactive bulk substances, to strengthen regulatory oversight and accountability in the pharmaceutical supply chain. The proposed amendments to the Drugs Rules, 1945, seek to introduce separate application (19-BC) and licence (20-BC) forms for the wholesale of bulk drugs, distinct from the existing licensing provisions for formulations. At present, a common licence covers the wholesale of both formulations and bulk drugs. The proposed amendment seeks to establish a dedicated licensing framework for bulk drugs, enabling more focused regulatory oversight of their wholesale trade and greater accountability in the pharmaceutical supply chain, the ministry said in a statement. The police are investigating whether it is a case of suicide. He was reportedly rushed to Tagore Medical College and Hospital, where the doctors declared him dead on arrival. The police registered a case and have sent the body for a post-mortem. The student was allegedly caught indulging in malpractice during an exam on Wednesday, a police note accessed by The Hindu said. He was informed by authorities that an inquiry would be conducted, the fear of which could have prodded him to take the extreme step, the note added. The student was a native of Jharkhand and his parents were expected to reach Chennai on Thursday evening. Attempts to reach out to VIT Chennai authorities did not yield results. 53ebce943f76d307.title: GTA 6 developers worry about layoffs despite working on Rockstar's ‘biggest’ game: ‘We have had no indication’
53ebce943f76d307.summary: Rockstar Games has released Grand Theft Auto 6 (GTA 6) , a title expected to generate massive revenue. However, while the launch has sparked excitement among gamers, concerns about job security continue to trouble some of the developers behind the blockbuster game. In an article for The Guardian, Nestor Uriarte, an animation programmer at Rockstar Games, highlighted the uncertainty surrounding employment in the gaming industry. He pointed out that contributing to one of the world's biggest video game releases does not necessarily protect developers from potential job cuts, particularly as studios continue to reduce their workforces. "After the big day, we have had no indication that layoffs are coming, but It’s hard not to worry about what the future holds," Uriarte wrote. Rockstar animation programmer Nestor Uriarte said that working on a major game does not guarantee job security. He pointed to widespread job cuts across the gaming industry in recent years. Uriarte said employees had received no indication that layoffs were coming. He added that uncertainty across the gaming industry still made it hard not to worry about the future. Rockstar North employees are voting on whether to secure union recognition. If approved, the union could represent more than 1,600 employees. Uriarte said AI is changing how gaming studios work and raising questions about the future relevance of developers’ skills. He noted that gaming companies worldwide have eliminated thousands of positions in recent years, with an estimated 24,000 jobs disappearing over the past two years. The scale of these cuts, he said, has left even employees working on highly successful projects concerned about their professional future. "It says a lot about the industry that even my colleagues and I, working on the biggest game of all time, are worried about getting laid off," he added. The growing concerns over job security have also prompted employees at Rockstar North to consider collective action. Workers

598a429bcc296620.title: Devotees visiting Guruvayur temple must be treated with respect, says Kerala High Court
598a429bcc296620.summary: Published - November 20, 2026 07:00 am IST - KOCHI The Kerala High Court has held that every devotee visiting the Guruvayur Sree Krishna Temple ought to be cared for and treated with respect. Temple employees at every level must act with the highest degree of equanimity and must not lose their temper with any devotee. Every devotee would like to spend as much time as possible in front of the deity, and employees must ensure that the queue moves, with hundreds of others waiting for darshan. It thus requires a fine balance between rival interests. Whatever be the reason or provocation, an altercation or bad behaviour on the part of any employee cannot be tolerated, the High Court said. The standing counsel for the Guruvayur Devaswom Board intervened to say that there were instances when some devotees unfairly created provocation, leading, in one case, to a stabbing incident. Undoubtedly, the responsibility and obligation of civility is mutual. But if heated situations are not properly managed, things may spiral out of control, which will be deleterious to the pious and sanctified atmosphere of the temple, the court held, while closing two suo motu petitions based on complaints from devotees who alleged harassment by Devaswom staff. Every devotee would like to spend as much time as possible in front of the deity, and employees must ensure that the queue moves, with hundreds of others waiting for darshan. It thus requires a fine balance between rival interests. Whatever be the reason or provocation, an altercation or bad behaviour on the part of any employee cannot be tolerated, the High Court said. The standing counsel for the Guruvayur Devaswom Board intervened to say that there were instances when some devotees unfairly created provocation, leading, in one case, to a stabbing incident. Undoubtedly, the responsibility and obligation of civility is mutual. But if heated situations are not properly managed, things may spiral out of control, which will be deleterious to the pious and sanctified atmosphere of the temple, the court held, while closing two suo motu petitions based on complaints from devotees who alleged harassment by Devaswom staff. 488ecaef9940c3f2.title: Shivraj Singh Chouhan unveils India's 1st home-grown H5N1 bird flu vaccine
488ecaef9940c3f2.summary: Union minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan unveiled the country's first indigenously developed H5N1 vaccine to protect chickens from bird flu here on Friday. The vaccine has been developed by the ICAR-National Institute of High Security Animal Diseases in Bhopal, officials from the Union Agriculture Ministry said. This is the first-of-its-kind vaccine developed in India against the H5N1 virus of Clade 2.3.2.1a of the highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI), they said. Speaking on the occasion, Chouhan said, "This vaccine is an example of India's self-reliance." HPAI, commonly known as bird flu, is a serious disease affecting chickens and other birds. Outbreaks can result in almost 100 per cent mortality among infected birds. Besides the Union Agriculture Minister, Madhya Pradesh Sports and Youth Welfare and Cooperatives Minister Vishwas Sarang and Bhopal BJP MP Alok Sharma, among others, were also present at the ceremony held here.

8854a402fa731af5.title: Inauguration of Bhavan’s Margazhi Mahotsav 2026 held
8854a402fa731af5.summary: Updated - November 21, 2026 01:09 am IST - CHENNAI Dignitaries at the inauguration of the Bharatiya Vidya Bhavan’s Margazhi Mahotsav 2026 in Mylapore on Friday. | Photo Credit: V. UMESH KUMAR Bharatiya Vidya Bhavan touches the lives of millions of people directly, N. Ravi, Chairman of Bhavan’s Chennai Kendra and Director of Kasturi and Sons Limited, said on Friday. At the inauguration of Bhavan’s Margazhi Mahotsav 2026, organised in association with South Zone Cultural Centre, Mr. Ravi said the institution has a vast national and global footprint retaining its original vision, ideals, and values. Bhavan’s activities encompass culture in its widest sense and are carried out through its kendras . “This Margazhi season, there are over 2,000 music and dance performances in the city, making it one of the largest music festivals in the world. In tune with this character of the city, the Chennai Kendra has organised this festival as its flagship event. For the next 45 days, we will be featuring over 1,000 artists in the main and supporting roles,” he added. B.K. Krishnaraj Vanavarayar, Vice-President, Bharatiya Vidya Bhavan, said, “There is something each country will be proud of. As far as India is concerned, our culture is our pride and it is rooted in spirituality. All the great acharyas, political leaders, and great men have visited the Bhavan’s various branches.” K.K. Gopalakrishnan, Director, South Zone Cultural Centre, said he was glad they were able to collaborate with an organisation of a global repute like the Bhavan. Bhavan’s Chennai Kendra Vice-Chairman Nalli Kuppuswami Chetti, Secretary M. Murali, and Director K.N. Ramaswamy were among those who spoke at the event. fca58b12f1386646.title: IJCCI to lead business delegation to Japan from Nov. 30
fca58b12f1386646.summary: Updated - November 21, 2026 01:19 am IST - CHENNAI A 16-member delegation from Osaka took part in the business networking meeting held by the Indo-Japan Chamber of Commerce and Industry in Chennai on Friday. | Photo Credit: RAGU R. The Indo-Japan Chamber of Commerce and Industry (IJCCI) organised a business networking meeting with a 16-member business delegation from Osaka, Japan, to strengthen bilateral business ties and explore opportunities for trade, investment, and industrial collaboration between India and Japan. The delegation was led by Hiromitsu Morishima, Chairperson, International Business Committee, Osaka Chamber of Commerce and Industry, and Yasushi Ninomiya, Director-General, JETRO Osaka. The companies spoke about their products and business opportunities. To strengthen bilateral economic relations, IJCCI is leading a 16-member delegation to Japan from November 30 to December 4. The delegation will visit Tokyo, Yokohama, Kochi, Fukuoka, Hiroshima, and Osaka. “We particularly look forward to strengthening our engagement with Osaka, which is one of Japan’s leading commercial and industrial centres,” said IJCCI president S. Padmanabhan. “India, with its large domestic market, growing manufacturing capabilities, and developing digital economy, offers significant opportunities for Japanese businesses,” Mr. Padmanabhan added. He further said that Indian companies can benefit from Japanese technology, management practices, and innovation. a3d95c5cf6358b76.summary: Published - November 21, 2026 06:00 am IST Shahu Patole, author of Dalit Kitchens of Marathwada ( Anna He Apoorna Brahma. ). | Photo Credit: Special arrangement When Shahu Patole was growing up in Khamgaon village, in Osmanabad taluka in Maharashtra, in the 1960s, he remembers stories of how toor dal was difficult to come by. The food crisis in the mid-1960s, triggered by two successive droughts, had made pulses scarce and expensive. Toor dal production, for instance, fell from 1.89 million tonnes to 1.13 million tonnes between 1964 and 1967, according to government data. So, traders would sell lakh dal (grass pea; Lathyrus sativus) instead of toor , which was a long-duration crop that took more than six months to mature, or adulterate toor with the cheaper, drought-resistant legume. This was despite the Indian government prohibiting the sale of lakh dal in 1961, because the slightly bitter-tasting dal was dangerous for health. It caused lathyrism, an irreversible neurological and skeletal condition (many people suffered from paralysis of the lower limbs). The fact that such dangerous alternatives continued to be consumed in certain States, shows how essential people considered dals to be. “When meat wasn’t available, we relied on dals ,” says Patole, 63, author of Dalit Kitchens of Marathwada (2024), adding that today toor , mung , chana , masur , urad , matki , chavli , and watane are the staples. 0682d324144b9209.title: Blue-green infrastructure, heat-risk modelling considered for Chennai’s Third Master Plan
0682d324144b9209.summary: Published - November 21, 2026 01:09 am IST - Chennai Integrating greenhouse gas emissions reductions, heat adaptation and flood mitigation into statutory planning, zoning regulations and master plans was discussed at the Conference on Climate Responsive Urban Planning in Chennai on Friday. The event detailed how heat-risk modelling, hydrological vulnerability assessments, and blue-green infrastructure strategies from three years of collaboration with the Chennai Metropolitan Development Authority (CMDA) are shaping statutory policies for Chennai’s Third Master Plan (2026-2046), according to a press release. Two 60-minute technical sessions covered integrating climate actions into urban planning and localising climate action. They included discussion on bridging Climate Action Plans with day-to-day spatial planning, and a presentation on the Madhavaram Local Area Plan. Marking 10 years of Chennai’s C40 Cities membership, the conference launched the Climate Action Guide for Urban Planners in India, following the 2024 Cairo global guide. The Clean Air Zones Report, Urban Planning Accelerator signing, and Chennai’s entry into Youth Reinventing Cities for a Tiruvottiyur neighbourhood were also announced. The Jameel C40 Urban Planning Climate Labs with the CMDA and the Greater Chennai Corporation (GCC) convened the event. More than 75 exhibitors from over 10 States and five international destinations are taking part. Rajasthan Tourism and Delhi Tourism are the partner States. Andhra Pradesh Tourism is showcasing the State’s beaches, heritage sites, pilgrim centres and nature tourism. The stalls cover hotels, resorts, airlines, cruises and travel technology. The expo is open to the travel trade and the public. “Visakhapatnam is an important and growing travel market, and we are delighted to bring this platform to the city,” said Rohit Hangal, Director, Sphere Travelmedia and Exhibitions Pvt. Ltd. Tours and Travels Association of Andhra Pradesh president K. Vijaymohan, Hotel and Restaurant Association of Andhra Pradesh president Pavan Kartheek and officials of the Rajasthan, Delhi and Andhra Pradesh tourism departments attended the inauguration. The expo ends on Saturday. The next edition will be held in Coimbatore on January 29 and 30, 2027. 9b05f1cbd283c534.title: World Bank to assist CAG in urban governance audit for 101 Indian cities
9b05f1cbd283c534.summary: New Delhi: The World bank will assist India's Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG) in examining how 101 Indian cities manage their finances, build infrastructure and deliver essential public services, as growing urban needs put pressure on municipal resources. The multilateral agency will provide technical expertise and international best practices to support the audit. The CAG is conducting a multi-year audit of urban infrastructure and services, starting with urban mobility, to provide a comprehensive assessment of municipal governance, finances and service delivery. The exercise will subsequently cover water and sanitation, housing, air quality management and liveable urban environments, with a different theme taken up each year, the comptroller and auditor general K. Sanjay Murthy said on Friday. The World Bank initiative, 'Strengthening Audit Capacity and Governance Accountability in India's Urban Sector', has been endorsed by the department of economic affairs. The exercise comes against the backdrop of growing need to strengthen municipal finances through better revenue mobilization, improved cost recovery and innovative financing mechanisms that are critical for cities to meet growing infrastructure and service delivery needs. The Union budget for 2026-27 also underscored government's focus on urban infrastructure development and the need to boost finance streams of urban local bodies, particularly for their ability to diversify revenue sources, improve financial sustainability and mobilize resources for expanding civic infrastructure. Speaking at a two-day workshop on urban infrastructure financing and municipal finance in New Delhi, Murthy said the audit of 101 cities would provide a holistic and comparable assessment of how cities are performing. He called for a sectoral approach to auditing so that multiple aspects of urban development could be assessed together. ec1b997eca2300f5.title: Indian dream has a Thai address
ec1b997eca2300f5.summary: Published - November 21, 2026 12:17 am IST Among overseas property destinations for Indian buyers, Dubai used to be the most popular and often go-to choice. However, with Thailand and its relatively accessible prices, tourism-led rental demand and holiday home appeal, Phuket, particularly, is drawing Indian buyers. According to Stuart Reading, managing director, Group Property Development at Banyan Group, “Indians are the fifth-largest buyers by value for Laguna Phuket, and they are the second-largest group of tourists in Phuket.” Banyan Group runs Laguna Phuket, a 1,000-acre integrated resort at Bang Tao with six hotels, a golf course and more than 3,000 branded residences. He says that Thailand drew over 35 million visitors in 2025, and foreign buyers account for over 60% of Phuket’s condominium purchases. “The core buyer is a high-net-worth individual or family office purchasing a legacy or trophy asset rather than a first home. It is often a second or third property bought for long-term capital preservation as much as lifestyle. We’re also seeing more second-home buyers relocating seasonally or working remotely from Phuket,” adds Reading. According to Shiv Garg, director of Forteasia Realty Pvt. Ltd, a Delhi-based real estate developer, Thailand, particularly Phuket, is gaining traction as an alternative option rather than as a direct substitute for Dubai, largely due to its relatively lower property prices. Phuket is also perceived to offer greater capital appreciation potential. 2592b7889ee0f9b9.title: Metrowater MD reviews work to resume production at Minjur desalination plant
2592b7889ee0f9b9.summary: Published - November 21, 2026 01:14 am IST - CHENNAI Chennai Metrowater has stepped up efforts to resume drinking water production at the 100 million litres a day plant. | Photo Credit: R_Shivaji Rao Chennai Metrowater has stepped up efforts to resume drinking water production at the 100 million litres a day (mld) Minjur desalination plant, with the first phase aimed at restoring its 20 mld capacity. Metrowater’s Managing Director T. Anand reviewed the ongoing works on Friday and directed the officials to submit weekly progress reports. A press release said he reviewed the work to remove accumulated sediment from the seawater intake sump and clean it using the jet wash method. He also reviewed works to restore the membranes in the seawater reverse osmosis section, which is a key component of the desalination process. Mr. Anand also enquired about the measures being taken to strengthen the plant’s automation and instrumentation systems, and progress of the detailed project report being prepared by the Tamil Nadu Water Investment Company. a093184977a9a8bb.title: Ensure no household is left out in Census enumeration, officials told
a093184977a9a8bb.summary: Published - November 21, 2026 12:26 am IST - VISAKHAPATNAM District Revenue Officer S.D. Anita on Friday directed officials to complete the population enumeration phase of Census 2027 accurately and within the stipulated time. Addressing a two-day training programme for district and charge-level officers at the Greater Visakhapatnam Municipal Corporation (GVMC) South Zone office at Suryabagh, she said that because the city is densely populated, officials should make sure no household is missed. Homeless people must also be counted, she added. Ms. Anita said self-enumeration would be open to residents from January 10 to 24, 2027. The technical glitches in the app during the housing listing phase had been fixed, she said, and officials should make the public aware of the facility. She pointed out that citizens are legally required to provide information under the Census Act, 1948. GVMC Additional Commissioner K. Ramesh suggested a target of at least 40% self-enumeration to reduce the burden on field staff. Census Joint Director S. Dayasagar also spoke. c06a14ccdd7f3879.title: Court rejects anticipatory bail pleas of six in Siddaramaiah ‘sting’ case
c06a14ccdd7f3879.summary: Published - November 21, 2026 12:49 am IST - Bengaluru A Bengaluru court on Friday rejected the anticipatory bail applications of six people, including expelled Congress leader Kripa Alva, media coodinator to Union Minister H. D. Kumaraswamy, in connection with the alleged sting operation targeting former Chief Minister Siddaramaiah. Another suspect in the case Power TV owner and editor Rakesh Shetty has also filed a separate anticipatory bail plea that is still pending, sources said. The applications were filed by six people, including Kripa Alva, Prajwal Prasad, Chandan, Vinod Kumar, Prashanth, and one other person. The Bengaluru City Police had opposed the bail applications. The rejection of anticipatory bail pleas of the six accused in the case, may likely lead to their arrest and custodial interrogation, sources said. Bengaluru City Police had registered a case under the Information Technology Act, 2000 based on a complaint by Mr. Siddaramaiah of a video, allegedly being circulated to defame him. The probe into the contents of the video had led the police to the official residence of Union Minister H. D. Kumaraswamy. Former Bengaluru City Police Commissioner Seemant Kumar Singh had said that Ritesh Pandey who had uploaded the video online had got a mobile phone for the purpose at the Union Minister’s residence. Meanwhile, the city police had also questioned the woman in the video, reportedly making allegations of sexual abuse against the former chief minister and she has reportedly denied any abuse. She has reportedly claimed she made those statements under pressure. This has put Kripa Alva and Rakesh Shetty, allegedly in the video in a spot and are facing heat from the police. 3318e4b46085b06a.title: Gurugram court fines Burger King, Swiggy ₹72,000 over delivery of non-veg burgers instead of veg
3318e4b46085b06a.summary: Burger King India and food delivery platform Swiggy have been held liable by a consumer court for delivering non-vegetarian burgers instead of vegetarian ones, following which two children reportedly fell ill. The Gurugram District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission imposed a combined penalty of ₹ 72,000 on the two companies in connection with the 2021 incident. According to the complaint, Bhagwan Das Mangla, a resident of Sector 46 in Gurugram, had ordered four vegetarian burgers from Burger King through the Swiggy app on April 2, 2021, for his unwell wife. However, as she was not feeling well enough to eat, she left the package unopened. The burgers were subsequently opened and consumed by her children. According to Mangala, they found the taste strange and experienced nausea and vomiting. He said when he checked the package in the evening, he realised the food was non-vegetarian, which prompted him to raise a complaint with Swiggy. "This incident hurt the religious sentiments of my vegetarian family, leaving them under mental distress. When they raised an objection, a Burger King representative acknowledged the error and proposed an out-of-court settlement. The company offered to sponsor a pilgrimage to one or two destinations of the family's choice, in addition to providing compensation of ₹ 25,000. I rejected this proposal and filed a case in the consumer court, seeking compensation of ₹ 60,000," Mangla said. According to his counsel Megha Gupta, the matter was heard by a bench comprising Commission Chairperson Sanjeev Jindal and members Jyoti Siwach and Khushwinder Kaur. The Commission stated that the invoices, Swiggy app chat history, and complaint-related documents submitted by the complainant are sufficient to establish negligence on the part of the companies. He said when he checked the package in the evening, he realised the food was non-vegetarian, which prompted him to raise a complaint with Swiggy. "This incident hurt the religious sentiments of my vegetarian family, leaving them under mental distress. When they raised an objection, a Burger King representative acknowledged the error and proposed an out-of-court settlement. The company offered to sponsor a pilgrimage to one or two destinations of the family's choice, in addition to providing compensation of ₹ 25,000. I rejected this proposal and filed a case in the consumer court, seeking compensation of ₹ 60,000," Mangla said. According to his counsel Megha Gupta, the matter was heard by a bench comprising Commission Chairperson Sanjeev Jindal and members Jyoti Siwach and Khushwinder Kaur. The Commission stated that the invoices, Swiggy app chat history, and complaint-related documents submitted by the complainant are sufficient to establish negligence on the part of the companies. 2ab0bd08a06939ca.title: TNGCTA writes to CM, Higher Education Minister to appoint senior govt. college principal as DCE
2ab0bd08a06939ca.summary: Published - November 21, 2026 01:10 am IST - Chennai The Tamil Nadu Government College Teachers Association (TNGCTA) has submitted a petition to the Chief Minister, Higher Education Minister, and Higher Education Secretary requesting the appointment of a senior college principal as the Director of Collegiate Education. The Association urged the government to revert to the old practice that was prevalent before January 2024, when a the senior-most principal of a government college would occupy the post of Director of Collegiate Education (DCE). Putting forth its argument, the association stated that the responsibility of administering over a 1,000 government Arts and Science colleges, government colleges of education, government-aided colleges, and self-financing colleges in the State should be entrusted to a person with deep understanding of the inner workings of these institutions. S. Suresh, general secretary, TNGCTA, said in a statement that senior principals had extensive experience in administering several of these institutions, which had prompted the government to appoint them and run the department for about three decades. However, on January 30, 2024, the then DCE was placed under suspension on administrative grounds and an IAS officer was appointed to streamline the affairs at the Directorate. This appointment was to be for a period of one year but the government kept appointing IAS officers ever since. The petition was prompted by the fact that the current DCE has gone on long leave due to personal reasons and the Commissioner of Technical Education, another IAS officer, was given additional charge of DCE. While the Commissioner has to administer a large number of technical educational institutions, he is also the head of Vice-Chancellor Convenor Committees of at least two State-run universities. Saddled with all these responsibilities, the Commissioner would find it difficult to ensure smooth functioning of the Collegiate Education department, Mr. Suresh

4dfc64ac7349a59e.title: India's core sector growth hit 31-month high of 10.9% in October
4dfc64ac7349a59e.summary: Output of key infrastructure industries rose 10.9 per cent in October 2026, up from 0.8 per cent in the year-ago month, driven by strong performance in coal, iron ore, electricity and cement. According to the official data released by the Commerce and Industry Ministry on Friday, the core sector expanded by 8.2 per cent in September 2026. Among segments, iron ore output rose by 26.4 per cent, electricity by 21.6 per cent, coal by 23.1 per cent, and cement by 15.4 per cent. During April-October this fiscal, these nine segments expanded by 6 per cent against 2.3 per cent in the same period last year.

1ac5415d69379357.title: Forum explores perspectives on equity-oriented social progress and health systems
1ac5415d69379357.summary: Updated - November 21, 2026 01:07 am IST - CHENNAI Panellists discuss equity-oriented social development and health systems at the “Transdisciplinary Practice and Research Forum” in Alwarpet on Friday. | Photo Credit: VELANKANNI RAJ B. Bringing together researchers, practitioners, policymakers, and people with lived experiences, a ‘Transdisciplinary Practice and Research Forum’ provided a platform to discuss diverse perspectives and experiences in addressing equity-oriented social development and health systems. The Banyan Academy of Leadership in Mental Health (BALM), along with Athena Institute at Vrije Universiteit, Amsterdam, organised the forum as part of their collaborative work on transdisciplinary research and practice. It sought to explore how academic and societal knowledge could be integrated into equity-oriented social development and health systems and how to build a community of practice around it. A panel discussion on “Epistemic Justice and Politics of Knowledge” discussed the epistemic politics of knowledge production, what is rendered visible or authoritative, by whom, and against which criteria of validity. Namita Jacob of Chetana Trust spoke about their work on creating accessible books for children with disabilities. “We need to understand their way of knowing the world,” she said, adding that they also run a library that travels to places so that children can have access to books. The books, she said, were not based on their impairments, but the barriers they faced or their requirements. Kavitha Muralidharan, independent journalist, said, “We must create spaces for people to tell their stories, rather than assuming that we must speak for them.” Journalists, she said, need to be careful about the hierarchy they create. She also stressed the importance of oral history. Pradeep Narayanan of Praxis said research methodology tools must not imprison conversations.
