b94d9fe20128b287.title: Freshwater fish species discovered in Western Ghats
b94d9fe20128b287.summary: Published - November 21, 2026 12:17 am IST - KOCHI Researchers at Kerala University of Fisheries and Ocean Studies (Kufos) claimed to have discovered two new freshwater fish species from the Periyar-Cardamom Hills of the Western Ghats. Mesonoemacheilus mannanorum, one of the two species, has been named after the Mannan community and is found in streams deep inside the Periyar Tiger Reserve. The second species, Mesonoemacheilus sabariensis, is named after the Sabari hills and is found in streams near Angamoozhi in the Pamba river system, according to a communication. The discoveries were made by a team led by V.K. Anoop and Rajeev Raghavan from the Kufos and Neelesh Dahanukar from the Shiv Nadar Institution of Eminence, New Delhi. The research has been published in the Journal of Fish Biology , it said. e4b128486e1a1120.title: Woman delivers triplets after non-ART treatment at Telangana govt. hospital; premature babies discharged after NICU care
e4b128486e1a1120.summary: Updated - November 21, 2026 01:20 am IST - HYDERABAD The Gandhi Hospital team with the woman and her triplets. | Photo Credit: ARRANGEMENT After a nine-year wait and unsuccessful fertility treatment at private hospitals, a couple welcomed triplet boys following treatment at Gandhi Hospital’s IVF Centre. The premature babies, who weighed between 1.4 kg and 1.5 kg at birth, spent over a month in the hospital’s Neonatal Intensive Care Unit (NICU). They were discharged along with their 32-year-old mother after responding well to treatment. Avanthi enrolled at Gandhi Hospital’s IVF Centre in January this year. Doctors opted for ovulation induction, a non-assisted reproductive treatment, and she conceived in the second cycle. After scans revealed a triplet pregnancy and a short cervix, doctors performed a McDonald’s cervical cerclage at 14 weeks. However, her water broke prematurely at 32 weeks, prompting doctors to deliver the babies on October 7. The newborns were admitted to the NICU, where they received treatment and close monitoring for over a month before being discharged with their mother. Director of Medical Education Vanii appreciated the efforts of the team, including head of the Department of Gynaecology Shobha, IVF specialists Krishnaveni and Fathima Rafi, embryologist Shiva Krishna, lab technician Ashok and counsellor Kavitha. IVF specialist Dr Krishnaveni said that they opted ovulation induction as a first line of treatment, which is not a In Vitro Fertilization (IVF) method. “We conduct evaluations to know if non-IVF methods can be used as first line of treatment to avoid burden on couples who are already in distress,” she said. Currently, over 500 couples have rolled for treatments at the government hospitals IVF centre. d5544a7f2b36e4c0.title: Singareni keen to supply Naini coal to NTPC Kaniha plant after meeting TG needs
d5544a7f2b36e4c0.summary: Published - November 21, 2026 12:54 am IST - HYDERABAD Singareni CMD Buddhaprakash Jyoti (third from left) and two senior executives of SCCL with NTPC CMD Gurdeep Singh (second from left) in New Delhi on Friday. | Photo Credit: By Arrangement Singareni Collieries Company Ltd (SCCL) has agreed to supply coal from its Naini Block mines in Odisha to local industries and NTPC’s Kaniha (Talcher) Thermal Power Station in Angul district there after meeting the coal requirements of Telangana. Chairman and Managing Director of the SCCL Buddhaprakash Jyoti expressed the company’s readiness during a meeting with CMD of the National Thermal Power Corporation Ltd (NTPC) Gurdeep Singh in New Delhi on Friday. Executive Director (Coal Movement) B. Venkanna and General Manager (Coordination and Marketing) T. Srinivas of SCCL also attended the meeting. During the meeting, Dr. Jyothi briefed Mr. Singh on production at the Naini coal block. He stated that the coal requirements of Telangana are being given priority with a major share of Naini coal mined now being supplied to the TG-Genco’s Yadadri Thermal Power Station. The remaining coal is being supplied to local industries. He assured that SCCL was ready to supply coal to NTPC’s Kaniha plant in addition to its existing coal supply agreements with NTPC. Mr. Jyoti added that SCCL has been supplying coal to NTPC plants in Telangana, Maharashtra, Karnataka and other States for decades under the fuel supply agreements. After Telangana, NTPC plants receive the largest share of SCCL’s coal production. The SCCL CMD stated that the Naini coal block is expected to produce 10 million tonnes of coal annually from next year and the production is planned to continue for the next four decades. Accordingly, the SCCL is ready to supply coal to the nearby NTPC Kaniha plant under a long-term fuel supply agreement. 93c8d28d1658354a.title: One held in theft case; 40 grams gold recovered in Anakapalli
93c8d28d1658354a.summary: Published - November 21, 2026 12:25 am IST - ANAKAPALLI Anakapalli Town police on Friday cracked a house break-in case within 24 hours of the complaint and arrested a 23-year-old habitual offender, recovering the entire stolen gold jewellery weighing 40.590 grams from him. The accused was identified as K Rakesh, a catering worker and resident of Sarada Nagar Colony, Anakapalli. According to the police, the accused Rakesh gained entry into a locked house in Sarada Nagar Colony. The owners, after returning home on November 19, found that the gold was stolen and lodged a complaint. The police used technical evidence to identify the suspect and apprehended the accused. Entire stolen gold of 40.590 grams was recovered Police said Rakesh was a habitual offender and had been previously arrested in three theft cases at Anakapalli Town, S. Rayavaram and Munagapaka police stations. The accused was subsequently produced before the court. 2b427905a1ebf0dd.summary: The Supreme Court on Friday allowed the lighting of the Karthigai Deepam lamp atop Thiruparankundram hill on November 24 as a one-time measure. A bench of Justices Aravind Kumar and Vipul M Pancholi said only authorised persons from Devasthanam (temple administration) and government officials can go for lamp lighting and ordered authorities to deploy necessary security if required. The top court, however, stayed the Madras High Court judgment allowing the lighting of the traditional Karthigai Deepam lamp atop Thiruparankundram hill. The Tamil Nadu government had contended on Wednesday that allowing the lighting of the traditional Karthigai Deepam lamp atop the stone pillar near the dargah could lead to thousands of survey pillars across the country acquiring a religious character. The Karthigai Deepam controversy at the Arulmigu Subramaniaswamy temple in Madurai centres on a dispute over where and by whom the lamp should be lit on the Thiruparankundram hill. Along with the increase in prices of the devices, consumer expectations are also rising, and consumers are looking for meaningful specifications that can match the desired experience across processing speed of the mobile phones, camera, battery, durability, after-sales service, etc. "A few years ago, a Rs 1-lakh smartphone was a rarity in India. Today, as flagship prices keep rising, this price point is becoming increasingly common. bd1e48fa31b9c29e.title: Andhra govt to explore SMR nuclear plants as alternative to thermal power
bd1e48fa31b9c29e.summary: The Andhra Pradesh government on Friday approved tapping nuclear power employing Small Modular Reactor (SMR) technology, advanced nuclear reactors, as an alternative to thermal power, an official said. K Vijayanand, special chief secretary (Energy), said the southern state would explore setting up nuclear power plants using SMR technology at "retiring thermal power units or other suitable locations in the state after SMR technology is stabilised." "Government, after careful consideration of the request of the Managing Director, APGENCO (Andhra Pradesh Power Generation Corporation), hereby accord approval to explore establishment of a Nuclear Power Plant using SMR technology, as an alternative to thermal power," Vijayanand said in a Government Order (GO). The special chief secretary noted that the private sector will be allowed to participate in Andhra Pradesh's endeavour to set up SMR nuclear power plants.

71f45d913f0e75c2.title: NYC Fitness Buffs Bristle at City Plan to Close Outdoor Gym
71f45d913f0e75c2.summary: (Bloomberg) -- In New York’s neighborhood-level disputes over government projects, even pull-up bars have become a flashpoint. At Tompkins Square Park in Manhattan, the paint on a set of bars is chipping. But the fitness buffs who work out in the park daily are holding on to them for dear life. At issue are city proposals to close the outdoor gym for months and replace it with equipment that is more accessible to people with disabilities. Regulars argue the equipment is sufficiently accessible and that the city could reconstruct it with inferior materials. Some simply dread a monthslong separation from the bars that have become part of their daily lives. For Theophilus London, the stakes feel particularly personal. About three months ago, when he was struggling and looking to change his life, he found his way to the pull-up bars in Tompkins Square Park. “I was in a desperate need of a change of lifestyle,” London said on a recent afternoon, between sets at the East Village park. “This park changed my life.” London, a musician nominated for a Grammy Award with Kanye West in 2016, visits the pull-up bars daily. He is among many park-goers speaking against plans to close the decades-old fitness equipment for renovations. The park adds to a list of government projects that some New Yorkers have perceived as community interference. A few blocks southwest, in Nolita, residents protested the construction of an affordable housing project at Elizabeth Street Garden for more than a decade. Across the East River in Brooklyn, plans to build a skate park at Mount Prospect Park concerned neighborhood groups that said the facility would exacerbate the problem of higher temperatures in urban areas. “The idea that it’s an adult fitness area that needs reconstruction is totally and completely misguided,” said Salo Coslovsky, an urban planning professor at New York University, at a recent local advisory board meeting on the Tompkins Square Park pull-up bars. 800d656f16ed2f2d.title: No suburban service cancelled in morning peak hours due to new timetable: Railways
800d656f16ed2f2d.summary: Published - November 21, 2026 01:10 am IST - Chennai The Southern Railway has denied that there has been a reduction of suburban train services because of the new timetable that came into effect from November 1. In response to an article published in The Hindu, titled ‘Commuters from Pattabiram hit by reduced suburban services after revision of timetable’ on November 19, the Southern Railway has clarified that no suburban train services have been cancelled or withdrawn during the morning peak hours. Instead, the existing pattern of train operations has been strategically reorganised to improve overall operational efficiency, punctuality, and passenger convenience. With reference to the stoppage of the Pattabiram turnback service, which was extended to Tiruvallur, the Southern Railway says the turnback, introduced in 2004, involved a complex crossover movement, as the train had to cross over three lines to reach Pattabiram station, which is located on the line leading towards Pattabiram Military Siding. This crossover resulted in a speed restriction of 15 km per hour. The crossover movement consumed 10 to 12 minutes, causing the halting of trains on the three lines while approaching Pattabiram, leading to delays of mail and express trains as well. 224994778036cc8f.title: Cauvery dispute: SC dismisses Tamil Nadu's pleas for 11 TMC water release
224994778036cc8f.summary: The Supreme Court on Friday dismissed two pleas of the Tamil Nadu government seeking a direction to Karnataka for the release of 11 thousand million cubic (TMC) feet of Cauvery river water. A bench of Justices Vikram Nath and Aparesh Kumar Singh said that Tamil Nadu has filed a third application for bringing on record some additional documents, which will also be dismissed. In its pleas, the Tamil Nadu government sought directions to Karnataka to make sure that the backlog of 11 TMC of Cauvery water as on October 7 is cleared immediately and ensure the same at the rate of 1.3 TMC per day in 10 days at Billigundulu, a key water-measuring station on the banks of the river along the Karnataka-Tamil Nadu border. On October 12, the top court reserved its decision on the two applications of the Tamil Nadu government. The Karnataka government had told the top court that it would be difficult to meet Tamil Nadu's demand for the release of 11 TMC feet of Cauvery river water for making good

be6caf1bfca67d9e.title: India, Canada conclude sixth round of talks for proposed trade pact
be6caf1bfca67d9e.summary: India and Canada have concluded the sixth round of negotiations for a trade agreement, aimed at unlocking new opportunities in trade and investment, and diversifying supply chains, an official statement said on Saturday. The negotiations covered key areas, including trade in goods, trade in services, rules of origin, trade remedies, intellectual property and investment promotion, the commerce ministry said. Commerce Secretary Rajesh Agrawal held a meeting with Glenn Purves, Vice Minister of International Trade of Canada, and his delegation to review the progress of negotiations for the proposed Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA). The ten-day talks concluded on November 20. "Both sides reaffirmed their shared commitment to concluding an ambitious, balanced and commercially meaningful agreement that delivers tangible benefits to farmers, industries, businesses and Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) in both countries," it said.

1610f8d0b3d08f0a.title: AIPC Tamil Nadu to support MSMEs through professional network
1610f8d0b3d08f0a.summary: Published - November 22, 2026 01:12 am IST - CHENNAI The All India Professionals’ Congress (AIPC) Tamil Nadu chapter should function as a professional support network for micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs), helping them access legal, financial and technical expertise, said its national chairman Madhu Goud Yaskhi at the organisation’s annual summit in Chennai on Saturday. Mr. Yaskhi proposed that chartered accountants, lawyers, engineers and IT professionals associated with the AIPC volunteer their time to help MSMEs with taxation, regulatory compliance, financial management and delayed payments. He said over ₹7 lakh crore owed to small enterprises across India remained stuck in delayed payments, with large companies often taking more than 120 days to clear dues despite the statutory 45-day limit. The AIPC could also take up delayed payments by State public sector undertakings with the Tamil Nadu government, he said. Lawyers could help MSMEs pursue their dues through legal notices, while chartered accountants could assist with invoice discounting and compliance. Outgoing AIPC chairman and Rajya Sabha MP Praveen Chakravarty said Congress needed to reconnect with professionals in major urban centres, where it had lost electoral ground since 2014, he said. He also urged professionals to help implement and promote the Tamil Nadu government’s policies, including the Private University Bill, startup initiatives and tourism projects, saying the Congress’s participation in the coalition government brought responsibilities beyond its share in the Cabinet. After the event, Higher Education Minister P. Viswanathan told reporters that the Private University Bill passed by the Assembly had received the Governor’s assent. The government would prepare a standard operating procedure and issue guidelines for its implementation, he said. RAGHUNATHAN While early years after Independence in India saw excessive veneration of Gandhi, the recent trends have shifted to a “venomous detestation” of the man by the right-wing ecosystem led by the Sangh Parivar, historian Ramachandra Guha said here on Saturday while discussing his latest book Arguments with Gandhi. “When I was young, the ethos in India was excessive veneration of Gandhi. Now, it has become parricide,” he told the audience. “For the Sangh Parivar – it includes the BJP, the RSS, all BJP cabinet ministers – the demon is Gandhi. That should be very evident from whatever they say about Gandhi. Actually, Gandhi is their core ideological enemy, as he has once been of the Left.” Dr. Guha averred. Citing an analogy, he said that Prime Minister Modi, in his article on Gandhi in the New York Times on his 150th birth anniversary, “praised him for everything except Hindu-Muslim harmony”. Mr. Modi, he said, seem to think that he needs to praise Gandhi because he is a global figure, but the hardcore footsoldiers of the Sangh Parivar detest Gandhi venomously. He was in conversation with Tamil author and novelist B. Jeyamohan. Elaborating on the reasons for such attacks on Gandhi, Dr. Guha emphasised that Gandhi had come to represent the feminine in the eyes of the “macho Right”, what with his non-violent policy, inter-faith harmony, his scepticism of the State, or his scepticism of progress. “Gandhi raises almost all the important questions of human existence today. You can think of no other thinker; he catches so many vital aspects of our lives,” Dr. Guha observed, as the conversation veered towards his ideas of non-violent science which influenced several scientists, including J.B.S. f178aaed7009168f.title: T.N. may see solar energy installations slowing down, say energy generators
f178aaed7009168f.summary: Published - November 22, 2026 01:12 am IST - COIMBATORE Tamil Nadu, which has 10,000 MW-11,000 MW of installed solar energy capacity, may see a slowdown in solar energy installations in 2027, according to industry representatives. The single window system for obtaining approvals is not functioning effectively, finer details based on the recently-announced Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) Policy should be notified by the Tamil Nadu Electricity Regulatory Commission, and costs are escalating, say solar energy investors. “No approvals have been granted for solar energy projects for almost six months now. Only now has the government started accepting the applications. Even if they are approved now, it is difficult to commission the projects by March 2027. From April next year, it is mandatory for all new projects to have BESS, and this will push the costs up,” said one of the solar energy investors in Coimbatore. “We had a detailed discussion with the TNERC on the BESS policy. The policy says there will be waiver of wheeling charges. The wheeling charges are applicable only if a consumer buys under open access. However, the policy says solar energy generators who store energy can sell it only to the State utility. There are many such issues with the policy that need better clarity in the policy ,” says AD Thirumoorthy, State Level Renewable Energy Committee Member, Government of Tamil Nadu. The single window approval system is functioning effectively for solar energy projects that come as a part of foreign direct investments. The others require multiple approvals, starting right from the rural local body heads. These lead to delays, pushing up the costs, he added. While the BESS policy is a welcome move, the Tamil Nadu Green Energy Corporation should ensure that stored solar energy is evacuated within 24 hours, so that the generator can store freshly generated energy the next day, said L. cde4ace93eda6db5.title: PM Modi to launch development projects worth ₹34,470 cr in Bihar's Vaishali
cde4ace93eda6db5.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi will visit Bihar's Vaishali district on Saturday to launch projects worth nearly 34,470 crore, including a six-lane bridge over the Ganga river, and address a public meeting, officials said. This would be the Prime Minister's first visit to the eastern state since May, when he had attended a function marking the expansion of the cabinet headed by Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary, the first BJP leader to lead a government in Bihar. Elaborate security arrangements, including the suspension of vehicular movement on the national and state highways concerned for a stipulated period, have been made in Vaishali and Patna for the PM's visit, they said. The 9.76-km-long six-lane bridge, which connects Bidupur block in Vaishali to Kachchi Dargah on the outskirts of Patna, has been named 'Nitish Setu', in deference to the former Bihar chief minister, on whose watch the project was conceived and came close to completion. "The PM will visit 'Nitish Setu' in Vaishali.

939b04311350f6ba.title: Trump seeks 10% cap on credit card interest rates with Democrats' support
939b04311350f6ba.summary: President Donald Trump said Saturday that he would work with the incoming Democratic Congress to cap credit card interest rates, hoping to fulfill a promise he made on the 2024 campaign trail but couldn't deliver on because of industry pressure and a lack of interest from his fellow Republicans. "I would do it. These credit card companies have made a lot," Trump told Fox News Channel's "Saturday in America." Democrats and the Republican president have both backed capping credit card interest rates, with the standard proposal being capping rates at 10 per cent. It would substantially reduce what credit card companies can charge customers. The median credit card interest rate is roughly 22.2 per cent, according to an August survey by the New York Federal Reserve. Trump proposed capping credit card interest rates in January, as part of the White House's affordability push. abbdb2f04643f301.title: Raja Ravi Varma Gallery of Oleographs and Chromo Lithographs inaugurated in Chennai
abbdb2f04643f301.summary: Updated - November 22, 2026 01:12 am IST - CHENNAI Congress MP Shashi Tharoor inaugurating the Raja Ravi Varma Gallery of Oleographs and Chromo Lithographs at the C.P. Ramaswami Aiyar Foundation on Saturday. | Photo Credit: J. Johan Sathyadas Congress Member of Parliament Shashi Tharoor on Saturday inaugurated the Raja Ravi Varma Gallery of Oleographs and Chromo Lithographs at the C. P. Ramaswami Aiyar Foundation (CPRAF) to mark the institution’s 60th anniversary. He also released two books, Heritage, Education and Nature – 60 years of the C.P.Ramaswami Aiyar Foundation, and A catalogue of Ravi Varma’s Oleographs and Chomo Lithographs. Speaking during the launch, Mr. Tharoor, a long-time friend of the family, said as an MP for Thiruvananthapuram, he represented a city and a region whose history is closely connected with both Sir C.P. Ramaswamy Iyer and Raja Ravi Varma. To find their legacies brought together here in Chennai in an institution that has spent 60 years serving the wider public, is a particularly happy conjunction of history. He said the lithographs of Raja Ravi Varma, while becoming familiar objects across the country, also allowed the many who were barred from entering temples to worship the deities as well. One of the most significant reforms associated with Sir C.P.’s term as Dewan of Travancore was the temple entry proclamation, he added. He praised the work of the various schools run by the Foundation. including the Saraswathi Kendra in Chennai that was the city’s first school for children with autism, dyslexia and learning disabilities. Former Madras High Court judge P. N. Prakash, who received the first copies of the books, said that Sir C.P. had a magnetic personality, was a tennis player, and a polyglot who could speak several languages including, French and Latin; and he was the youngest Advocate General of Madras High court. f97096ca850df3be.title: Vasan urges political parties to fight for Cauvery water rights
f97096ca850df3be.summary: Published - November 22, 2026 01:14 am IST - CHENNAI Tamil Maanila Congress (Moopanar) president G.K. Vasan on Saturday urged the Cauvery Water Management Authority (CWMA) to direct the Karnataka government to release water due to Tamil Nadu. He also sought the cooperation of political parties in Tamil Nadu in securing the State’s rights by setting aside their differences. In a statement, Mr. Vasan expressed shock over the Supreme Court dismissing Tamil Nadu’s plea seeking the release of 11 thousand million cubic feet of Cauvery water by Karnataka. He said that, in the past, the Karnataka government had not complied with the directions of the CWMA and had acted in a step-motherly manner. Farmers in the Cauvery delta are under severe economic distress due to an acute shortage of water for irrigation. The Karnataka government should understand that the Cauvery water-sharing issue and the Mekedatu issue are not only river water disputes, but also the lifelines of the people of Tamil Nadu, Mr. Vasan added. 2635f0246638e795.title: Hero FinCorp aims to double loan disbursements over next two quarters
2635f0246638e795.summary: Hero FinCorp aims to double its loan disbursement volumes over the next two quarters, after disbursing over 4.80 lakh loans across northern India between January and September this year. Financial services company Hero FinCorp Ltd is a division of two-wheeler manufacturer Hero MotoCorp. The company's growth plans will be supported by its diversified lending portfolio, distribution network and artificial intelligence-led underwriting capabilities, according to a statement. The non-banking financial company caters to diverse financing needs through a comprehensive portfolio of retail, MSME and corporate lending solutions. "Over 4.8 lakh households and businesses across seven states have chosen us this year for a two-wheeler, a car, a personal loan, working capital or a loan against property. "We aim to double our growth in the region over the next two quarters while keeping the customer's trust at the centre of every decision we make," Hero FinCorp's spokesperson said.

27555e7734ca00ee.title: Karnataka seeks 50 more workdays under VB-G RAM G in view of drought

The Centre has fixed the guarantee at 125 days a year for each rural job card holder under the scheme. The state sought the extra days to help farmers and rural labourers affected by deficient rainfall, Khandre said. The Rural Development and Panchayat Raj minister was speaking after visiting a desilting work site at a check dam within the Adavi Somapur Gram Panchayat limits in Gadag taluk, where he interacted with workers. "Due to drought, rural people are forced to migrate in search of work. 4d91efeef6d93a25.title: PPFAS Mutual Fund has no plans to expand its 7-scheme portfolio for now, says Neil Parikh
4d91efeef6d93a25.summary: PPFAS Mutual Fund will continue operating with its current portfolio of seven schemes while not launching new ones. CEO Neil Parikh emphasized the fund's clearly defined product architecture aimed at different investment horizons. The company focuses on value investing by identifying mispriced securities and maintaining a disciplined long-term approach. Parikh highlighted the importance of patience and underlined potential short-term underperformance due to strict valuation criteria.

360933fb0939b9d4.summary: Work crews were boxing up the venue of this year's United Nations climate talks in Turkiye, as negotiators went into overtime on Saturday in an attempt to reach a final agreement to address global warming. But hopes are slim that additional discussions will result in concrete plans to drastically slash the use of fossil fuels. The added day of talks came as the two-week annual summit, called COP31, which was supposed to end Friday, drew strong condemnation from activists and some countries for failing to mention fossil fuels in a draft of the final agreement. The final document is meant to address how the world will deal with climate change, which is contributing to devastating heat waves, floods and other disasters. To avert the most catastrophic effects of warming, experts said the world needs to urgently and drastically cut emissions from the use of coal, oil and gas. f0fc613bfcb38260.summary: US-based Heller Industries Inc on Friday inaugurated its first Indian manufacturing facility near Ahmedabad, becoming the first global reflow oven maker to produce the critical semiconductor and electronics assembly equipment locally in the country. Operated through its subsidiary Heller Thermal Systems Private Limited (HTS) at Gallops Industrial Park in Rajoda, the 30,000 sq ft facility has been established with the strategic and operational support of long-term Indian partner NMTronics India Pvt Ltd, a company statement said. ed4e5a9832ad1c5e.title: Chennai International Book Fair 2027 to be held from January 16 to 18
ed4e5a9832ad1c5e.summary: Updated - November 22, 2026 01:08 am IST - CHENNAI Rajmohan, Minister of School Education, unveiling the logo of Chennai International Book Festival 2027 at Anna Centenary Library in Chennai on Saturday. | Photo Credit: B. VELANKANNI RAJ Minister for School Education Rajmohan on Saturday unveiled the logo of the Chennai International Book Fair (CIBF) 2027, which is scheduled to take place from January 16 to January 18, next year, at the Chennai Trade Centre. The Minister also inaugurated the training programme for global literary agents at the Anna Centenary Library in Chennai. The upcoming CIBF will be its fifth edition, with publishers, authors, and translators from more than 110 countries expected to participate. The Publishers and Booksellers Association of Thailand (PUBAT) will participate as a special guest. At the inaugural edition of the CIBF in 2023, publishers from 23 countries participated. The number of participating countries gradually rose from 40 in 2024 to 65 in 2025 and 102 in 2026. Across these editions, 415 translation grants were awarded to 183 authors for translating 258 books into 50 languages. The training programme for global literary agents, which began on November 21, will continue until December 5. Layola Mani, Chairman of the Tamil Nadu Textbook and Educational Services Corporation, and R.V. Shajeevana, Director of Public Libraries, were present at the event. 749104a1bab252f1.title: Diversion of sanctioned posts raises concerns over postal operations in Tamil Nadu
749104a1bab252f1.summary: Updated - November 22, 2026 01:12 am IST - CHENNAI The diversion of various sanctioned supervisory and operational posts from the Tamil Nadu Postal Circle to other States by the Postal Directorate has triggered concerns over its impact on the T.N. Circle’s administrative efficiency, service delivery and employment opportunities. The redistribution was carried out as part of the nationwide restructuring and rebalancing of administrative units across the Department of Posts. The Directorate had recently issued an order on the redistribution of the posts. The order has resulted in the transfer of nearly 180 posts across eight cadres from Tamil Nadu to other postal circles, including Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, Punjab, Assam, Andhra Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Jammu and Kashmir and the North-East. Sources in the department said the Tamil Nadu circle has lost only a few posts in the past decade. But this time, a large share of posts, including postal assistants, multi-tasking staff, inspectors and postmen, are being redeployed. The redistribution has come under scrutiny over the absence of an adequate assessment of the workload and establishment requirements of the Tamil Nadu Circle before the posts were diverted. Tamil Nadu postal circle handles a substantial volume of postal operations. For instance, it operates nearly 3.68 crore post office savings bank accounts across the State, which is highest number in the country, sources said. Similarly, Tamil Nadu postal circle stands second in the revenue generation with Rs.1,733 crore in 2025-26 after Maharashtra. The diversion of a large number of posts would adversely affect postal operations in about 10,000 post offices across TN, sources said. bfb228e20ab5f123.title: DMRC transplanted trees without Forest Department’s approval, official tells HC
bfb228e20ab5f123.summary: Published - November 22, 2026 04:42 am IST The Delhi Metro Rail Corporation (DMRC) transplanted trees removed during the construction of an underground metro line at Ajmal Khan Park without obtaining prior approval from the Delhi government’s Forest Department, the Delhi High Court was informed. The submission was made in a status report filed by the Deputy Conservator of Forests (West Division), Department of Forest and Wildlife, in response to a petition alleging that large-scale construction work was being carried out in the area, damaging fully grown trees. The petition, on which the court had earlier issued notices to the authorities, is scheduled to be heard next on November 23 by Justice Jasmeet Singh. The petitioner, advocate Arpit Bhargava, submitted that the DMRC was carrying out extensive construction work on vacant land belonging to the Delhi Development Authority on Desh Bandhu Gupta Road in Karol Bagh, behind his residence, where several large trees stand. He said substantial quantities of iron and steel rods and other construction material were being cut and processed using mechanical equipment as part of the construction work, generating smoke, dust, fumes and particulate matter. In its status report, the Forest Department said officials of the West Division conducted a joint inspection of the project site at Ajmal Khan Park on October 7, when tree transplantation work was under way. The construction is part of the Inderlok-Indraprastha Corridor of the Delhi Mass Rapid Transit System (MRTS) Project under Phase IV. According to the report, of the 534 trees at the site, 524 were to be transplanted and 10 felled. During an inspection, it was found that around 10-15 transplanted trees were showing signs of survival and new leaf growth, and remaining trees can survive in future as transplantation is under process, the report stated. “The transplantation site had not been approved by the Forest Department before the work began,” it added. bfb228e20ab5f123.headline_en: DMRC transplanted trees without Forest Department’s approval, official tells HC
bfb228e20ab5f123.raw_facts: Published - November 22, 2026 04:42 am IST The Delhi Metro Rail Corporation (DMRC) transplanted trees removed during the construction of an underground metro line at Ajmal Khan Park without obtaining prior approval from the Delhi government’s Forest Department, the Delhi High Court was informed. The submission was made in a status report filed by the Deputy Conservator of Forests (West Division), Department of Forest and Wildlife, in response to a petition alleging that large-scale construction work was being carried out in the area, damaging fully grown trees. The petition, on which the court had earlier issued notices to the authorities, is scheduled to be heard next on November 23 by Justice Jasmeet Singh. The petitioner, advocate Arpit Bhargava, submitted that the DMRC was carrying out extensive construction work on vacant land belonging to the Delhi Development Authority on Desh Bandhu Gupta Road in Karol Bagh, behind his residence, where several large trees stand. He said substantial quantities of iron and steel rods and other construction material were being cut and processed using mechanical equipment as part of the construction work, generating smoke, dust, fumes and particulate matter. In its status report, the Forest Department said officials of the West Division conducted a joint inspection of the project site at Ajmal Khan Park on October 7, when tree transplantation work was under way. The construction is part of the Inderlok-Indraprastha Corridor of the Delhi Mass Rapid Transit System (MRTS) Project under Phase IV. According to the report, of the 534 trees at the site, 524 were to be transplanted and 10 felled. During an inspection, it was found that around 10-15 transplanted trees were showing signs of survival and new leaf growth, and remaining trees can survive in future as transplantation is under process, the report stated. “The transplantation site had not been approved by the Forest Department before the work began,” it added. 5b4808b44ac4942b.title: MHA sanctions more Central forces for Tripura municipal elections
5b4808b44ac4942b.summary: Published - November 21, 2026 11:36 pm IST - Agartala The Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) has sanctioned an additional 25 companies of Central Armed Police Forces (CAPF) for deployment during the Urban Local Body (ULB) elections in Tripura slated for November 27. State Election Commissioner (SEC) Pradip Chakraborty said the MHA has informed the State government of its decision on Saturday. He added that with local availability of the CAPF, a total of 29 companies of the Central forces will be deployed on election duties. The deployment will remain in force even after the declaration of results on December 2. The Opposition CPI(M) and Congress have long been demanding adequate deployment of Central forces alleging that the ruling BJP is trying to turn the elections into a farce through gross irregularities and use of government machinery. They have accused the State police of failing to discharge duties neutrally. The SEC had announced a schedule to hold elections for 21 ULBs including Agartala Municipal Corporation (AMC). However, the Congress and CPI(M) said clamed their candidates were prevented from filing nomination papers for five civic bodies. The BJP secured victory in five ULBs unopposed and hence, the polls will technically occur in 16 areas instead of 21. With the election campaign picking up pace, Opposition parties have alleged that their supporters are facing obstacles and threats during the door-to-door campaign. The parties have also sought the attention of the authorities after spotting several masked youth taking part in an campaign procession of the BJP in Agartala on Saturday. They alleged the youth may have been brought in from outside the State. While Russia and the US lead the world by each possessing thousands of nuclear weapons, China is rapidly expanding its nuclear arsenal. b1169cb24f4db674.title: Man held in Tirupattur for killing two persons
b1169cb24f4db674.summary: Updated - November 22, 2026 12:36 am IST - TIRUPATTUR A special team led by Superintendent of Police Akshay Anil Wankhere inspecting the spot. | Photo Credit: SPECIAL ARRANGEMENT A 29-year-old man was arrested by Tirupattur Taluk police on Saturday for killing two persons on the outskirts of Tirupattur town a day ago over a reportedly extra marital relationship. Police identified the arrested person as V. Sanjay Gandhi, a resident of Tiruvannamalai. The victims are E. Ranjith Kumar, 30, a resident of Tiruvannamalai, and C. Malini, 45, a resident of Tirupattur. Initial inquiry revealed that Malini married Chiranjeevi and had two children. The family was living near Tirupattur town. Malini met her school friend Sanjay Gandhi at a function a few months ago and got in touch since then. Police said Malini got acquainted with Ranjith, a cab driver, when he visited her house to meet her husband for work. Sanjay got agitated over the relationship and warned Malini of dire consequences. Police said that on Friday, when Malini and Ranjith were returning to Tirupattur in a car, Sanjay noticed them. An argument broke between them. In a fit of rage, Sanjay killed them and fled the spot. Police said a few residents noticed the duo in a pool of blood and alerted police. A special team led by Superintendent of Police Akshay Anil Wankhere inspected the spot. CCTV cameras and mobile phones were tracked. Later, the police team nabbed Sanjay in the hideout in Tirupattur. A case was registered and further probe is under way. 22870d99b63f2f45.title: Residents demand halts for more long-distance trains at Melmaruvathur
22870d99b63f2f45.summary: Published - November 22, 2026 12:56 am IST - Chennai A CPI(M) leader noted that only a few express trains were stopping at the Melmaruvathur station as the Southern Railway had removed stoppages for several trains after the COVID-19 lockdown. (FILE PHOTO) | Photo Credit: D. GOPALAKRISHNAN The residents in several villages situated around Melmaruvathur have requested the Southern Railway to provide a stoppage for several mail and express trains, including Vande Bharat and Amrit Bharat trains, at the Melmaruvathur Railway Station. G. Purushothaman, secretary of the Communist Party of India (Marxist) in Seyyur taluk, has petitioned the Southern Railway to add stoppages for mail and express trains at Melmaruvathur. He said that only a few express trains were stopping at the station, as the Southern Railway had removed stoppages for Uzhavan Express, Kamban Express, and Silambu Express after the COVID-19 lockdown As Melmaruvathur was an important spiritual town, the place has also gained commercial importance. Residents of several villages, including Seyyur, Sithamur, Lathur, and Maduranthakam, also visit Chennai for studies, work, and trade. Similarly, those travelling to the southern districts for trade and education must go to Chengalpattu or Villupuram to catch long-distance trains. The residents want long distance trains to halt at Melmaruvathur as it has become a transport hub. A senior Southern Railway official said that since the provision of additional stoppages for mail and express trains at Melmaruvathur comes under the administrative purview of Zonal Headquarters, Southern Railway headquarters would have to take a decision. Regarding the extension of suburban trains beyond Chengalpattu, the railway officer said the tracks beyond Chengalpattu railway station has not been upgraded to the prescribed standards for operation of electrical multiple unit (EMU) train services. Hence the extension of EMU train services up to Melmaruvathur was operationally not feasible

"The court respectfully requests the assistance of receiving Indian courts in effecting service of process upon the defendants in this civil action pending before this court," read an order by Judge Katherine Polk Failla. 54678118d1e8a15e.title: EPF is becoming a retirement income plan. Is it a better one?
54678118d1e8a15e.summary: The Employees’ Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO) board in New Delhi on Thursday (November 19) approved a voluntary Systematic Withdrawal Plan (SWP) , the Labour Ministry said. Retirees can take savings in instalments, monthly, quarterly or half-yearly, instead of one lump sum. The ministry says the plan is meant to supplement pension benefits. It is voluntary and will first be open to members above 55 with over Rs 5 lakh saved. The board also eased withdrawal rules and approved in principle investing up to 3 per cent of fresh yearly inflows in alternative investment funds (AIFs), the ministry said. Table 1: What the EPFO board changed Vivek Iyer, partner and financial services risk advisory leader at Grant Thornton Bharat, says the plan addresses “a long-standing gap in India’s retirement system”. India has focused on saving for retirement, he says, but offered little help with turning those savings into income. The advisory firm’s illustration shows how it could work. A retiree at 58 with Rs 50 lakh takes Rs 40,000 a month. If the balance keeps earning 8.25 per cent, the money lasts about 24 years, to age 82. Unlike an annuity, Iyer says, the plan lets members “keep ownership and flexibility over their corpus”. If the member dies at 68, about Rs 39.6 lakh passes to the nominee, the illustration shows. Everything hinges on interest. The ministry says the remaining money will keep generating returns. Iyer says whether it keeps earning the EPF rate “is what makes the plan attractive”. Kunal Kabra, founder of Kustodian.Life, a provident fund recovery firm, says EPF interest stops three years after retirement under current rules. On Grant Thornton’s example, that would cut the 24 years to about 13, Business Standard’s calculation shows. “If the interest still stops, then this option doesn’t make any sense,” Kabra says. It is not yet clear whether the balance under the new plan escapes that rule. The ministry has not said how instalments will be taxed . It says a corres

6d2420f6b6418046.title: T.N. govt. gave no advance notice on Justice Kurian panel’s dissolution: member
6d2420f6b6418046.summary: Published - November 22, 2026 01:06 am IST - Chennai Retired IAS officer K. Ashok Vardhan Shetty, a member of the committee on Union-State relations, has stated that neither he nor the panel’s head, Justice Kurian Joseph, was informed prior to its dissolution. In a detailed interview with The Hindu 360 YouTube channel, Mr. Shetty revealed that the government had initially cleared the panel to continue its work. “I think it was on May 4 when a fellow member, M. Naganathan, resigned. Because of this, we were forced to seek clarity from the government on the continuation of the committee. I spoke to the Chief Secretary asking whether we should continue, and also requested him to consider not appointing a replacement for Dr. Naganathan if we were to carry on. About a week later, the then-Public Secretary, Reeta Harish Thakkar, called me and said, ‘Sir, the government has said you can continue,’ adding that no new member would be appointed. So, we continued. While all other committees constituted during the previous regime were contacted and asked to step down, nothing of that sort happened to us. Suddenly, one day, they dissolved it,” Mr. Shetty recounted. The mandate of the dissolved panel has now been handed over to the State Law Commission. Addressing the Government Order (G.O.) that cited the Kurian Committee’s status as a non-statutory body, Mr. Shetty pointed out that the Law Commission holds the exact same legal standing. “The Law Commission was created by a 1994 G.O., and ever since, it has been reconstituted through similar orders. So, the Law Commission is also an executive body — just like we were, and just like the Punchhi and Sarkaria Commissions,” he said. He also questioned the feasibility of the transfer, noting that the State Law Commission has never examined Union-State ties in its over three decades of existence. “In the last 32 years, the State Law Commission has never gone into this issue. 9191c68aeb3d42fe.title: Trump gives Vance, Rubio public audition as 2028 succession race heats up
9191c68aeb3d42fe.summary: Marco Rubio fidgeted and sighed. JD Vance smiled and furrowed his brow. For 90 minutes, the secretary of state and the vice president, both potential 2028 presidential contenders, stood nearly shoulder to shoulder in matching outfits, an arm's length from President Donald Trump as he spoke to reporters crowded into the White House press briefing room. It was the latest episode in the public audition on Friday that the president and former reality television star has appeared to delight in arranging for his potential successors as he nears his last two years in office. In the same room months earlier, Rubio and Vance each took a turn defending the president and selling his agenda while filling in as White House press secretary. The president has also been known to quiz his public and private audiences on their opinions of the two men. Vance and Rubio maintain that they're good friends and have both demurred about whether they'll seek the White House in the next presidential race. R

8d05a4e99835b13a.title: T.N. to set up Statewide online registry of voluntary donors with rare blood groups
8d05a4e99835b13a.summary: Published - November 22, 2026 01:13 am IST - CHENNAI To ensure timely availability of compatible blood for patients with rare blood groups during medical emergencies, the “Tamil Nadu Rare Blood Group Donor Registry” will be established under the Tamil Nadu State Blood Transfusion Council (TNSBTC). In an order issued recently, the State government permitted the Project Director of the TNSBTC to establish the registry. The TNSBTC will develop, maintain, and periodically update the Statewide online database of voluntary donors with rare blood groups. The order directed all licensed blood centres in Tamil Nadu to identify eligible rare blood group donors and facilitate their enrolment in the registry with due consent. The council is authorised to prescribe appropriate operational guidelines, standard procedures, and mechanisms for registration, verification, updating, utilisation and confidentiality of the registry. The Project Director had said that rare blood groups posed a significant challenge in managing patients requiring urgent blood transfusion. Timely identification and mobilisation of compatible blood donors are essential to ensure uninterrupted transfusion support in times of emergency, and it is for this that the registry had been proposed. At present, information regarding donors with rare blood groups is maintained at different blood centres and is not available through a unified State-level mechanism. This may result in delays in identifying and mobilising suitable donors during critical situations. In addition, the government also permitted the TNSBTC to establish “Blood Donor Clubs” in colleges having functional Red Ribbon Clubs (RRC) in the State. Currently, 2,379 RRCs function across the State. Each blood donor club will have a faculty coordinator and a student coordinator. 742391430617522f.title: 8th Pay Commission: Postal employees seek major changes in promotion rules, propose 1-4 years qualifying service
742391430617522f.summary: The Federation of National Postal Organisations (FNPO) has urged the 8th Central Pay Commission (CPC) to overhaul promotion rules for central government employees, proposing that the minimum qualifying service for promotions be fixed between one and four years, depending on the requirements of individual cadres. In a letter dated November 20 addressed to Justice Ranjana Prakash Desai, chairperson of the 8th Pay Commission, FNPO Secretary General Sivaji Vasireddy sought a comprehensive review of the existing promotion conditions specified in the Department of Personnel and Training (DoPT) office memorandum issued on September 20, 2022. The federation, which represents a significant section of Department of Posts employees, argued that the existing promotion framework has created prolonged career stagnation and affected the functioning of several postal offices. According to FNPO, the annexure to the DoPT memorandum prescribes widely varying qualifying service periods for promotions across different pay levels. Some promotions require employees to wait as long as 12 years. The transition from Level 6, 9 to Level 11 has the longest qualifying period of 12 years. Similarly, promotions from Level 4 to Level 6, Level 6 to Level 10 and Level 11 to Level 13 require 10 years of qualifying service. Other promotional transitions, including Level 2 to Level 4 and Level 6 to Level 9, require eight years. In contrast, several other promotions under the same framework have qualifying service requirements ranging from just one to three years, the federation pointed out. FNPO said the prolonged qualifying service requirements have adversely affected the Department of Posts, with several important positions remaining vacant for extended periods because fewer employees become eligible for promotion. The affected positions include Lower Selection Grade and Higher Selection Grade posts, supervisory positions in postal and Railway Mail Service (RMS) offices, Senior Superintendent of Post

b4d2355380c1f0e5.title: Guru Shiksha 2026 to be held in Chennai on November 27, 28
b4d2355380c1f0e5.summary: Published - November 22, 2026 01:07 am IST - Chennai The 11th edition of Guru Shiksha 2026, a State-level inter-school and inter-collegiate socio-cultural and educational programme, will be held at the Guru Nanak College and Guru Nanak Matriculation Higher Secondary School campus in Velachery on November 27 and 28, 2026. Organised by the Guru Nanak Educational Society and hosted by its Guru Nanak Centre for Consultancy and Outreach Initiatives, this year’s theme is ‘The Gurus’ Vision, A Woman’s Flight’, inspired by the vision of the Sikh Gurus. Oratorical events in English, Tamil and Hindi, poster-making, podcasts in English and Tamil, research papers in English, Tamil and Hindi, and letter-writing to Sikh Gurus in the three languages are some of the competitons. Students will be divided into five categories: Alpha (Classes I to V), Beta (Classes VI to VIII), Gamma (Classes IX to XII), Delta (college and university students and research scholars), and Epsilon (teaching and non-teaching staff and the general public, for specified competitions). The total prize limit exceeds ₹8 lakh. Online registrations are open, and spot registrations are available at the venue. acbc826c4119dbe5.title: State government examines new site for Hosur airport
acbc826c4119dbe5.summary: Published - November 22, 2026 12:50 am IST - CHENNAI The Tamil Nadu government is exploring a new site for the Hosur airport, after the site identified in Shoolagiri taluk in Krishnagiri district was rejected by the Ministry of Defence earlier this year. The new site is located near the Taneja Aerospace and Aviation Limited (TAAL) Aerodrome in Belagondapalli (about 15 km from central Hosur). Meanwhile, the Andhra Pradesh government has managed to get the site clearance for Kuppam airport project from the Ministry of Civil Aviation. This makes it even more difficult to obtain clearance for the initially identified site in Shoolagiri taluk (between Berigai and Bagalur), owing to airspace constraints. Earlier, the Tamil Nadu government had brought on board Bangalore International Airport Limited, which, over the past few weeks, had conducted a study on how to expand the site close to the TAAL airstrip and develop an airport for Hosur, sources said. The report was recently submitted to the government, based on which further discussions will be held on taking the project forward, and subsequently obtaining the site clearance. “First of all, the government had already tried twice to obtain approval for the Shoolagiri site from the Ministry of Defence, but it did not happen. The possibility for obtaining site clearance was very bleak, with Kuppam airport too vying for that airspace. As expected, Kuppam airport was granted site clearance. The Shoolagiri site was also facing stiff opposition to land acquisition from the residents. Keeping all this in mind, the site near TAAL is being considered now,” a source said. For the site near TAAL too, the State government must obtain approval from the Ministry of Defence, as the airspace is controlled by the Hindustan Aeronautics Limited. 4eca0410d663e864.title: USFDA flags 7 likely violations in check of NATCO Pharma's Hyderabad unit
4eca0410d663e864.summary: NATCO Pharma Limited on Saturday said it has received seven observations from the US health regulator following an inspection of its manufacturing facility in Kothur, Hyderabad. The US Food and Drug Administration (USFDA) conducted an inspection of the company's plant during November 12-20, NATCO Pharma said in a regulatory filing. Upon conclusion of the inspection, the company received seven observations in Form 483, it added. In USFDA parlance, a Form-483 is issued to a firm's management at the conclusion of an inspection when investigators observe conditions that, in their judgment, may constitute violations of the laws. "The company believes that the observations are procedural in nature and is confident of addressing these observations comprehensively within stipulated timelines," NATCO Pharma said.

7a1a7a181cda5ce7.title: Nikhil Gupta sentenced to over 19 years in US prison for plot to kill Khalistani separatist Pannun
7a1a7a181cda5ce7.summary: Indian national Nikhil Gupta has been sentenced to more than 19 years in prison after he admitted his role in a foiled 2023 plot to kill Khalistani separatist and US citizen Gurpatwant Singh Pannun in of New York. Gupta was sentenced to 235 months by US District Judge Victor Marrero at a hearing in Manhattan Friday. According to a statement issued from the US Department of Justice , 55-year-old Gupta, in February 2026, pleaded guilty to three criminal charges linked to a plan to kill Pannun . Justice Marrero called the plot to kill the US citizen inside the country "an attack on United States sovereignty", according to a Bloomberg report. Gupta was taken into custody in the Czech Republic in June 2023 and subsequently extradited to the US. The case forms part of what US prosecutors described as a wider conspiracy that strained relations between India and the US, as well as Canada. American authorities alleged that Gupta was associated with a network linked to the Indian government that sought to target Sikh separatists living overseas. The allegations also included the killing of Hardeep Singh Nijjar , who was shot dead by masked assailants outside a Sikh temple in western Canada in June 2023. According to prosecutors, Gupta recruited a person he believed to be a contract killer to carry out the assassination of Pannun. They alleged that he acted on instructions from Vikash Yadav, an official with India's external intelligence agency. Both Gupta and Yadav were charged with murder-for-hire, conspiracy to commit murder-for-hire and conspiracy to commit money laundering. Yadav remains outside US custody. "Today's prison sentence reflects the seriousness of Nikhil Gupta's conduct and should serve as a clear warning: the Department of Justice and its law enforcement partners will pursue and hold accountable anyone who attempts to commit violence on US soil or against US citizens," US Attorney Jamie McDonald said in a statement.
